And thus for this time we forbeare any further to enlardge, onelie wishinge you both for yo<sup>r</sup> owne pticuler to haue a reguard to the climate wherein you liue & soe to haue a care of yo<sup>r</sup> health, & to remember & admonish others that are w<sup>th</sup> you, to doe the like, & soe comend o<sup>r</sup> selues & all you and yo<sup>r</sup> busynes to the prouidence of God whoe guide you and yo<sup>r</sup> acc̃ons in his feare Amen.

> _[Margin: To or loueinge freind m<sup>r</sup> Tho: Morgan English marchaunt Resident att Bantam the 2 of December 1603.]_

<span class="sc">After</span> o<sup>r</sup> hartie Comendac̃ons. Yo<sup>rs</sup> of the 17<sup>th</sup> of ffebruarie 1602 We haue rec<sup>d</sup> o<sup>r</sup> shipps being all retourned thanke be to God saffe & their goode in good Condic̃on. The tyme heare by reason of agreat mortalitie & Contagion of the plaggue in diuers places of the Realme, & espetiallie in the Cittie of London hath beene verie vnsesonable for trade all marchaunte & others of any accompt haueing depted the Cittie all the sommer in w<sup>ch</sup> tyme there died betweene [p. 41] the 17<sup>th</sup> of December 1602 & the 10<sup>th</sup> of December 1603[^sec-04-fn-046] to the number of 38138 psoñs w<sup>th</sup>in the Cittie liberties and subvrbs thereof, But god be thanked the Contagion is very well seased, & there dieth not now of all diseases aboue 200 a weeke whereas there died in one weeke this sommer to the number of 3385 psoñs & neare the nomber of 3000 dyvers weekes togither. Beside this visitac̃on [God] tooke away vpon the 24<sup>th</sup> of March last o<sup>r</sup> late Queene yet did he not leaue vs w<sup>th</sup>out a souereigne for even the same daie was proclamed o<sup>r</sup> kinge Iames the first before kinge of Scotte whose proclamac̃on had noe one mouth that gaine said him, an entraunce and succession admired by all the kingdomes aboute vs, god blesse him & giue him a prosperous reigne ou<sup>r</sup> vs. The state of o<sup>r</sup> trade being by Godes prouidence thus prosperouslie begunn, & we purposeing by Godē grace to retourne o<sup>r</sup> 4 shipps back agayne for the fetching home of the rest of o<sup>r</sup> goodē & to Continue furder trade into the ptē of the East Indies according to the ffactory begunn by o<sup>r</sup> Generall S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster we haue thought yt meete to giue you to vnderstand that o<sup>r</sup> shipps shall godwillinge be redie to departe hence att the furdest w<sup>th</sup>in theis 2 monnethes, & therefore we pray [you] according to the direcc̃on and remembraunce left w<sup>th</sup> you by the said S<sup>r</sup> Iames & now renued by him in his lres sent by this Conveyaunce, to prepare & make redie the goodē appointed for their retourne, that the shipps be not occasioned to stay longe vpon their ladeinge. And for such goodē as are prouided as pepp̃ of the smoothest & lardgest sorte Cloues & Nutmeggē we pray you to haue acare to clense them & free them as much as ys possible from dust & the nutmeggē from Rumps that the Comodities w<sup>ch</sup> shall be retourned be cleane, w<sup>ch</sup> doth much Comend the sale of them, & besidē yt doth free o<sup>r</sup> shipps of an vnproffitable burthen w<sup>ch</sup> would fill vpp the bulke that might bestowe in place there of Comoditie of value. You may conceiue our desier w<sup>ch</sup> is y<sup>t</sup> o<sup>r</sup> goodē be laid abourde cleane & in good Condic̃on wherein we referr o<sup>r</sup> selues to yo<sup>r</sup> care thereof. And for yo<sup>r</sup> moc̃on touching yo<sup>r</sup> entertaynem<sup>te</sup> and Continuance in o<sup>r</sup> ymploym<sup>t</sup> we would willinglie haue aunsweare[d] yo<sup>r</sup> desier by theis o<sup>r</sup> lres, but m<sup>r</sup> Kenton being by reason of the sicknes not [p. 42] yett retourned or setled in the Cittie we could not haue tyme to Conferr w<sup>th</sup> him therein, but must referr you vntill the comeing of o<sup>r</sup> shipps by w<sup>ch</sup> we will advise what hath passed in o<sup>r</sup> Conference in that matter And being desierous to giue you all good Contentm<sup>t</sup>, doe purpose to send you such provysion of Oile & wyne for yo<sup>r</sup> health & Comforte as you haue writt for. Praying you to be carefull of yo<sup>r</sup> selfe and to haue a reguard to the Quesines of that Clymate & aire. And soe wishing you all good successe in yo<sup>r</sup> busynes we Comitt you to God.

> _[Margin: A lre from the Lo: Threr the last of Nouember 1603.]_

<span class="sc">After</span>[^sec-04-fn-047] o<sup>r</sup> hartie Comendaqons whereas there hath beene alredie proponed by me the L: Thr̄er in the behalfe of the kinge ma<sup>tie</sup> to you the Gou<sup>no</sup>r & Company of Aduenturers trading [into] the East Indies theis three thinge Ensuynge, first that although his ma<sup>tie</sup> by vertue of his princelie p<sup>r</sup>rogatiue maye lawfullie restraine the sale of yo<sup>r</sup> pepp latelie brought frome the East Indies vntill his owne Bulke & Masse of pepp now remaineing att Leaden Hall be first sold and vented, as by his ma<sup>ties</sup> learned Councell his highnes hath beene fullie resolved yet neu<sup>r</sup>thelesse such is his ma<sup>ties</sup> gratious favo<sup>r</sup> & inclinaqon towardes you, haueing respect to yo<sup>r</sup> soe worthie Adventure made & greate Chardges susteyned in this last longe voyadge by you sett forth, soe much for the Hono<sup>r</sup> of his ma<sup>tie</sup> & the publique good of the Realme as he is pleased to forbeare the vsinge of his p<sup>r</sup>rogatiue for this tyme, & to omitt his owne proffitt to giue meanes of benefitt vnto you. Secondlie that there should be a ioynt sale of his ma<sup>ties</sup> pepp and a like quantitie of yo<sup>rs</sup>, & soe to be vttered & sold together equallie & not otherwyse. Thirdlie yf you should thereof mislike then you to buy his ma<sup>ties</sup> pepp at some reasonable rate to be agreed vpon. Now for as much as we vnderstand that like as you doe humblie and thankfullie acknowledge his ma<sup>ties</sup> greate favo<sup>r</sup> towarde you, in not pressing his said prerogatiue [p. 43] vpon you. Soe you haueing considered of the two other offers, you doe w<sup>th</sup> all humblenes and thankefullnes embrace the second, namelie to conioyne in sale w<sup>th</sup> his highnes being not able as you pretend to proceede w<sup>th</sup> the latter, w<sup>ch</sup> is to buy the whole, Theis are therefore to signifie vnto you that his Ma<sup>tie</sup> being informed of theis thingę, is well pleased to allow of yo<sup>r</sup> said choise namelie of a Ioynct sale aswell of his ma<sup>ties</sup> pepp as of yo<sup>rs</sup> in a p̄portionable quatitie together. And for the better accomplishing of the same aswell for the kingę benefitt as yo<sup>r</sup> owne behoofe, wee haue thought good to recomend the whole ordering and manageinge of this busines to yo<sup>r</sup> good diligences, Cares, & discrec̃ons praying and requiring you to assemble yo<sup>r</sup> selues together, & to Consider of some such Course for the Carriadge of the same as may produce good effect of some spedie & reasonable benefitt vnto both, ffor the ffurtheraunce of w<sup>ch</sup> wee thinke y<sup>t</sup> requisite first that there be an Inhibition gen<sup>r</sup>all that noe pepp should be brought into this kingdome, by either English or Straunger vntill the said pepp proportionablie agreed vpon as is aforesaid to be sold be first vented, Secondlie y<sup>t</sup> all such pepp as is alredie brought in either by Straungers or English out of the lowe Countries or from the straightę should be sequestred lykewyse from sale. Thirdlie that a present Survey be made of all such pepp as you the Adventurers haue alreadie deliu<sup>r</sup>ed or shall deliu<sup>r</sup> vpon the diuident to p̄ticular Adventures of yo<sup>r</sup> Company w<sup>th</sup> spetiall chardge that noe p̄te thereof be sold vntill his ma<sup>ties</sup> p̄te And yo<sup>rs</sup> p̄portionablie be first vttered. Prouided alwayes that yt may be lawfull for any to transport pepp out of this Realme at their pleasure. And yt seemeth alsoe most iust & reasonable that strict order be taken w<sup>th</sup> the Grocers that they buye noe pepp but his ma<sup>ties</sup> and yo<sup>rs</sup> the same being whollsome & saleable pepp & to that end that a present surveie be made of such store & quantitie as the said grocers now haue vpon their handę. Theis pointę we haue thought ffitt to remember vnto you & that we maye w<sup>th</sup>all speede be adu<sup>r</sup>tised from you aswell of yo<sup>r</sup> opinion in theis thingę as of such other matters whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> as you shall thinke requisite to be further added and deuised for the better accomplishinge of this service, whereof soe soone as we shall haue significac̃on we shall p<sup>r</sup>sentlie giue order for the speedie expedic̃on thereof as [p. 44] appteyneth  Soe we bid you hartelie farewell from the Courte att Wilton the the last of Nouemb̃. 1603.

Yoʳ verie loueing freinde

Suffolke           Buckhurst      E Worcester Cumb̃land        Devonshire     W: Knollys HHoward          Ro: Cecill     E Wotton Stanhope         I ffortescue   I Popham

> _[Margin: The Companies aunsweare to th: llˢ lre.]_

RIGHT hon: oʳ duties most humblie remembred: we haue accordinge to yoʳ Loˢ: Commission to vs directed mett and Conferred together of some course to be taken touching the sale of his maᵗⁱᵉˢ pepp & haue examined the meanes ppounded by yoʳ LL: [(]being pleased to forbeare to put in vre his maᵗⁱᵉˢ pʳrogatiue) how the said meanes will sorte wᵗʰ the sale of his maᵗⁱᵉˢ pepp & vpholdinge of the Companie.  Wᶜʰ we finde must eyther stand or fall by such a moderac̃on as is to be carried herein, and fallinge into Considerac̃on of the first offer of favoʳ to the said Companie mencioned in yoʳ lᵖˢ Lres wᶜʰ was that a ioynct sale of his maᵗⁱᵉˢ pepp wᵗʰ a like quantitie of the Companies pepp should be vttered and sold to gether equallie & not otherwyse.  Wee finde in the Examinãcõn of that Course theis pticuler ympedimᵗᵉ followinge first agreate quantitie of the Companies pepp alredy disposed into many hande by a genʳal diuident agreed vpon amongst them selues before yoʳ ll: łres came to oʳ hande, beside other great quantities of pepp brought out of the lowe Countries and both of them soe passed from hand to hand from the mʳchaunt to the Grocer & from the Grocer to the Chapman in the Countrey that by this meanes there is sufficient pepp alreadie deliuʳed out abroade in the Cittie and Countrie, to forbeare any further sale for one yeare att the least, soe as the vent of his maᵗⁱᵉˢ pepp by a ioynt retayling sale wᵗʰ the remaynder of the Companies pepp cann noe way advaunce any some of money in Convenient tyme to his maᵗⁱᵉˢ vse, worthie the attending the Event of this course.  Wᶜʰ being soe then their resteth onelie the other meane wᶜʰ is the sale of the kinge pepp to the Companie, [p. 45] wherein we they Comitties on the said Companies behalfe doe humblie informe yo<sup>r</sup> ℔ that the said Companie haue vpon their hande alredie soe greate a masse of pepp, that allbeyt eu<sup>r</sup>y Adventurer thereof hath free libtie for the bringing in of 100<sup>li</sup> of money to take out vC<sup>li</sup> worth of pepper vpon his stocke to set forth a new voyadge to the East Indies to fetch home the remaynder of their goode there yet in reguard there is noe present sale thereof there is such drawing backe in pformeinge of this supplie that the voyadg hath not that expedi<span class="sc">c</span>õn w<sup>ch</sup> weare Convenient. Wherevpon we thinke that soe many pticuler men of soe diuers condi<span class="sc">c</span>õn will hardlie be drawen to ingage them selues for their seu<sup>r</sup>all propor<span class="sc">c</span>õns of their adventures to inlardg anie furder somes to buie a Comoditie that is like to lie soe longe vpon their hande. Vpon the Considera<span class="sc">c</span>õn of w<sup>ch</sup> difficultie, and the vnlikeliehood that the Generallitie of the Companie will be drawen to enterteyne this bargaine, we thought yt not meete to call the Companie together to propound this mo<span class="sc">c</span>õn vnto them, least yt should not onelie receiue a deniall, but being a matter putt into soe many distasted humo<sup>rs</sup> would be hardlie receiued and spoken off. We therefore seing noe present course to be followed that would bringe forth either benefitt to his ma<sup>tie</sup> or the Ccmpany, though[t] ffitt to shewe to yo<sup>r</sup> hono<sup>rs</sup> vpon what ympedim<sup>te</sup> we rest, desyreing to be furder directed herein. And we the Comitties for the Company doe humblie adu<sup>r</sup>tise yo<sup>r</sup> ℔ that yf the prepara<span class="sc">c</span>õn of the voyadge be any way crossed by vrging the gen<sup>r</sup>alitie w<sup>th</sup> further supplies of chardge, or hindring them in the vtteringe of their pepp diuided & to be devided amongst them before the deptinge of the ffleete w<sup>ch</sup> will be aboute the end of ffebruarie, the voyadge will whollie be ou<sup>r</sup>throwne w<sup>ch</sup> may by yo<sup>r</sup> Lo<sup>ps</sup> ffavo<sup>r</sup> be vphoulded both to the benefitt of the kinge and the good of the Comon wealth by this small tollera<span class="sc">c</span>õn & the shipps being once sent away the Company will be redie in all dutie to submitt them selues to any Course that shall seeme beneficiall to his ma<sup>tie</sup> for the venting of his pepp. And thus humblie resting at yo<sup>r</sup> ll Comaundem<sup>t</sup> & service we take our leaue London the 8<sup>th</sup> of Decemb̃ 1603.

Yo<sup>r</sup> Lo<sup>ps</sup> humble att Comaund

W<sup>m</sup> Rider

Thomas Smyth gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> [p. 46] Tho: Middleton		W<sup>m</sup> Romeny[^sec-04-fn-048] Samu: Saltonested	Tho: Bramley dep: Jo: Wolstonholme[^sec-04-fn-049]	Tho: Cordall.

> _[Margin: A lre from his matie to the kinge of Bantam in the East Indies by S<sup>r</sup> Henrie Middleton.[^sec-04-fn-050]]_

JAMES by the grace of God kinge of England Scotland ffraunce and Ireland defendo<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c: To the greate and mightie kinge of Bantam, & of the dominions & territories adioyning greetinge. Whereas the right of inheritaunce & possession of theis o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes of England ffraunce & Ireland by the decease of o<sup>r</sup> late deare Sister of ffamous memory is discended vpon vs, & ioyned to o<sup>r</sup> other principalities & kingdomes w<sup>ch</sup> we form<sup>r</sup>lie enioyed, we being established & setled in the possession thereof haue received into [p. 47] o<sup>r</sup> hande vpon the retourne of S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster & other of o<sup>r</sup> subiecte from yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>ties</sup> kingdomes & territories w<sup>th</sup> their shipps & marchandize, not onelie yo<sup>r</sup> Princelie łres directed and sent to o<sup>r</sup> said deceased Sister, but alsoe yo<sup>r</sup> kinde present w<sup>ch</sup> did accompanie the same holding o<sup>r</sup> selfe after her deaceased inter-ressed therein by the right of o<sup>r</sup> Crowne & Septer. Vpon the pvsall of w<sup>ch</sup> łres we weare possessed w<sup>th</sup> noe small ioye, that yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> had soe gratiouslie accepted the Comeing of o<sup>r</sup> subiecte into yo<sup>r</sup> dominions and kingdomes & soe fauorablie and Royallie delt w<sup>th</sup> them whilest they aboade & Contynued theare in traffique w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>r</sup> subiecte : Of all w<sup>ch</sup> ffavors & other yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>ties</sup> princelie pceedinge w<sup>th</sup> them o<sup>r</sup> said subiecte, S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster hath made vnto vs verie lardge & ample relac̃on. This Introducc̃on being made into a mutuall amitie & entercourse betweene yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> & vs, we are desirous to Nourrish & Contynue the same by all good meanes and oportunities that may be thought vpon or conceiued on o<sup>r</sup> pte. And to that end we haue geven lycence to diu<sup>r</sup>s of o<sup>r</sup> subiecte to prepare & sett forth a new voyadge towarde yo<sup>r</sup> Countries and kingdomes, amongest w<sup>ch</sup> manie of them w<sup>ch</sup> were in the former voyadge are desirous for the good & honorable vsadge they formerlie founde by yo<sup>r</sup> princelie favo<sup>r</sup> to visitt the same againe : others vpon their reporte are encouradged, notw<sup>th</sup>standing the longe & daungerous Nauigac̃on to see the state & manner of behavio<sup>r</sup> of people in Countries farr remote. Theis Considerac̃ons moueing both vs & o<sup>r</sup> Subiecte to visitt yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>ties</sup> Countries with lawfull & peaceable traffique of m<sup>r</sup>chandize, we doubt not but your ma<sup>tie</sup> will be well pleased therew<sup>th</sup>, & not onelie soe, but w<sup>th</sup> the Continuanc[e] of an entercourse from yeare to yeare of o<sup>r</sup> m<sup>r</sup>chaunte w<sup>th</sup> their shipps & goode into yo<sup>r</sup> kingdomes ; whome we dare be bold to Com̃end to [p. 48] yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> for a people Civill and iust in their dealeing and trade & euery way as able to furnish yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> & yo<sup>r</sup> people w<sup>th</sup> all such C omodities w<sup>ch</sup> this parte of the world doth yeald, or affordeth as any Nac̃õn or people whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> heretofore haue made trade or traffique w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>r</sup> people. And because a Capitulac̃õn & establishing of Amitie, [and] entercourse to be contynued betweene yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> and vs cannot convenientlie be p̄formed by discourse of łres o<sup>r</sup> seu<sup>r</sup>all kingdomes being so farr distant & remote thone from the other. We therefore pray yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> to giue eare therein to this bearer & to giue him Creditt in whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> he shall vndertake or promyse in o<sup>r</sup> name concerninge the same w<sup>ch</sup> we promyse for o<sup>r</sup> p̄te in the worde of a prince shall be p̄formed, and will be redie gratefullie to requite any loue kindnes or favo<sup>r</sup> that o<sup>r</sup> said Subiectę shall receiue at yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>ties</sup> handę. And in token of o<sup>r</sup> Princelie loue to yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup>, we send you by this bearer a remembraunce & kindnes, w<sup>ch</sup> we pray you to accept as from one that wisheth vnto yo<sup>u</sup> all good successe, & happines. And soe Comend yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> to the tuic̃õn of the most highe God.

Note that the kinge writeth him not brother. And that another łre was now alsoe written from the kinge to some other Prince in those p̄tę of The teno<sup>r</sup> of that form<sup>r</sup>lie from Queene Elizabeth.[^sec-04-fn-051]

> _[Margin: A Comission from his matie to Sr Henry Middleton]_

<span class="sc">Iames</span> by the grace of God kinge of England Scotland ffraunce and Ireland defendo<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c : Trustie and welbeloued Henrie Middleton Esquier & to o<sup>r</sup> trustie and welbeloued xpofer Colthurst[^sec-04-fn-052] Gentleman greetinge. Wheareas diuers of o<sup>r</sup> loueing subiectę att their owne Adventures Costes and chardges aswell for the hono<sup>r</sup> of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England as for the encrease and advauncem<sup>t</sup> of trade & m<sup>r</sup>chandize [p. 49] w<sup>th</sup>in the same did heeretoforℯ sett forth a voyadge to the East Indies w<sup>th</sup> c<sup>r</sup>teyne shipps and Pynnacℯ by way of marchandizeinge, by w<sup>ch</sup> shipps & Pynnacℯ they haueing discou<sup>r</sup>ed and begun to settle a trade in some pte of the said East Indies. And their shipps being retourned from thence laden w<sup>th</sup> sundrie marchandize brought from those partes they the said m<sup>r</sup>chauntℯ intendinge to frequent those Countries of the East Indies by Continuing the trade alredie discou<sup>r</sup>ed and begon & endevo<sup>r</sup>inge further discou<sup>r</sup>y of trade of those partℯ for the more ample vent of the Natiue Comodities of o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes, & retourninge from the places of their discou<sup>r</sup>y of such necessarie Comodities as shall be of spetiall vse & benefitt both to vs & o<sup>r</sup> subiectℯ are in hand to prepare and make redie their said shipps latelie retourned from the East Indies & and to sett them forth againe for a new voyadge. And wheareas the said m<sup>r</sup>chauntℯ haue chosen you the said Henrie Middleton to be principall Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup>, or Generall, and you the said x̄pofer Colthurst to be Leiuetenaunte Generall of all the m<sup>r</sup>chauntℯ Marriners and other o<sup>r</sup> subiectℯ w<sup>ch</sup> are or shall be shipped in any of the said shipps. We gratiouslie favo<sup>r</sup>ing their intended voyadge, & approueing & allowinge of their choyse of you to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>te</sup> being desierous to furnish you, w<sup>th</sup> all ffitt & Convenient power & aucthoritie to rule & Gou<sup>r</sup>ne all & eu<sup>r</sup>y o<sup>r</sup> subiectℯ imployed in this voyadge by a due obedience to be by them yealded, vnto you in obserueing & executeinge of all such good orders & Constitucõns as you shall thinke Convenient to ordeine & appointe for the ffurtheraunce of the said voyadge to the hono<sup>r</sup> of vs and o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes, & for the advauncem<sup>t</sup> of the said trade. We doe heereby straightlie chardge and Comaund all & eu<sup>r</sup>y pson & psons ymployed vsed or shipped in this voyadge, in any of the said ships, to giue all due obedience & respect vnto you dureing the said voyadge, & to beare them selues therein one towardes another in all good order & quietnes for avoideing any occasion that might breede Mutinie, quarrells or discention amongest them to the hindraunce of the good suckcess w<sup>ch</sup> is to be hoped for by Godℯ prouidence of the said intended voyadge, & in default of such dutie and obedience to be pformed towardes you & for the correccõn & quenching of all such Mutenie quarrells or dissention, that shall or maye growe or be moued by the [p. 50] disorder, euill dispoticõn or pversnes of any of the said psons. We doe heereby aucthorize you Henrie Middleton Gen<sup>r</sup>all dureing the said voyadge or dureing soe longe tyme as you shall liue in the said voyadge. And in Case of yo<sup>r</sup> decease w<sup>ch</sup> God forbid, we doe then likewyse hereby aucthorize you the said Christopher Colthurst to chastice correct and ponnish all Offenders and Transgresso<sup>rs</sup> in that behalfe according to the qualitie of their Offences w<sup>th</sup> such ponishm<sup>t</sup> as are Comonlie vsed in all Armyes by Sea when the offences are not capitall. And for Capitall Offences as wilfull murder w<sup>ch</sup> is hatefull in the sight of God, or mutenie w<sup>ch</sup> is an offence that maie tend to the ou<sup>r</sup>throue of the said voyadge, the same being trulie & iustlie proued agaynst any of the pson or psons aforesaid. We doe hereby giue vnto you the said Henrie Middleton during all the tyme of the said voyadge, or dureing soe long tyme as you shall liue in the said voyadge. And in Case of yo<sup>r</sup> decease we doe giue to you Christopher Colthurst full power and aucthoritie to vse and putt in execution o<sup>r</sup> lawe called Martiall in that behalfe and theis o<sup>r</sup> lres shall be vnto you sufficient warrante and dischargde for the doing & executeinge of all & singuler the p<sup>r</sup>misses. And forasmuch as at this present tyme wee are in Amitie w<sup>th</sup> all xptian People & are vnwilling that any of o<sup>r</sup> subiecte should giue occasion of breach or hindraunce of that league or Amitie w<sup>ch</sup> we hold w<sup>th</sup> any o<sup>r</sup> Confederate ffreinde or Allies and because we are not ignorant of the Emulačõn and Envie that doth accompany the discou<sup>r</sup>y of Countries and trades, & of the quarrells and contenčõns w<sup>ch</sup> doe many tymes fall out betweene the subiecte of diu<sup>r</sup>s Princes y<sup>t</sup> meete the one w<sup>th</sup> the other in fforraine and ffarr remote Countries, in the Course & psecuteinge of their discou<sup>r</sup>ies, and being desirous y<sup>t</sup> o<sup>r</sup> subiecte should forbeare to moue or begin any quarrell or contenčõn vpon the subiecte of o<sup>r</sup> Confederate ffreinde or Allies either in the pceedinge or retourne vpon or from any of their voyage. Wee therefore doe hereby straightlie chardge & Comaund you Henrie Middleton & you xptofor Colthurst, & all others vnder yo<sup>r</sup> Gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup>, that neither in your voyadg outwarde or homeward nor in any Countrie Iland Porte or place where you shall abide or come during the tyme of yo<sup>r</sup> being abroade out of o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes or dominions where you [p. 51] may meete w<sup>th</sup> any the subiecte of the kinge of Spaine or of any other of o<sup>r</sup> Confederate ffreinde or Allies, their shipps vessells goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandize, you doe attempt or goe aboute to sett vpon take or surprise their psons shipps vessells goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandize or offer any iniurie or discourtesie vnto them, vnlesse you shall first by them thearevnto iustlie be pvoked or driuen in the iust defence of yo<sup>r</sup> owne psons, yo<sup>r</sup> shipps vessells goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes as you will Aunswere to the Contrarie at yo<sup>r</sup> vttermost pills. In witnes whereof we haue caused theis o<sup>r</sup> łres to be made Pattente witnes o<sup>r</sup>selfe att Westminster the 3 daie of March in the first yeare of o<sup>r</sup> Reigne of England ffraunce & Ireland & of Scotland the Seauen & Thirteth.

<span class="sc">A Comission</span> sett downe by vs the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> the Deputie & Comitties of the East India Companie to o<sup>r</sup> loueing ffreinde m<sup>r</sup> Henrie Middleton Generall of the m<sup>r</sup>chaunte marrino<sup>rs</sup> & others ymployed by vs in this present intended voyadge, being o<sup>r</sup> second voyadge to the East Indies & to m<sup>r</sup> xptofer Colthurst, m<sup>r</sup> Roger Style[^sec-04-fn-053], m<sup>r</sup> Wittm Kealinge[^sec-04-fn-054] & m<sup>rs</sup> o<sup>r</sup> principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunte and ffacto<sup>rs</sup> in the said voyadge, & eu<sup>r</sup>r of them respectiuelie, as the direccons & instruccons of this o<sup>r</sup> p<sup>r</sup>sent Comission maye Concerne their seu<sup>r</sup>all places of trust wherein the are ymployed the w<sup>ch</sup> voyadge Almightie god in his mercie make prosperous.

<span class="sc">Wheareas</span> we haue vpon a spetiall conceite of yo<sup>r</sup> [p. 52] wysedome, discrecõn & good gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup>, made choyse of you m<sup>r</sup> Henrie Middleton to be principall Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Generall of o<sup>r</sup> ffleete & haue submitted to yo<sup>r</sup> Comaund the ꝑsons of all the marchaunte Marriners & others ymployed in the seu<sup>r</sup>all shipps thereof w<sup>ch</sup> shipps we haue fitted and furnished w<sup>th</sup> all necessaries not onelie meete for the voyadge but such as you could require or wish to be supplied w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>r</sup> full Contentm<sup>t</sup>.

> _[Margin: [^sec-04-fn-055] The Compa: inducem<sup>t</sup> to make choise of theis psons.]_

WEE therefore expect on yo<sup>r</sup> parte, such a ꝑformaunce & carrying of this Gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>te</sup> Comitted to yo<sup>r</sup> Chardge as may not onelie Confirme vs in that hope and good concipt w<sup>ch</sup> induced vs to the choyse of yo<sup>u</sup> to this ymploym<sup>t</sup> but may add vnto yo<sup>r</sup> selfe an encrease & advancem<sup>t</sup> of yo<sup>r</sup> owne reputacõn, w<sup>ch</sup> noe doubt you may effect, obserueing this moderacõn in yo<sup>r</sup> said Gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>te</sup> soe to Comaund as you may be both loued and feared, not vsing aucthoritie to worke yo<sup>r</sup> private respect or revenge but studieing and endevo<sup>r</sup>inge to bringe this longe and Tedious voyadge to a ꝑfitable end, w<sup>th</sup> care of the saffetie, health & Comforte of yo<sup>r</sup> people & vsing yo<sup>r</sup> industrie to recompence soe greate a Chardge of ꝑvisions and other burthens and expences borne in this voyadge w<sup>th</sup> a ꝑfitable retourne to the gen<sup>r</sup>all state of the Companie.

> _[Margin: [^sec-04-fn-056] To vse the assistaunce of c<sup>r</sup>taine nominated.]_

AND that you may the better ꝑceede in an vnfallable hope of agood yssue of yo<sup>r</sup> endevo<sup>rs</sup> we wish and exhorte you first to depend Confidentlie vpon Godes ꝑvidence, & next ꝑpound to yo<sup>r</sup> selfe the good example of yo<sup>r</sup> late p<sup>r</sup>dicesso<sup>r</sup> S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster in the carryinge of the former voyadge. And forasmuch as noe man is soe absolute in his Course and direccõns for the manageing of any occasions of ymportaunce, but he May therein receiue light & espetiall helpe and furtheraunce by Conference w<sup>th</sup> others, Therefore we haue for yo<sup>r</sup> Assistaunce & helpe the better to vndergoe the Chardge of o<sup>r</sup> busines made choyse of m<sup>r</sup> x̃ptofer Colthurst, m<sup>r</sup> Roger Style, m<sup>r</sup> Will̃m Keeleing, m<sup>r</sup> Robert Browne[^sec-04-fn-055] & m<sup>r</sup> Edward Highlord,[^sec-04-fn-056] [p. 53] as o<sup>r</sup> principall m<sup>r</sup>chauntę ymployed in this voyadge to be readie w<sup>th</sup> their advice & aide to assist you in any thinge that may belonge to the same whome we pray and requier you not onelie to heare but loueinglie & kindlie to vse and respect soe as by yo<sup>r</sup> kinde Conversacõn mutuallie vsed & had the one w<sup>th</sup> the other there maye growe betweene yo<sup>u</sup> in soe firme a vnitie as shall be subiect to noe Iarr or distaste wherein yf you linke together, all thinge will passe w<sup>th</sup> felicitie and Contentm<sup>t</sup> otherwyse yf there fall amongst you Envie emulacõn or disagreem<sup>t</sup> there is noe hope of good successe of the voyadge but apparant hazard to the ou<sup>r</sup>- throw of the same. & this shall suffice for o<sup>r</sup> generall advise vnto you for such a moderacõn of gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>te</sup> to be pformed on yo<sup>r</sup> pte as may breede a good affeccõn towardes you in those that are submitted vnto yo<sup>r</sup> Com̃aund.

> _[Margin: <sup>3</sup> Dalie prayer to be vsed by the wholle Companie.]_

AND to thend that the wholle Companie Comitted to yo<sup>r</sup> chardg may pforme that due obedience & respect vnto you w<sup>ch</sup> is ffitt to be yealded to their Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or Generall, we doe herein ppound vnto you the care of the due execution of that principall meane w<sup>ch</sup> draweth all Christians to Conformitie and submission to such as are set ou<sup>r</sup> them w<sup>ch</sup> is the dayly invocacõn & religious wo<sup>p</sup>: & service of God, requiring you to take order that c<sup>r</sup>teine houres & tymes in eu<sup>r</sup>y day may be sett aparte for publique prayer & calling vpon the name of God, that like orders w<sup>th</sup> penalties to be seu<sup>r</sup>elie published & sett vpp in eu<sup>r</sup>y shipp agaynst the blasphemeing of the name of god, & all Idle and filthie Comunicacõn: That all vnlawfull gameinge especialie dice play may be abolished as that w<sup>ch</sup> pcureth not onelie the blasphemeing of the name of God, but Envie and quarrellinge frome whence many tymes pceedeth murders or att the least the impou<sup>r</sup>ishinge and vndoinge of many of the poore vngou<sup>r</sup>ned Marriners, who by the lib̃tie of dice playe loose their whole wages of the voyadge as yt is not vnknowne vnto you, by the practise of diuers in the last voyadge who to furnish them selues w<sup>th</sup> money in that vnthrifftie ymploym<sup>t</sup> ingaged them selues to pay 3 for 1 vpon their retourne, & thus haueing wasted [p. 54] their wage by such vnthriftie meanes went aboute to laye a scandall vpon the Companie, alledgeing they were oppressed by necessitie in the voyadge to enter into those excessiue vsurious Contente[^sec-04-fn-057] to mayntayne their liues.

> _[Margin: <sup>4</sup> To keepe Comp: one with another.]_
> _[Margin: <sup>5</sup> Warlike guard to be kept in watering or refreshing men &c:]_

<span class="sc">You</span> haueing thus sett an order to be obserued in eu<sup>r</sup>y shipp both for the service of God, & the Civill behavior of the Company amongest them selues, then for the better Assistaunce strength & Comfort that the whole ffleete may take one of another by keeping Company together through out the wholle voyadge vntill you come into the East Indies into the porte or Haven of Bantam, where you are to take order w<sup>th</sup> the m<sup>rs</sup> & Companie of eu<sup>r</sup>y shipp by the best observac̃ons & direccons w<sup>ch</sup> you shall in yo<sup>r</sup> Conference together agree vpon that you depte not out of sight one of another soe longe as you may possiblie keepe together to thend that yf any of you should be any way distressed vpon any occasion you may be releued and Comforted by the Assistaunce of some of yo<sup>r</sup> Consorte not being farr of. And yf you shall happen to be sepated by ffowle weather & cannot recouer the sight one of another in shorte tyme, yf yo<sup>r</sup> separac̃on or dispersinge happen to be before you come to Iland of May[^sec-04-fn-058] then lett that Iland be the place of yo<sup>r</sup> repaier or rendevous, that you may be drawen agayne together in Companie & there to staie one for an other 7 or 8 daies, & haueing made staie there soe longe & the Company missing, not being Come thither, then to depte forwardes on the voyadge, leaueing some apparent marke behinde you that you haue beene at the said Iland, as by raysing some heape of Stones together, setting vpp of a stake or marke and leaueing there *some lre* in or neare the place w<sup>ch</sup> may be found by them as shall come after, whereby they may knowe that the other shipp or shipps are past that place. And yf yo<sup>r</sup> seperac̃on be beyond the Iland of May then yo<sup>r</sup> Rendevous to be att the Iland of St Lawrence. And yf you shall be occasioned to land in any place for fresh water, or to refresh yo<sup>r</sup> men yt shall behoue you to keepe good order, & discipline by warlike guarde for the saffetie of your Companie least they should be surprized and fall into daunger by ou<sup>r</sup> much Confidence and [p. 55] securitie & the saffetie of yo<sup>r</sup> ꝑsons being ꝑvided for then yo<sup>r</sup> wholle Companie to be admonished to behaue them selues peaceably & Civillie towardes the people of that place, where you refresh for the supplie of yo<sup>r</sup> wantę, & that they be alsoe exhorted to a moderac̃on in feeding of fruitę & fresh victualls of that soyle, the w<sup>ch</sup> by their intemperate & vnmoderate dyet, may breede inconveniences formerlie found by experience to be the losse of many mens liues. And in such place or places of refreshing you shall doe well to giue spetiall order to some men chosen & appointed to that end, to make the gen<sup>r</sup>all ꝑvision bot of ffresh victualls & fruite for the whole ffleete whereby an equall repartition thereof may be made for the Company of eu<sup>r</sup>y shipp and that eu<sup>r</sup>y one be not w<sup>th</sup>[out] lymitac̃on, to victuall hymselfe according to his intemperate appetite, and this order to be taken ꝑhibiting eu<sup>r</sup>y ꝑson vpon payne of seveare ponishm<sup>te</sup> that they doe not raunge and straggle after fresh victualls and fruitę but by such order as shall be p<sup>r</sup>scribed vnto them.

> _[Margin: 6 refreshing by landing not to be vsed vpon light occasion.]_

VPPON such oportunities of necessarie landinge of yo<sup>r</sup> people for refreshinge, w<sup>ch</sup> by noe meanes we would haue otherwyse to be vsed vpon light occasion for that yt will greatlie hinder the voyadge wee doe requier you to giue order vnto the preacher to prepare him selfe to preach to the people being Come together out of the seu<sup>r</sup>all shipps, makeing his choyse of such ffitt argum<sup>te</sup> & places of scripture as may be most agreable to the tyme and occasion whereby the whole Company may be exhorted and taught the better to carrie themselues in the gen<sup>r</sup>all busynes. And that the preacher may haue the more Comforte in his mynistry, we pray you be carefull that all due respectę be geven him, not onelie by yo<sup>r</sup> selfe but by the wholle Company that his doctrine & exhortac̃ons by Contempt or neglect of his mynistrye retourne not w<sup>th</sup>out proffitt. for the place of yo<sup>r</sup> refreshinge we wish yt to be the Iland of St Lawrence, but not at Saldania in any wyse for the inconveniences of that Iland noted vnto vs by men of good experience, & their causion geven vs to be ware of the daunger of that place wherefore we requier you to shun this place as o<sup>r</sup> expresse order & will herein.

> _[Margin: 7 To goe thence to Bantam & to dispose of busines.]_

YOUR refreshing place being left & all oportunities taken [p. 56] for thadmonishing of yo<sup>r</sup> people both to the service of God w<sup>th</sup>out w<sup>ch</sup> noe enterprize cann be prosperous and to the Civill & orderlie carryinge of them selues in the voyadge, & in all service thereto belongeinge > they[^sec-04-fn-059] you are to shape yo<sup>r</sup> Course directlie for Bantam aforesaid. Att w<sup>ch</sup> porte as soone as you shall arriue & that you may Convenientlie drawe yo<sup>r</sup> selues together in Conference w<sup>th</sup> m<sup>r</sup> Willm Starkey [or] the agent w<sup>ch</sup> you shall finde theare succeedinge him in the busines. Then we doe requier you as god hath guided & brought you to yo<sup>r</sup> expected & appointed porte, where you may enter into the disposeing of yo<sup>r</sup> busines, that then you being Come to the m<sup>r</sup>chaundizeing porte of the voyadge you doe pceede therein as followeth. Viz.

> _[Margin: 8 To advice and Conferr, of y<sup>e</sup> state of the place : vsadge & all other Circumstances.]_
> _[Margin: 9 To lande moneys]_
> _[Margin: 10 Garblers sent]_

WEE DOE will and require you m<sup>r</sup> Henrie Middleton o<sup>r</sup> Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or Gen<sup>r</sup>all of the whole voyadge, & you m<sup>r</sup> xptofer Colthurst, m<sup>r</sup> Roger Style, m<sup>r</sup> Willm Kealinge, m<sup>r</sup> Robt Browne & m<sup>r</sup> Edward Highlorde o<sup>r</sup> principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunt*e* for the disposeing of the m<sup>r</sup>chandises & traffique of yo<sup>r</sup> saide voyadge that you advise & Conferr together w<sup>th</sup> m<sup>r</sup> w<sup>m</sup> Starkey, or w<sup>th</sup> whome soeu<sup>r</sup> standeth in the place of the Agent resident att Bantam of the state of the place & of the vsadge that o<sup>r</sup> Agent and ffactor<sup>s</sup> haue receiued since they were left theare & of all other Circumstaunces that may concerne the saffetie and benefitt of the trade, w<sup>ch</sup> being found to stand in good tearmes then you are to deliu<sup>r</sup> o<sup>r</sup> lres to o<sup>r</sup> said Agent & w<sup>th</sup> his advise to deliu<sup>r</sup> the king*e* ma<sup>ties</sup> lres & present to the kinge of that place, & then to land all such moneys as are laden in o<sup>r</sup> 4 seu<sup>r</sup>all shipps viz 11160<sup>li</sup> 12<sup>s</sup> in Royalls of 8 whereof in the red dragon DRAGON ffiue Chest*e* Cont: 4000<sup>li</sup> in Royalls in 40 bagg*e* HECTOR, ffower Chest*e* cont: 3200. in Royalls in 32 bagg*e*. ASSENTION, three Chest*e* Cont: 2400 in Royalls in 24 bagg*e* SUZAN, twoe Chest*e* Cont: 1560⅔ in Royalls in 15 bagges. [p. 57] w<sup>ch</sup> being done then to take informacon, from the Agent of the state of o<sup>r</sup> busines left in his chardge what quantetie of ladeing he hath in aredines for the shipps causing cawsing the dust to be sifte from the pepp, yf yt be not doene alredie vpod advise geuen [to] that end by o<sup>r</sup> former łres for w<sup>ch</sup> purpose we send w<sup>th</sup> you garblers w<sup>th</sup> siues and ffanns to thend that o<sup>r</sup> shipps should not be dischargded w<sup>th</sup> vnproffitable Comodities.

> _[Margin: II What Comodities fitt & what prouided att the Molloccos.]_

TO TAKE like informačon what Comodities & how much ladinge is pvided att the Molloccos conferringe w<sup>th</sup> o<sup>r</sup> said Agent what shipps of o<sup>r</sup> ffleete ar ffittest to goe for the Molloccos remembring that the Hector and Assenčon are victualled for 24 monnethes: the experience of o<sup>r</sup> said ffact[o<sup>rs</sup>] gayned by their longe aboade att Bantam will well informe you how to pceede in the sending of o<sup>r</sup> shippinge to the Molloccos and for the ordering of the m<sup>r</sup>chandize for that place.

> _[Margin: 12 The ships laden & sent from Bantam for England whoe is to goe to the Molloccos & to what end.]_

THE pvision for the ladeinge att Bantam being laden abourde o<sup>r</sup> shipps that are first to retourne for England & the Comaunders thereof shipped in the said shipps and those shipps p<sup>r</sup>pared readie w<sup>ch</sup> by you & the Agente shall be resolved vpon to goe for the Molloccos o<sup>r</sup> direcčon is that you m<sup>r</sup> Henrie Middleton to goe yo<sup>r</sup> selfe in one of the said shipps to the molloccos takeing w<sup>th</sup> you such of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors to leaue to reside in the Molloccos & such stocke for their maynetaynaunce, as you shall vpon Conference together att Bantam agree vpon to remayne in their hande for the mayntenance of them & the residue w<sup>ch</sup> are alredie Resident att Bantam by their aboade theare, in w<sup>ch</sup> space they may both learne the languadge of the Countrie, and dispatch such busines as they shall be by you appointed vnto: And we wish you to take w<sup>th</sup> you to Banda one or both of the garblers w<sup>th</sup> their instrm<sup>te</sup> and provisions to Clense the Cloues from dust and stalkes & the Nutmegge from Rumps and dust that o<sup>r</sup> shipps be not pestered w<sup>th</sup> the dust or garble of theis kinde of Comodities.

> _[Margin: noe particuler trade &c: pena[^sec-04-fn-060] losse of]_
> _[Margin: the Commodities laden except &c:]_

AND for that the voyage of this Condičon & greate chardge cannot admitt any priuate trade, o<sup>r</sup> will is that neither yo<sup>r</sup> selfe nor any others vpon any pticuler [p. 58] or other Accompt then the gen<sup>r</sup>all and ioynct stocke doe lade or be pmitted to lade any of theis Cōmodities in o<sup>r</sup> shipps viz: pepp Cloues mace Nut muge China silke Indigo, Amber greece, muske, sivitt, Bezar stones Camphire, Beniamyn Burrace[^sec-04-fn-061] or Synamon, but that what quantitie soeu<sup>r</sup> of theis Cōmodities may be had or brought vpp shall be laden for the ioynt accompte of the Company vpon payne of the losse of eu<sup>r</sup>y such Cōmoditie soe laden, & not laden vpon the ioynct Accompte. But yf vpon lycence demaunded of you the said Generall & you o<sup>r</sup> said principall marchaunte any m<sup>r</sup>, marriner or others shall be desirous to lade some small pporcõn or quantitie of China dishes or light triffles not exceeding the value of Three pounde, or not beareing aboue the bulcke of a small chest Then we doe order that all such goode soe laden by yo<sup>r</sup> privitie & lycence shall be entred into the Pursars Booke of such shipp wherein the same is laden to thend that yf any of them doe die by the waye their freinde may enioye that w<sup>ch</sup> is theirs according to their wills.

> _[Margin: what goodes left in theast Indies since bought &c what moneys & debtes &c:]_

<span class="sc">And</span> for the better remembraunce & instruccõn of you the said Gen<sup>r</sup>all & of you the principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunte what goode were left behinde at Bantam, in the Comeing away of S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster out of the Indies & what hath beene puided since by the Agent there as by their advice sent vs since the comeing home of o<sup>r</sup> shipps maye appeare. You shall vnderstand That S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster left att Bantā aboue 1500 bagge of pepp & by their łres sent from Bantam by the dutch shipps the agent wrote that he had puided 1500 bagge more. And after S<sup>r</sup> Iames gaue Comission to the Agent at his depture from Bantam that yf the dutchmen were disposed to buie any of the Companies pepp & and would giue good pffitt for yt that then the Agent should sell yt & pvide more for the Companie att better oportunitie & better rate vpon w<sup>ch</sup> Comission soe left you maye inquire what hath beene done for the benefitt of the Companie.


<!-- page: 151 | folio: 59 -->
<span class="sc">Itt</span> doth alsoe appeare by the abbreuiate of the accompte sent home out of the Indies that there remayned in the hande of the Agent m<sup>r</sup> Starkey 482 ffardells of Callicoes viz 8 Canisters of Pinthadoes[^sec-04-fn-062] & 117 ffardells of Checkered stuffes 51 ffardells of long malow girdles[^sec-04-fn-063] 59 ffs of girdles for *Sysan*,[^sec-04-fn-064] 110 ffs of Iava girdles,[^sec-04-fn-065] 13 Cheste of fine Pinthadoes 6 Cheste of diuers sorte of Comodities, 42 ffs of Browne Callicoes & in loose Pinthadoes, & in loose Pinthadoes by estimate made by S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster aboute 80 ffe att the least of all sorte soe [p. 60] that there might be in all packe & canister aboute 482 ſſe as aforesaid & in loose Callicoes so[m]e 30 ſſe soe as there appereth in the whole to be 512 ſſe since the dꬴpture of our shipps we vnderstand by their łres of the 15<sup>th</sup> of ffebruarie 1602 they had shipped [52 ſſe] for Banda in the Molloccos abourd o<sup>r</sup> Pinnace[^sec-04-fn-066] w<sup>ch</sup> we trust arriued there in saffetie w<sup>th</sup>in shorte tyme after her dꬴpture from Bantam, vpon the pceede of w<sup>ch</sup> 52 ſſe yt is hoped by vs that there maie be sufficient w<sup>th</sup> a lardge ou<sup>r</sup>plus to lade the 2 shipps we here appointed to the Molloccos w<sup>th</sup> mace, Cloues, & Nutmuge soe that there remayned after the dꬴpture of the Pinnace from Bantam 452[^sec-04-fn-067] ſſe or thereaboute Conteyneing the best & richest Comodities of the whole Complem<sup>te</sup> of the prize the other 52 ſſe sent to the molloccos being of the meanest & basest kinde of the said prize goode w<sup>ch</sup> greate remaynder of goode att Bantam of the best & greatest value cannot but vpon the pceede thereof [make] readie before yo<sup>r</sup> arrivall att Bantam great quantities of Comodities to be retourned from thence.

> _[Margin: The 11160 <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>5</sub><sup>li</sup> 12<sup>s</sup> to be ymployed not in spices but in other Commodities mor proffitable.]_

BESIDES all w<sup>ch</sup> seu<sup>r</sup>all quantities of goods before mencioned there remayned in the hande of m<sup>r</sup> Starkey & the rest at the dꬴpture of the shipps homewarde 4907 Royalls of Eight & in debte 3941. pece of 8 being Compassed in the same 77 bagge of pepp w<sup>ch</sup> pepp was rec<sup>d</sup> into their Custodie soe as yf all the goode & money left w<sup>th</sup> them & that w<sup>ch</sup> might & hath pceeded thereof doe rest in saffetie you shall not onelie haue sufficient to lade yo<sup>r</sup> fower shipps w<sup>th</sup> pepp mace Cloues & Nutmuge but as many more shipps of the like burthen beside the moneys w<sup>ch</sup> you carrie alonge w<sup>th</sup> you in the shipps amounteing to 11160 <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>5</sub><sup>li</sup> 12<sup>s</sup> in Royalls as aforesaid, w<sup>ch</sup> moneys because yo<sup>u</sup> knowe that spices are heere of noe value we wish you to ymploy in some other Comodities that may be of more estimãcõn & yeald a better pffitt as rawe silke well Chosed & bought at resonable prices or such like Comodities wherew<sup>th</sup> theis parte of Christendome haue not beene gluted as w<sup>th</sup> spices.

> _[Margin: The 11160 <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>5</sub><sup>li</sup> 12<sup>s</sup> not to be mixt in accompt]_
> _[Margin: w<sup>th</sup> the former Adventure & cause whie.]_

AND touching the said 11160 <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>5</sub><sup>li</sup> in Royalls now sent in theis ships forsomuch as yt is a new supplie of stocke sent out vpon a new Aduenture, we will not haue [p. 61] the same to be mixed in accompt w<sup>th</sup> the former adventure but doe requier you to keepe the accompt of the ymploym<sup>t</sup> hereof alone by y<sup>t</sup> selfe. And to the end that the same may be distinguished from the former accompte of the first Adventure we doe pray and requier you the said Gen<sup>r</sup>all and principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunte by Conference and assistaunce of the ffactor<sup>s</sup> resident both att Bantam & Banda to make a valuacõn as neare as you cann of all the remaynder of the first stocke, what it may be worth to be sold, for that many of the Adventurers who are vnwilling to hange & Contynue longe in accompte vnpfect & vndetermined ar desirous to sell their remaynders of their stocke to such as will Continue the trade, and therefore a valuacõn is to be conceiued & sent w<sup>th</sup> the retourne of theis shipps att any hand being a matter not onelie desiered by the gen<sup>r</sup>alitie but expreslie agreed vpon & Chardged vpon vs that haue the ordering of the busines to see y<sup>t</sup> pformeđ, w<sup>ch</sup> chardge being not in vs to pforme we laye vpon you in whose power the pformaunce thereof lieth as you will aunsweare the neglect thereof.

> _[Margin: what m<sup>r</sup> Starkey hath besides the former goodes &c: left att Bantam.]_

<span class="sc">Besides</span> the former pticulers of prize goode & moneys before mencioned there appeth further to rest in the hande of m<sup>r</sup> Starkey and the other ffactor<sup>s</sup> 10 peeces of Clothes of diuers coullor<sup>s</sup> Cont: 514 english yarde a bason & Ewer of siluer poiz 102 oz, twoe standing Cupps poiz 63 oz whereof they are to giue you an accompt att yo<sup>r</sup> being att Bantam.

> _[Margin: What wood is to be prouided.]_

<span class="sc">Iff</span> those pte of the Indies doe yeald any good quantitie of Ibony ffarnando bucke[^sec-04-fn-068] or such like heavie wood of value, you may pvide soe much thereof as will ballast yo<sup>r</sup> shipps soe that the same take vpp [p. 62] noe roome of stowinge that maye otherwyse be more p̃fitablye ymployed.

> _[Margin: To p̃rvent the Portingalls mallice & what is to be carried to the Molloccos.]_

<span class="sc">And</span> forasmuch as we are not ygnoraunt that the mallice of the Portingalls towarde o<sup>r</sup> discou<sup>r</sup>y of the trade to those p̃tes will not lett him abstayne from all practices of annoyaunce w<sup>ch</sup> lieth in his power to offer and p̃forme to the trade of the Mollocos, who happilie[^sec-04-fn-069] maye by some layinge of waight for the intercepting of o<sup>r</sup> Penace sent to Banda depri[ue] vs of the p̃visions w<sup>ch</sup> otherwyse that voyadge might supply vs w<sup>th</sup>all yf any such or other p̃rventing accident hath happened: yet would we haue you to carrie in yo<sup>r</sup> twoe shipps appointed for the Molloccos such quantitie of Pinthadoes moneys & other p̃visions as may suffice to lade the said twoe shipps.

> _[Margin: leaueing other thinges of the state of y<sup>e</sup> busines to Consideracon and the states & healthes of men &c:]_

<span class="sc">Thus</span> we haue touched many p̃ticulers of o<sup>r</sup> busines not w<sup>th</sup>standinge many other thinge may occur w<sup>ch</sup> may greatlie concerne vs, w<sup>ch</sup> we must leaue to yo<sup>r</sup> good Considerac̃ons to deale therein as time and occasion shall offer you occasion Comendinge vnto your care the state of such as shall fall sicke in the voyadge either outward or inward that they may be Comforted: And yf the die see that their goode may be kept in saffetie, and their wills & dispotition thereof soe well testified that there growe not theke[^sec-04-fn-070] suspition of the truth of some of their wills as hath beene had of the wills of others that dyed in the last voyadge.

> _[Margin: Anie dieing others to be placed as they were first appointed & soe consequentlie &c:]_

<span class="sc">And</span> forasmuch as the daies ot mans lyfe are lymitted & the c<sup>r</sup>taine lymitac̃on thereof onelie knowne vnto god, we doe heere by ordeyne & puide, that whereas we haue appointed & placed you the said Henrie Middleton in the Redd Dragon as Gen<sup>r</sup>all or gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the wholle ffleete & you m<sup>r</sup> xptofer Colthurst as leiuetenant gen<sup>r</sup>all and principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunt in the Hecto<sup>r</sup> & you m<sup>r</sup> Roger Style o<sup>r</sup> principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunte in the Assenc̃on, & you m<sup>r</sup> Will̃m Keeleinge another of o<sup>r</sup> principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunte in the Suzan: yf therfore yt shall happen any of you to decease in this voyadge we doe ordeyne that he that in place & order by vs appointed to [p. 63] goe as principall in eu<sup>r</sup>y shipp w<sup>ch</sup> shall surviue the ptie deceased shall & may by the appointem<sup>t</sup> of the Generall, shall[^sec-04-fn-071] him selfe in the shipp out of w<sup>ch</sup> the said ptie did decease, and hold his place in the same shipp and the place that the ptie deceased held gen<sup>r</sup>allie in the voyadge and soe a succession to be held from the generall to the Leiuetenaunte from the leiuetenaunte to the principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunt placed in the Assenc̃on from the principall m<sup>r</sup>chant of the Assenc̃on to the principall m<sup>r</sup>chant placed in the Suzan : And yf yt shall happen all the principalls of the seu<sup>r</sup>all shipps to decease (as god forbid[]) the like succession to holde & be kept by the seu<sup>r</sup>all m<sup>r</sup>chaunte appointed to hold the second places in eu<sup>r</sup>y the said shipps & soe in succession from one to another according as the seu<sup>r</sup>all m<sup>r</sup>chaunte hold place in eu<sup>r</sup>y shipp.

> _[Margin: wheare m<sup>r</sup> Starkey shall be shipped yf he retourne home.]_

P<span class="sc">ROUIDED</span> alwayes that yf m<sup>r</sup> Wittm Starkey o<sup>r</sup> Agent resident att Bantam doe come home in the retourne of the shipps then we doe requier you o<sup>r</sup> generall & principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunte to take espetiall order that he be pvided for & placed in such shipp as he shall be shipped as a man that we hould to be had in good reguarde, & to be respected accordinglie and yf any of the principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunte places fall void by the death of any of them, or otherwyse, that then he supplie that place in his retourne homewardes.

> _[Margin: m<sup>r</sup> Colthurst leauetenaunt to succeede m<sup>r</sup> Hen: Middleton gen<sup>r</sup>all yf he decease vnto whome Comaund of the men shall be as in the gen<sup>r</sup>all.]_

A<span class="sc">ND</span> lastelie whereas his ma<sup>tie</sup> vnder his great seale of England hath appointed you the saied m<sup>r</sup> Henrie Middleton the generall and principall Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of all his subjecte ymployed in the voyadge & you the saied m<sup>r</sup> xptofer Colthurst to be leiuetenaunt gen<sup>r</sup>all, And yf you the said xptofer Colthurst surviue the said Henrie Middleton then to succeed him in the place of Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or Generall w<sup>th</sup>out appointing any further succession by like warrant to any that is ymployed in the said voyadge and that yt lyeth not in vs to giue to any of the residue of o<sup>r</sup> principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunte any warrant for the Correc̃on of Offences by penall lawes to be executed vpon the bodies of any his ma<sup>ties</sup> subiecte, we doe in that behalfe as to men haueing [p. 64] reason and discrecõn & to men that feare god offer vnto yo<sup>r</sup> Consideracõns the benefitt of order & peaceable gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>te</sup> in matters & enterprizes vndertaken for a Comon good, reposeing in you o<sup>r</sup> seuerall m<sup>r</sup>chauntę & all you o<sup>r</sup> sev<sup>r</sup>all Officers appointed & intertayned in this voyadge a spetiall hope trust and Confidence that you will accorde and agree together and ioyne in freindshipp & amytie to doe & execute yo<sup>r</sup> vttermost endevo<sup>rs</sup> for the benefitt of the voyadge w<sup>th</sup>out Contencõn discord or emulacõn to be vsed amongst you guideing yo<sup>r</sup>selues therein by that gen<sup>r</sup>all Regim<sup>t</sup> & sea gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>te</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> o<sup>r</sup> English ffleete doe vse when they sorte them selues together, haueing espetiall & due respect to him that is the principall or cape m<sup>r</sup>chante & soe we Comend yo<sup>u</sup> and yo<sup>r</sup> endeuo<sup>rs</sup> to goode[^sec-04-fn-072] puidence who guide you w<sup>th</sup> his feare and defend you from all daungers Amen.

> _[Margin: Post scriptū.]_
> _[Margin: vnto whome the power of the factors placing shalbe in & o<sup>r</sup> placeing to be noe rule.]_

<span class="sc">As</span> touching such ffacto<sup>rs</sup> as are to be left in the Countrie or of those w<sup>ch</sup> goe now in theis shipps we doe agree and giue order by this o<sup>r</sup> Commission that the appointm<sup>t</sup> of the said ffacto<sup>rs</sup> to reside in those places shall be att the direccõns and Consent of you o<sup>r</sup> Generall, m<sup>r</sup> xptofer Colthurst, m<sup>r</sup> Starkey and m<sup>r</sup> Morgan or any three of you, wherein we hope you will haue that Consideracõn as to make choyse of the fittest : neither lett the placeing of o<sup>r</sup> ffacto<sup>rs</sup> in the seu<sup>r</sup>all shipps as, they are alredie placed be any rule to you, or any ground for them to enioye those places of ymploym<sup>t</sup> wherein you are to bestowe them, otherwyse then they shall be found able & meete to deserue that trust of ymploym<sup>te</sup>.

> _[Margin: what we were advised of out of the lowe Countries from Bantam since all thinges were in a redines.]_

<span class="sc">The</span> shipps being readie to depte & all o<sup>r</sup> Comissions & instruccõns being resolued vpon and finished : wee receiued łres out of the lowe Countries w<sup>ch</sup> came from o<sup>r</sup> ffacto<sup>rs</sup> from the East Indies by the dutch shipps viz from m<sup>r</sup> Will<sup>m</sup> Starkey of the 22<sup>th</sup> of Iune and 2 other łres one from Edmond Scott and the other from Thomas Tudd both dated the 17<sup>th</sup> of August 1603. by w<sup>ch</sup> latter łres we were aduised of the death of m<sup>r</sup> Starkey and m<sup>r</sup> Morgan & of others who were left att Bantam and alsoe of the damadge that [p. 65] happened vnto vs in o<sup>r</sup> goode burnt by fyer in the dutch warehowse together w<sup>th</sup> the disappointem<sup>t</sup> of o<sup>r</sup> intended voyadge to the Molloccos by the Contrarietie of wynde.[^sec-04-fn-073] All w<sup>ch</sup> thinge being Considered we take them as they were indeede the hand of god, who disposeth of all enterprizes according to his good will & pleasure, w<sup>ch</sup> Accidente howsoeu<sup>r</sup> by the death of o<sup>r</sup> said principall ffacto<sup>rs</sup> they doe in some manner moue vs to alter o<sup>r</sup> said Comissions & advises soe farr as we had appointed any thinge to be done by the advise of the said m<sup>r</sup> Starkey & m<sup>r</sup> Morgan, yet in substance we purpose to hold o<sup>r</sup> former resolucõns for the following of o<sup>r</sup> busines And in steede of the ꝑsons deceased we wysh you to advise & vse Conference w<sup>th</sup> the ffacto<sup>rs</sup> remayneing, whome you finde most apt & able to assist you in the direction of the busines and touching yo<sup>r</sup> pceedinge in the voyadge from Bantam to the Molloccos after order for lading of the Dragon and the Suzan w<sup>th</sup> pepp to retourne for England being taken we thinke y<sup>t</sup> fitt you Capt: Middleton p<sup>r</sup>pare yo<sup>r</sup>selfe w<sup>th</sup>all speede to goe for Banda and doe furnish yo<sup>r</sup> selfe w<sup>th</sup> the most aptest & ffitest of o<sup>r</sup> ffacto<sup>rs</sup> to attend you, and to be left att Banda, for the furder followinge of that trade according as yt may be found likelie to bring benefitt to the Companie wherein you are accordinge to yo<sup>r</sup> good discrecõn & Consideracõn to vse the more or fewer ffacto<sup>rs</sup> to be left there as you shall finde the more or lesse hope of benefitt to be made by their residence in that place not forgetting the Companyes desire as neere as you cann possiblie to cleare the former voyadge according to o<sup>r</sup> former direccõn, by a discreete & resonable valuacõn of the remayner. And for the accomplishing of ladeing att Banda in the Moloccos you o<sup>r</sup> said gen<sup>r</sup>all are to take w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> soe much of the Comodities remayneing in o<sup>r</sup> ffacto<sup>rs</sup> hande att Bantam as they thinke will serue for the puiding of yo<sup>r</sup> ladinge att the Molloccos according to the pportion geuen by S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster to puide, remembring that they dutchmen bought of Spillesbe[^sec-04-fn-074] the like Comodities to carrie to the molloccos [p. 66] for the better furnishing of their lading : but for yo<sup>r</sup> better assuraunce least the saide Comodities should not be in request there, you shall doe well to take w<sup>th</sup> you 10000, 15000, or 20000 Royalls of 8 as you shall thinke meete & being soe furnished both by wares and money, you may both puide you ladinge and supplie yo<sup>r</sup> ffactors w<sup>ch</sup> you shall thinke ffitt to leaue to recyde theare w<sup>th</sup> sufficient stocke for puision of Cloues and Mace agaynst another yeare. This piect being lade downe for the trade att Banda you shall doe well in yo<sup>r</sup> going thither to touch att the Iland of Amboyna or any other Iland by the way where Cloues may be had and to furnish yo<sup>r</sup> selfe w<sup>th</sup> what quantitie you cann gett whereby you may the lesse depend vpon yo<sup>r</sup> puision of Cloues att Banda, & haueing directed and ordered yo<sup>r</sup> busines for the Moloccos, then vpon yo<sup>r</sup> retourne to Bantam to take full and pfect knowledge of the wholle state of o<sup>r</sup> busines & to leaue 10 or 12 ffactors there w<sup>th</sup> such stocke as shall remayne vnymployed or as may be spared o<sup>r</sup> shipps being laden admonishing the ffactors to be more carefull to buye their pepp att the best advantage then they haue beene, & to buie of the largest pepp w<sup>ch</sup> heare beareth the best estimac̃on, and vnlesse you shall finde yt verie necessarie that some ffactors be left att Banda, we are of opinion & doe like well that the residue of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors be holden altogether att Bantam but herein we leaue you to yo<sup>r</sup> owne experience, as yo<sup>u</sup> shall finde the Course most convenient And soe as before Comend you to godę puidence

AND whereas o<sup>r</sup> ffactors deceased doe appeare to haue left some estatę behinde them w<sup>ch</sup> must haue meanes to come to the hande of such as haue interest therein we doe wysh you to take order: that all thingę that doe appeare to belonge vnto them be duelie and trulie inventoried & shipped aparte by them selues, and their wills saffelie kepte and brought home together w<sup>th</sup> their bookę & notę of their buieing and sellingę whereby there estates were encreased & gotten, to thend that the Company may be satisfied that they haue beene well delt w<sup>th</sup>all therein & their ffreinde receaue that w<sup>ch</sup> shall rightfullie appteine vnto them.


<!-- page: 159 | folio: 67 -->
> _[Margin: from the kinge of Tedora to his matie by Captaine Henrie Middleton deliured to his matie in Maye. 1606.]_

<span class="sc">This</span>[^sec-04-fn-075] writeing of the kinge of Tydore to the kinge ma<sup>tie</sup> of England is to lett yo<sup>r</sup> highnes vnderstand that the kinge of Holland hath sent hither into theis partes, a ffleete of shipps to ioyne w<sup>th</sup> o<sup>r</sup> auncient enymie the kinge of Turnato & the ioyntelie together haue ouer runn and spoyled parte of o<sup>r</sup> Countrie & are determined to distroy both vs and o<sup>r</sup> subiecte. Now vnderstanding by the bearer hereof Capt: Henrie Middleton that yo<sup>r</sup> highnes is in freindshipp, w<sup>th</sup> the kinge of Spaine we desire yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> that you would take pittie of vs that we may not be distroyed by the kinge of Holland, and Turnato to whome we haue offered noe wronge But they by forceable meanes seeke to bereaue vs of o<sup>r</sup> kingdome, and all greate kinge vpon the Earth are ordeyned by God to sucker all them that be wrongfullie oppressed soe I appeale vnto yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> for sucker agaynst my enimyes not doubting but to finde releefe att yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>ts</sup> hande. And yf yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> send hither I humblie intreate that yt may be Capt: Henrie Middleton or his brother w<sup>th</sup> whome I am well acquainted: Thus we end praying God to enlardge yo<sup>r</sup> kingdomes & bless yo<sup>u</sup> & all yo<sup>r</sup> Councells. Tydore.

> _[Margin: from the kinge of Bantam to or kinge wth a prsent of twoe Bezar stones by genrall Henr Middleton deliured to his matie ye 25 of Maye 1606.]_

<span class="sc">Alre</span>[^sec-04-fn-075] geven from yo<sup>r</sup> freinde the kinge of Bantam sent vnto the kinge of England of Scotland ffraunce & Ireland desiering god to p<sup>r</sup>serue yo<sup>r</sup> health & to exalt yo<sup>u</sup> more & more & all yo<sup>r</sup> Councells. And whereas yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> hath sent Generall Henrie Middleton he came vnto me in health. I did heare that yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> was come to the Crowne of England w<sup>ch</sup> doth greatlie reioyce my harte now England and Bantam are both as one. I haue alsoe receaued a present from yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup>. The w<sup>ch</sup> I giue you many thanke for yo<sup>r</sup> kindnes. I doe send yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> 2 Bezar stones the one waying 14 masses[^sec-04-fn-076] & the other 3. And soe god haue you in his keepeing.


<!-- page: 160 | folio: 68 -->
> _[Margin: ffrom the kinge of Turnato to his matie sent by Henrie Middleton or genrall directed to o<sup>r</sup> kinges matie wth a p<sup>r</sup>sent & deliu<sup>r</sup>ed in May 1606.]_

<span class="sc">The</span>[^sec-04-fn-077] kinge of Mollocco to the kinge ma<sup>tie</sup> of England Scotland ffraunce and Ireland sendeth greeting heareing the good reporte of yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> & of the greatnes of yo<sup>r</sup> kingdomes by the greate Captaine ffrancis Drake in the tyme of my ffather w<sup>ch</sup> was aboute 30 yeares past[^sec-04-fn-078] by the w<sup>ch</sup> Capt: my ffather did send a Ringe vnto the Queene of England as a token of Remembrance w<sup>ch</sup> yf the foresaid Drake were liueing he could Certifie yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> of the greate loue and freindshipp on either side he in the behalfe of the Queene my ffather for him & his successo<sup>rs</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> tyme after the depture of the said Capt we haue dalie expected his retourne, my father liueing many yeares after. And I after the death of my ffather liued in the same hope till I was ffather to 11 Children, since w<sup>ch</sup> tyme we haue beene informed that English men were men of bad dispotition, & came not as peaceable m<sup>r</sup>chaunte but as theeues. and robbers and to depose vs of o<sup>r</sup> Countries, w<sup>ch</sup> by the comeing of the bearer hereof yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>ties</sup> servant Capt: Henrie Middleton we haue found to the Contrary whereof we greatelie reioyce. And after many yeares of expectacõn of some English fforces by the pmyse of Capt: Drake heere arriued certeine shipps w<sup>ch</sup> we well hoped had beene English men, but they pued to be Hollenders, & then being out of all hope of sucker of the english nation we were enforced to wryte to the Prince of Holland to craue aide and succo<sup>r</sup> of him agaynst o<sup>r</sup> auncient enymies the Portingalles. And according to o<sup>r</sup> request he hath sent hither his forces w<sup>ch</sup> hath expelled all the Portingalls out of the fforte they here hould att Ambweno[^sec-04-fn-079] and Tydore, And whereas yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> hath sent vnto vs a most kinde łre by Capt Henrie Middleton yt doth not a little reioyce vs: as alsoe the said Capt Henr Middleton was desierous [p. 69] to leaue a ffactory here we were very willinge there vnto, and gaue o<sup>r</sup> Consent, w<sup>ch</sup> the Admirall of the Hollenders vnderstandinge he came and Challenged a former pmyse w<sup>ch</sup> we had wrytte to the Prince of Holland that yf he would send vs such Succo<sup>r</sup> as should expell the Portugalls out of theis pt*e* that noe other Nation should haue trade heare but onelie they, soe that we were enforced agaynst o<sup>r</sup> likeing to yeald vnto the Hollenders Capt request for this p<sup>r</sup>sent tyme. Wherefore we craue pardon of yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup>. And whereas the Hollenders Admirall doth soliscite vs not to hold any ffreindshipp w<sup>th</sup> the englishe nor to giue eare nor Creditt to yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>te</sup> łres : yett neu<sup>r</sup>theless for all their sute yf yt please you to send hither agayne they shall be most freindlie wellcome, & in token of ffreindshipp w<sup>ch</sup> we desire w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup>. Wee haue sent you a small remembraunce of a Bahare of Cloues o<sup>r</sup> Countrie being poore & yealding noe other Comoditie w<sup>ch</sup> we pray yo<sup>u</sup> to accept in good parte. And soe we leaue you to god who bless you and all yo<sup>r</sup> Councells. *Tarnata.*

Theis 3 foresaid łres were translated out of the India speech into English.

I MOSTE[^sec-04-fn-080] mightie kinge of Dachem and Sumatra to all psons that shall read this present writeinge, Greeting.

> _[Margin: Priuiledges from the kinge of Dachem and Sumatra to the Companie.]_

<span class="sc">In token</span> of o<sup>r</sup> espetiall freindshipp & vpon many good Consideracõns vs moueing, and cheeflie vppon the Contemplasing of the gratious łres receiued from the most famous Queene of England: we of o<sup>r</sup> espetiall meere motion doe signifie and declare to all people, that we haue intertayned into o<sup>r</sup> freindshipp, [p. 70] & holie league o<sup>r</sup> well beloued the *SERINISSIMA REGINA DE ENGLA TERRA*. to hold and keepe true and faithfull league w<sup>th</sup> her accordinge to the Comendable Course & law of all nations, vnto whose subiecte, we wish much felicitie and therefore doe giue and graunte by theis p<sup>r</sup>sente for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires & successor<sup>rs</sup> as much as in vs lieth to the said subiecte of the most noble Queene of England o<sup>r</sup> Confederate & eu<sup>r</sup>y of them theis articles, graunte & priuiledge heereafter expressed and declared.

FFIRSTE we doe giue and graunte ffree licence aucthoritie & power to all the people, ffactor<sup>s</sup>, m<sup>r</sup>chaunte or subiecte of the Queene of England that they may att all tymes heereafter for eu<sup>r</sup> suerlie and saffelie come into any portes or els wheare into theis o<sup>r</sup> dominiones & kingdome of Sumatra w<sup>th</sup> their shipps goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandize w<sup>th</sup>out any deteinm<sup>te</sup> or hindraunce to them, or to their goode: & theare to abide soiourne, buie & sell, barter and exchaunge according to their owne[^sec-04-fn-081] manner and fashion w<sup>th</sup> all manner of Nations whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> as well as w<sup>th</sup> o<sup>r</sup> owne naturall subiecte: both in spices & all other m<sup>r</sup>chandizes & soe they may tarrie in o<sup>r</sup> Countrie soe long as they will, & goe away when the list, w<sup>th</sup>out any ympedim<sup>t</sup> lett or hindraunce, paying all such debte as they shall owe to any of o<sup>r</sup> subiecte w<sup>th</sup>in o<sup>r</sup> said dominion.

FFURTHERMORE o<sup>r</sup> will & pleasure is that all such goode and m<sup>r</sup>chandize as any of the subiecte of the Queene of England shall bringe into this o<sup>r</sup> kingdome or any the partes thereof shall be ffree of all Custome or paym<sup>t</sup> whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> as well for that w<sup>ch</sup> shall be brought into theis o<sup>r</sup> dominions as for all manner of m<sup>r</sup>chandize they shall transporte out of the same for any forreine pte whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>.

ITEM yf any of their shipps in tempest of weather shall be in daunger to be lost, & pishe, & therevpon shall stande in neede of o<sup>r</sup> helpe wee will and Comaund that o<sup>r</sup> vessells w<sup>th</sup> all speede doe helpe & succo<sup>r</sup> them, to saue the same shipps & goode and what may be saued, to retourne to the said m<sup>r</sup>chaunte or their assignes they paying resonable Considerac̃on for their travell.

ITEM yf any Englishe man shall make his will & Testam<sup>te</sup> to [p. 71] whomesoeu<sup>r</sup> (by the same will [ )] he shall giue his goode, the ptie shall haue them accordinglie, and yf he die intestate, he to whome the cheefe ffacto<sup>r</sup> or gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> shall saie the goode of the dead to belonge, he shall posses the same.

ITEM that eu<sup>r</sup>y b̄gaine made by the said m<sup>r</sup>chauntę w<sup>th</sup> any manner of p̄son for any kinde of m<sup>r</sup>chandize shall be firme and staple & that noe man of either ptie may shrinke or goe backe from the same & yt shall be lawfull for them to goe before any of o<sup>r</sup> Iustices & to register the same in a Booke according to the teno<sup>r</sup> thereof, yf any Controu<sup>r</sup>sie shall aryse present iustice to be done to both p̄ties, & when they haue sold any of their wares to o<sup>r</sup> subjectę or any other they shall not retourne the said wares vpon the m<sup>r</sup>chauntę hande, but paie for them or ells they shall haue present iustice

ITEM yf any English m<sup>r</sup>chaunte ffacto<sup>r</sup> or servant shall offend the Agent or cheefe Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the ffactorie yt shall be lawfull for the said Gouerno<sup>r</sup> to doe iustice vpon the said ptie, or to send him home into England att his pleasuer, & further we graunte vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> power and aucthoritie to end any Controu<sup>r</sup>sie that shall aryse betweene them & to doe iustice accordinge to their owne lawes and Customes.

ITEM we doe graunte the said marchauntę and to their Successo<sup>rs</sup>, that yf any of them or of their servantę shall be wounded or be slaine in any pte or place of o<sup>r</sup> dominion, then informačon thereof being geven we o<sup>r</sup> iustices and other Officers will execute due correcčon & punishm<sup>t</sup> w<sup>th</sup>out delaie accordinge to the cause of the offence, soe that yt shall be an example to all others not to offend in the like. And yf it shall happen the ffactors servauntę or mynisters of the said m<sup>r</sup>chauntę to trespasse or offend, whereby they or any of them shall incurr the daunger of death, or of punishm<sup>t</sup>, that then the goode wares or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes of their Senio<sup>rs</sup> shall not therefore be forfected Confiscate seazed vpon nor spoyled by vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or Successo<sup>rs</sup> or by any of o<sup>r</sup> Officers ministers or subiectę but shall remaine franke & free as dischardged of all punishm<sup>t</sup> & losse.

ITEM we doe p̄myse the foresaid m<sup>r</sup>chauntę graunting yt for eu<sup>r</sup> for vs & o<sup>r</sup> heires that yf any shall bringe any manner of goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandize meete for Treasurie that we will not cause anie [p. 72] staie or arrest to be made of their said goode or m<sup>r</sup>chaundize to vs or for o<sup>r</sup> vses w<sup>th</sup>out present Content to be made by o<sup>r</sup> Thr̄er at such reasonable prises as the m<sup>r</sup>chaunte could sell them for ready money, & that noe price or valuacõn shalbe set vpon their goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes by vs or any Officers of o<sup>rs</sup>.

ITEM we of o<sup>r</sup> goodnes haue graunted to the said English m<sup>r</sup>chaunte their successo<sup>rs</sup> servaunte & deputies that doe or shall remayne in any pte of this o<sup>r</sup> kingdome of Sumatra whether yt be in Dachem or any other pte of o<sup>r</sup> dominion freelie to keepe their owne lawe & in any wyse none of o<sup>rs</sup> to force them to o<sup>r</sup> lawe or faith against their wills.

ITEM yf any man shall saie, that theis being Christians haue spoken any thinge to the derogacõn of o<sup>r</sup> holie faith & religion & haue slaundered the same, in this matter as well as in all others there shall noe false witnes in any case be admitted.

LAST of all to thintent that this league w<sup>th</sup> her ma<sup>tie</sup> & the aforesaid graunte & priuiledge w<sup>th</sup> her subiecte, may the better be obserued and inuiolablie be pformed, we by the grace of God greate kinge of Dachem & Sumatra for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires & sucssessors doe pmyse by o<sup>r</sup> princelie word in stead of an Oath inviolablie to maintaine & preserue & will cause to be inuiolablie kept p<sup>r</sup>served & mayntayned frome tyme to tyme & att all tymes heereafter & for the more ratificacõn we comaund all o<sup>r</sup> Captaines Iudges Customers Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>rs</sup> & servaunte wheresoeu<sup>r</sup> theis łres or priuiledge shall be seene throughout all o<sup>r</sup> dominions that they be obeyed in all pointe accordinglie as longe as the Queene of England of her pte shall duelie keepe and obserue this league & holie peace expressed in this priuiledge w<sup>th</sup> vs and o<sup>r</sup> subiecte we alsoe of o<sup>r</sup> Royall pte doe chardge & Comaund the same soe longe to be strayghtlie kept & obserued. And the Contrarie to this diuyne league and priuiledge, lett noe man presume to doe or saie any thinge.


<!-- page: 165 | folio: 73 -->

### A DISCRIPCON[^sec-04-fn-082] of the Iland of Banda w<sup>th</sup> the Townes and Ilande thereof: w<sup>th</sup> the wares or marchandizes therein spent & vttered & wares to be bought theare as followeth.

TO witt Lunter[^sec-04-fn-083] Nere[^sec-04-fn-084] in w<sup>ch</sup> towne we bought o<sup>r</sup> Nutmegges & maces, and theare sould diuers sortes of o<sup>r</sup> Stuffe Pinthados Iava girdles in barter for maces & nutte[^sec-04-fn-085] Madgawgen, Lykou, Artatten,[^sec-04-fn-086] Semar, Kamber[^sec-04-fn-086] Rere, Anwen, Dunno<sup>r</sup>, Dedyer, Rossengen,[^sec-04-fn-087] Laba taker[^sec-04-fn-086] Latter, Loekra Regacke Rata muferr Polayu,[^sec-04-fn-088] Palroyen.[^sec-04-fn-089]

> _[Margin: India wares]_
> _[Margin: Townes and places where the are made.]_

Wares and m<sup>r</sup>chandizes spent & vttered there namelie stuffe or Clothes as our men call them: & called by the Dutchmen kleetghees[^sec-04-fn-090] being the same & such like stuffe as S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster tooke w<sup>ch</sup> are made att Bengalla Mesepatamya[^sec-04-fn-091] Cheremandalle & St Thome, and as some saye alsoe att Suratt & Cambaya w<sup>ch</sup> stuffes as the dutchmen saie are thus called viz Dragon, Patta Kassa of the ffinest *Torya, Baffa, Telle Pricken, Kantkey*, *Mossaffey, Patta Malim Tzijnd, Sorassa Madynceus*[^sec-04-fn-092] Brasse peeces of Ordinances w<sup>th</sup> Chambers in the breeches w<sup>ch</sup> are to be had in Bantam but brought from Chyna as thought.
