IGHT high &c: att the retourne of o<sup>r</sup> subiectę from their last voyadge into yo<sup>r</sup> Countries we rec<sup>d</sup> from you both a łre of great kindnes & twoe Bezar stones both w<sup>ch</sup> we tooke verie kindlie as a testimony of yo<sup>r</sup> [desire][^sec-05-fn-046] to enterteyne Amitie w<sup>th</sup> vs. Especiallie we were pleased [to vn][^sec-05-fn-046]derstand by their reporte how kindlie they were vsed in yo<sup>r</sup> Cou[ntrie][^sec-05-fn-046] in matters concerning their traffique w<sup>ch</sup> hath incouraged th[em][^sec-05-fn-046] to p̃ceede in yt. And vs to recomend them to you & yo<sup>r</sup> p̃tec̃cõn agaynst any that would oppose agaynst them, or molest them in their said trade in as ample measure as we would be willinge to doe to any of yo<sup>rs</sup>. yf their desires shall be to visitt o<sup>r</sup> Countries. To testifie vnto you o<sup>r</sup> kinde acceptaunce of yo<sup>r</sup> favo<sup>r</sup> shewed them & o<sup>r</sup> desire to continue Amitie w<sup>th</sup> you. We haue sent by this bearer o<sup>r</sup> servant atoken of o<sup>r</sup> loue w<sup>ch</sup> we hope shall alwaies continue & encrease betweene vs. Dated att o<sup>r</sup> Pallace of Westmī the 23<sup>th</sup> of ffebruarie 1606.


<!-- page: 201 | folio: 109 -->

### HIS MA<sup>TIE</sup> TO THE KINGE OF THE MOLLOCCOS.

> _[Margin: His ma<sup>tie</sup> to the kinge of the Molloccos. All the foresaid 7 lres w<sup>th</sup> the blanck were againe sent from his ma<sup>tie</sup>: to the Indies 1607 w<sup>th</sup> this addition onelie as followeth Viz Although we wrote vnto you the last yeare after y<sup>e</sup> retourne of o<sup>r</sup> subiectes from those partes, & sent you a present yet for that we doubt whether those lres be come to yo<sup>r</sup> handes, we haue thought good to visitt you againe w<sup>th</sup> new lres & w<sup>th</sup> a new present, & to lett you vnderstand that the contentes of o<sup>r</sup> form<sup>r</sup> lres were to this purpose That[^sec-05-fn-047]]_

JAMES BY the grace of God kinge of greate Brittaine ffraunce and Ireland defendo<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c: To the mightie kinge of the Molloccos & of the teritories & dominions adioyneing. <sub>^</sub> Att the retourne of o<sup>r</sup> subiecte from their last voyadge in yo<sup>r</sup> Countries we receiued from you a łre of greate kindnes & a Bahar of Cloues, w<sup>ch</sup> we tooke very kindlie as a testimony of your desire to enterteyne Amitie w<sup>th</sup> vs, but especiallie wee weare pleased to vnderstand of yo<sup>r</sup> kindnes towarde them in matters conc<sup>r</sup>ning their trade & traffique w<sup>th</sup> you, w<sup>ch</sup> hath incouraged them to pceede in yt, & vs to recomend them to you & yo<sup>r</sup> ptecc̃on agaynst any that would oppose agaynst them, or molest them in their trade in as ample manner as we would be willing to doe to any of yo<sup>rs</sup>, yf their desire shall be to visitt o<sup>r</sup> Countries. And whereas we vnderstand that some Hollenders whoe traffique w<sup>th</sup> you doe oppose them selues agaynst o<sup>r</sup> Subiecte w<sup>th</sup> euill speeches & other practizes to hinder their trade Although we doubt not but y<sup>t</sup> in yo<sup>r</sup> owne Iudgement you can easilie conceiue that m<sup>r</sup>chaunte not onelie of diuers Nac̃ons, but of one & the same nation will ofte tymes Calumniate each others for diuers respecte, & hinder what they cann those that happen into the saime trade w<sup>th</sup> [^sec-05-fn-048] the[^sec-05-fn-049] vse: yet haue we thought good to assure yo<sup>u</sup> soe much by o<sup>r</sup> łre, that their Superio<sup>rs</sup> & Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>rs</sup> will disallowe them in that practise being w<sup>th</sup> vs in verie good Amitie. Wherefore we doubt not but you will graunte vnto o<sup>r</sup> subiecte ffreedome of quiet traffique w<sup>th</sup> you w<sup>th</sup> saffetie for their psons, ships, & goode, & libertie to establish a ffactorie theare, (yf they shall desire yt) according to yo<sup>r</sup> princelie Offer in yo<sup>r</sup> said łre. And in the meane tyme for atoken of o<sup>r</sup> good will & desire to enterteyne yo<sup>r</sup> Princelie Amitie we haue by this bearer o<sup>r</sup> servant [p. 110] sent you a small present w<sup>ch</sup> we pray you to accept. Wherew<sup>th</sup> we Comend yo<sup>r</sup> ma<sup>tie</sup> to the tuition of the most high God. Dated att o<sup>r</sup> Pallace of Westminster the 23<sup>th</sup> of ffebruarie 1606.


#### THE IUDGE[^sec-05-fn-050] of the Admiralties warrant to app<sup>r</sup>hend such of the shipps Company as shall absent themselues.

WHEARAS diuers of the Companie hired for the East India voyadge absent them selues from the shipps, & some of them endevo<sup>r</sup> to shifte themselues away to the hindraunce of the voyadge now readie to sett sayle & the m<sup>r</sup>chauntę interessed therein. Theis are to will & requier you that you apprehend or cause to be app<sup>r</sup>hended all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such disordered p̄sons, as shall any way Offend conc<sup>r</sup>ning the p<sup>r</sup>misses, that he or they may be deliu<sup>r</sup>ed on shippbourde to their Comaunders theare to remayne, & to be p̄ceeded w<sup>th</sup> according to the quallitie of his or their offence. Whereof fayle you not as you will aunsweare the Contrarie att yo<sup>r</sup> pill. ffrom my howse neere the Doctor<sup>s</sup> Commons the 16<sup>th</sup> of March, 1606.

Your loueing freind *Tho Crompton.*

To m<sup>r</sup> Will̄m Pope Marshall of the Admiraltie or in his absence to the Generall of the East India Companies shipps, & all other Officers of the Admiraltie, & other his ma<sup>ties</sup> subiectę


<!-- page: 203 | folio: 111 -->
> _[Margin: A Commission from nis matie: to m<sup>r</sup> W<sup>m</sup> Kealinge and m<sup>r</sup> W<sup>m</sup> Hawkins februarie. 1606.]_

JAMES[^sec-05-fn-051] BY the grace of God kinge of England Scotland ffraunce and Ireland defendo<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c: To o<sup>r</sup> trustie & welbeloued Willm Kealinge & Willm Hawkins[^sec-05-fn-052] greeteing. Whereas diuers of o<sup>r</sup> loueing subiecte att their owne Aduentures coste & chardge aswell for the Hono<sup>r</sup> of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England as for the encrease & advancem<sup>t</sup> of trade of m<sup>r</sup>chandize w<sup>th</sup>in the same haue formerlie sett forth 2 voyages to the East Indies w<sup>th</sup> c<sup>r</sup>teyne shipps & Pinnaces by way of marchandizeing by w<sup>ch</sup> ships & Pinnaces they haueing discou<sup>r</sup>ed & begon to settle atrade in some pte of the said East Indies & their shipps being retourned from thence laden w<sup>th</sup> sundrie m<sup>r</sup>chandize brought frome those pte they the said m<sup>r</sup>chaunte intending to frequent those Countries of the East Indies by Continueing the trade alredie discou<sup>r</sup>ed & begoon, and endeu<sup>r</sup>ing furder discou<sup>r</sup>y of trade of those pte for the more ample vent of the Natiue Comodities of o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes, & retourning from the places of their discou<sup>r</sup>y such necessarie Comodities as shall be of spetiall vse & benefitt, both to vs and o<sup>r</sup> subiecte, are in hand to prepare & make readie their said shipps latelie retourned from the East Indies & to sett them forth agayne on a new voyadge. And whereas the said m<sup>r</sup>chaunte haue chosen you the said Willm Kealinge to be principall Gou<sup>r</sup>nor or [p. 112] Generall of all the m<sup>r</sup>chaunte Marriner*s* and other o<sup>r</sup> subiecte w<sup>ch</sup> are or shall be shipped in any of the said shipps. And you the said Willm Hawkins to be leiuetenante generall of all the m<sup>r</sup>chaunte Marriner*s* & other o<sup>r</sup> subiecte, w<sup>ch</sup> are or shall be shipped in any of the said shipps. We graciouslie favoringe their intended voyadge & approueing & alloweing of their choyse of you to the same Gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>te</sup>, being desirous to furnish you w<sup>th</sup> all fitt & Convenient power and aucthoritie to rule & gou<sup>r</sup>ne all & eu<sup>r</sup>y o<sup>r</sup> subiecte ymployed in this voyadge, by a due obedience to be by them yealded vnto you in the obserueing and executeing of all such good orders & Constituçõns as you shall thinke Conuenient, to ordaine & appointe for the furtheraunce of the said voyadge to the Hono<sup>r</sup> of vs & o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes & for the advauncem<sup>t</sup> of the said trade doe hereby straightlie chardge & Comaund all & eu<sup>r</sup>y pson & psons ymployed vsed or shipped in this voyadge in any of the said shipps to giue all due obedience & respect vnto you duringe the said voyadge, & to beare them selues one towarde an other, in all good order & quietnes for avoydinge any occasion that might breed Muteny quarrells or discension amongst them to the hindrance of the good successe, w<sup>ch</sup> is to be hoped for by gode puidence of the said intended voyadge, and in default of such dutie & obedience to be pformed towarde you, & for the Correcçõn & quenchinge of all such Muteny quarrells or dissention that shall or may be moued by the disorder euill dispotiçõn, or pversnes of any of the said psons. Wee doe hereby authorize you the said Willm Keelinge during the said voyadge, or during soe longe tyme as you shall lyue in the said voyadge to Chastice correct & ponnish all offenders & transgresso<sup>rs</sup> in that behalfe according to the qualitie of their Offences w<sup>th</sup> such punishm<sup>te</sup> as are comonlie vsed in all Armyes by Sea, when they are not capitall. And for Capitall Offences as for wilfull murther w<sup>ch</sup> is hatefull in the sight of God, or mutenie w<sup>ch</sup> is one offence that may tend to the ou<sup>r</sup>throw of the said voyadge the same being trulie and iustlie proued agaynst any of the pson or psons aforesaid. We doe hereby giue vnto you the said Willm Kealeing during all the tyme of the said voyadg or during soe longe tyme as you shall liue in the same, full power & aucthoritie to vse & putt [p. 113] in Execution o<sup>r</sup> lawe called Marshall lawe in that behalfe. And in case of yo<sup>r</sup> decease (w<sup>ch</sup> god forbidd) we doe then likewyse hereby aucthorize you the said Will̃m Hawkins to execute the power & aucthoritie by this o<sup>r</sup> Comission graunted to the said Will̃m Keeleing in as ample manner as is herein before expressed, & in such sorte as the said Will̃m Kealeing did or might doe by vertue hereof. And theis o<sup>r</sup> l̃res shall be vnto you, and either of you sufficient warrant & discharge, for the doing & executeing of all and singuler the p<sup>r</sup>misses. And for as much as att this present tyme we are in ametie w<sup>th</sup> all Christian Princes, & are vnwilling that any our subiectę should giue occasion of breach or hindraunce of that league or ametie w<sup>ch</sup> we hold w<sup>th</sup> any o<sup>r</sup> Confederatę ffreindę or Allyes. And because we are not ignorante of the emulac̃on & envie that doth accompany the discou<sup>r</sup>y of Countries & trade & of the quarrells & Contenc̃ons w<sup>ch</sup> doe many tymes fall out betweene the subiectę of diuers Princes that meete the one w<sup>th</sup> the other in forreine & farr remote Countries, in the Course & p̃secuteing of their discou<sup>r</sup>ies, and being desirous that o<sup>r</sup> subiectę should forbeare to moue or beginn any quarrell or contenc̃on vpon the subiectę of o<sup>r</sup> Confederatę ffreindę or Alleys either in their p̃ceeding, or retourne vpon or from any of their voyagę. Wee therefore doe hereby straightly chardge & Comaund you the said Will̃m Keeling & you the said Will̃m Hawkins & all other vnder yo<sup>r</sup> Gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>te</sup>, that neither in yo<sup>r</sup> voyadge outward or homeward or in any Countrie, Iland, Porte or place where you shall abide, or come duringe the tyme of yo<sup>r</sup> being abroade out of o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes or dominions where you meete w<sup>th</sup> any the Subiectę of the kinge of Spaine, or of any other o<sup>r</sup> Confederatę ffreindę or Alleys, or any other Nac̃on or people, their shipps, vessells goodę or m<sup>r</sup>chandize, you doe not attempt or goe aboute to sett vpon, take or surprise their p̃sons shipps vessells goodę or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes, or offer any iniurie, or discourtesie vnto them vnlesse you shall first by them, therevnto iustlie be puoked, or driuen in the iust defence of yo<sup>r</sup> owne p̃sons, yo<sup>r</sup> shipps, vessells, goodę or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes, or for recompence or recou<sup>r</sup>y of any the p̃sons goodę or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes of any o<sup>r</sup> subiectę that are alredie in or neere the East Indies as you will [p. 114] aunsweare the Contrarie att yo<sup>r</sup> vttermost prills. Witnes o<sup>r</sup> selfe at Westminster the 14<sup>th</sup> day of ffebruary in the fourth yeare of o<sup>r</sup> Reigne of England ffraunce & Ireland & of Scotland the 40<sup>th</sup>.[^sec-05-fn-053]

Copia p̃ b̃re de priuato sigillo.


### IN THE NAME OF GOD. AMEN. THE 9<sup>TH</sup> DAY OF MARCH. 1606.

A Comission sett downe by vs the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup>, Deputie, & Com̃itties of the m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London trading to the East Indies for better direc̃cõn of o<sup>r</sup> loueing ffreinde the Generall Leiuetenaunte, and others the Captaines, m<sup>r</sup>chauntę, m<sup>rs</sup> & Marriners in this our intended voyadge to the East Indies, w<sup>ch</sup> we humblie beseech Almightie God to blesse w<sup>th</sup> a happie Conclusion.

> _[Margin: I]_

INPRIMIS wheareas we they m<sup>r</sup>chauntę aforesaid w<sup>th</sup> a greate chardge & trouble haue prepared twoe shipps & a Pynnace viz the Read Dragon of 700 Tonns Anthonie Hippon[^sec-05-fn-055] m<sup>r</sup>, the Hector of 500 Tonns Mathew Mollineux[^sec-05-fn-056] m<sup>r</sup>, & the Consent of 115 Tonns Edmond Bonham m<sup>r</sup>, for a voyadge by Godę grace by them to be made to theast Indies, & haue furnished the same sufficientlie, [p. 115] & in plentifull manner w<sup>th</sup> men tackle victualls & all other needfull puisions fitt for such a voyadge. Of a spetiall trust & Confidence w<sup>ch</sup> we had in the integritie & iust carriadge of o<sup>r</sup> loueing freind m<sup>r</sup> Will<sup>m</sup> Kealinge, we doe appointe & aucthorize him Gen<sup>r</sup>all to goe in the Read Dragon & to Comaund o<sup>r</sup> said shipps, and all the men in them, haueing ꝑcured him sufficient aucthoritie from our sou<sup>r</sup>eigne Lord the kinge ma<sup>tie</sup> for that purpose : not doubting but that he will soe behaue himselfe, as he may be both feared & loued, & that he will w<sup>th</sup> all his diligence & endevo<sup>rs</sup> psecute o<sup>r</sup> designes, and labo<sup>r</sup> to bringe this our costlie voyadge to a happie end.

2 ITEM we appointe & ordeyne our loueing freinde Will<sup>m</sup> Hawkins to be leiuetenante of the shipps & men to take passadge in the Hecto<sup>r</sup> & David Middleton[^sec-05-fn-057] Captaine in the Consent, All w<sup>ch</sup> Comaunders ffacto<sup>rs</sup> m<sup>rs</sup> & Marriners we trust will soe carrie them selues w<sup>th</sup> such due respect one to another, & obedience to eu<sup>r</sup>y one of their Superio<sup>rs</sup>, as loue & kindnes [p. 116] be Continued on all side, & all whollie applie their witte & endevo<sup>rs</sup> for the due pformaunce of this voyadge.

3 ITEM & for that religious Gouernm<sup>t</sup> & exercyse doth best bynde men to pforme their duties, yt is principallie to be cared for that prayers be said Morneing & euening in eu<sup>r</sup>y shipp & the whole Companie called there vnto, w<sup>th</sup> diligent Eies that none be wantinge, that all ioynctlie may w<sup>th</sup> reuerence & humilitie pray vnto almightie God to blesse & p<sup>r</sup>serue them from all daungers in this longe & tedious voyadge.

4 ITEM that noe blaspheameinge of God, swearing, theft dronkennes or otherlike disorders be vsed, but that the same be sevearelie ponished, & that noe diceing or other vnlawfull games be admitted for that most comonlie, the same is the begining of quarrellinge, & many tymes murther a iust occasion of Gode wrath and vengeance from w<sup>ch</sup> the Lord deliuer vs all. Therefore yt shall be needfull that such orders be sett vpp and published in eu<sup>r</sup>y shipp & such ponishm<sup>t</sup> appointed for such offences as may giue notice to eu<sup>r</sup>y man, what he ought to avoied.

5 ITEM that spetiall order be geuen, that noe liquor be spilt in the ballast of the shipps or filthines be left w<sup>th</sup>in bourde w<sup>ch</sup> in heate breedeth Noysome smells, & infec̃cõn, but that there be a diligent care to keepe the ou<sup>r</sup>lopps[^sec-05-fn-058] & other places of the shipps cleane & sweete, w<sup>ch</sup> is a notable preservac̃on of health, wherein the dutchmen doe farr exceede vs in Cleanelines to their greate Comendacons & disgrace to o<sup>r</sup> People.

6 ITEM that Continuall & true Iournalls be kept of eu<sup>r</sup>y daies course & Nauigac̃on during the wholle voyadge w<sup>th</sup> a true relac̃on of eu<sup>r</sup>y thinge that passeth, & this not onelie to be done by the seu<sup>r</sup>all Captaines, m<sup>rs</sup> Pylotte & m<sup>rs</sup> mate, but alsoe by the m<sup>r</sup>chaunte & Pursars: and that some of the Principalls in each shipp, may conferre together att convenient tymes, when the Generall shall call them theare vnto, to thend that yf any haue forgotten, what an other obserued the same may be added, soe as a pfect discourse may be sett downe to be [p. 117] presented to the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie, when god shall graunt them a saffe retourne, to be kept for better direc<span class="sc">c</span>õn of posteritie.

7 ITEM that the Generall & m<sup>r</sup> of his shipp, doe sett downe and deliu<sup>r</sup> such instructions to the Comaunders in the other shipps that they may all keepe Company together for the better releife & Comforte one of another : And yf sepera<span class="sc">c</span>õn of them should happen by Constrainte of Tempest that they should agree vpon a course before hand, & of a place, whither to applie their selues to finde the rest.

8 ITEM that the Generall, & m<sup>r</sup> of his shipp, take due notice of the seu<sup>r</sup>all p̄visions deliu<sup>r</sup>ed to eu<sup>r</sup>y shipp, & to settle the same in the chardge of the Officers, appointed for that purpose in each shipp, & that the same be entred in the Pursars Booke vnderwritten by the said Officers, to thend that such thinge as are p̄uided for their needfull supplies may not be ymbeselled, & that nothinge thereof be ymployed for any vse whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>, w<sup>th</sup>out a Warrant vnder the hand of the Generall directed to the Officer that hath such Chardge, w<sup>ch</sup> warrant shall serue for his dischardge in his accompte, otherwyse to be aunswearable for the same w<sup>th</sup> his wage : eu<sup>r</sup>y such warrant to be registred in the Pursars booke, the day of the monneth, & the occasion, & this vpon forfe<span class="sc">c</span>ture of soe much out of the Pursars wage, This order to be obserued alsoe in eu<sup>r</sup>y of the shipps by the Comaunders, m<sup>rs</sup>, Pursars & Officers as aforesaid.

9 ITEM we Com̄end vnto you the Gen<sup>r</sup>all principallie, & to the rest of the Comaunders & mrs an espetiall care, that at eu<sup>r</sup>y place where you shall water, & refresh yo<sup>r</sup> men you call the Companies together, geauing them seveare warninge to behaue themselues peaceablie & Ciuillie, towarde the people of that place (yf any be theare) the better to p̄cure their ffreindshipp, towarde the supplie of yo<sup>r</sup> wante, & the like in eu<sup>r</sup>y place wheare you come, least the losse of yo<sup>r</sup> lyues & ou<sup>r</sup>throwe of o<sup>r</sup> voyadge pay for yo<sup>r</sup> disorders, beside an vtter discreeditt to o<sup>r</sup> Nation, & that yo<sup>r</sup> men doe vse, a discreete meanes in eateing of fruite, or fresh victuals least they surfitt & ffall into diseases, whereof we haue had too much experience. And the better to refraine vnrulie appetite wee hold yt Convenient, that the Gen<sup>r</sup>all appointe some of the discreetest in the Companies, to p̄cure & [p. 118] puide in such places, what you want, & the same being brought to the Gen<sup>r</sup>all, by him to be reparted to eu<sup>r</sup>y Companie, what may be needfull, & that none p<sup>r</sup>sume to doe the Contrarie w<sup>th</sup>out seveare ponishment. And that a spetiall care be had, to releeue the sicke w<sup>th</sup> such fresh meate & other Comfortable thinge, wherew<sup>th</sup> we haue furnished each shipp for that purpose, & not other wyse to be spent in Royott & banquetting & soe the sicke pishe for wante of thinges needfull.

10 ITEM for the ffittest place of reffreshinge, we wysh you to shape your Course to the Porte of St. Augustine in the Iland of St. Lawrence[^sec-05-fn-059] where you shall finde good harbo<sup>r</sup> & plentie of victualls: in w<sup>ch</sup> place yt will not be ffitt to make longe aboade, but make hast & endevo<sup>r</sup> to be vpon the Coaste of Melynde in the monneth of Iulie att the furdes[t] but for yo<sup>r</sup> better direccoñ therein, we referr you to the instruccoñ[s] of S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster now deliu<sup>r</sup>ed you herew<sup>th</sup>,[^sec-05-fn-060] who can best direct you, for yo<sup>r</sup> Course vpon that Coaste by his owne experience except you in yo<sup>r</sup> discrecõns finde otherwyse more fitt: Still standing vpon yo<sup>r</sup> guard in euerie place, w<sup>th</sup>out yealding any trust to those people.

11 ITEM after yo<sup>r</sup> depture frome the Porte of S<sup>t</sup> Augustine towarde the Coaste of Melinde, beware of the fflatte of Ivdea[^sec-05-fn-061] w<sup>ch</sup> lie betweene the Iland of St Lawrence & the firme land: vpon w<sup>ch</sup> fflatte yt is said the Currant doth sett. There is alsoe an Iland [p. 119] vpon the Coaste of Melynde, verie ffitt for refreshinge yo<sup>r</sup> people as wee are informed, & whereof the Hollenders had experience in their last voyadge that way: The w<sup>ch</sup> Iland is called Zanzibar, where yf you finde yt needfull & haue tyme for that purpose, you may theare water and refresh yo<sup>r</sup> Companies: wheare yt shall not be amisse yf you cann haue them, to buy some Oliphauntę teeth, w<sup>ch</sup> are bought att Mozambique, & on the Coaste of Melinde in greate aboundaunce, & carried into the Indies: That Commoditie is exceedinglie well requested in *Cambaya*. Alsoe store of Amber greece, is likewyse to be had in the Coaste of Melynde, & att S<sup>t</sup> Lawrence Iland. But goe not either to Mozambick nor to the Iland of Pemba in any hand but leaue yt on yo<sup>r</sup> labo<sup>r</sup> side.

12 ITEM haueing refreshed yo<sup>r</sup> people w<sup>th</sup>all speed to shape yo<sup>r</sup> Course for Zocotora neere the mouth of the Read Sea, where alsoe is good refreshing, & the best Alloes Zacatrina, in the world, whereof we wysh you to buy 2 or 3 Tonns weight: beside yt is said there is stoore of Amber greece, & other good thinge whereof we pray you to take notice, & buye what you thinke Convenient: but still in all your m<sup>r</sup>chandizinge be carefull to putt of some of yo<sup>r</sup> English Comodities in truck, in this Iland we doubt not but that you may be furnished, both for Pilottę for Aden & vnderstand what trade is there to be had what they people be, & of what interteynem<sup>t</sup> towarde straungers, whereof informe yo<sup>r</sup> selues, in the best manner you may & soe w<sup>th</sup>all Convenient speed direct yo<sup>r</sup> Course for Aden, or some other place theareaboute, w<sup>ch</sup> you may learne to be more ffitt for intertaynem<sup>t</sup> of you w<sup>th</sup> all the 3 shipps, you haueing tyme inough to goe into the Indies w<sup>th</sup> that Monsoone, and being arriued neere the place, come to an Anco<sup>r</sup>, but take heede you come not w<sup>th</sup>in their daunger,[^sec-05-fn-062] still expecting & feareing evill though there be noe cause, & by some Convenient & speedie meanes lett yt be knowne to the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the place, that you are English m<sup>r</sup>chauntę, & haue brought łres vnto him, from the kinge ma<sup>tie</sup> seekeing onelie peaceable trade, aswell for the sale of o<sup>r</sup> Comodities, as for buying of others, for w<sup>ch</sup> purpose [p. 120] we appointe Willm Hawkins to deliu<sup>r</sup> his ma<sup>ties</sup> lres, to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup>, & therew<sup>th</sup> such present as you think fitt: & to treate w<sup>th</sup> him for priuiledge & ffreedome of trade for soe many yeares as you cann, declaring that o<sup>r</sup> kinge is in league w<sup>th</sup> the Grand Signio<sup>r</sup> that o<sup>r</sup> people doe trade into Cairo, Aleppo, Damasco, Constantinople, & in all other his dominions freelie. And that o<sup>r</sup> kinge hath now a leidger[^sec-05-fn-063] Imbassado<sup>r</sup> in Constantinople, w<sup>ch</sup> loue of the Grand Signio<sup>r</sup> towarde our Nac̃on hath ymbouldened vs to visitt that place w<sup>th</sup> our shipps & goode now desireing by his favorable lycence to trade as Ciuill and peaceable m<sup>r</sup>chaunte, & that you desire to settle a factorie theare, yf by his honorable favo<sup>r</sup> you may be pmitted soe to doe: assureing him that by o<sup>r</sup> trade his Customes will be greatlie encreased, for that we shall indevo<sup>r</sup> to fetch that from thence w<sup>ch</sup> we now fetch from the Molloccos Bantam & diuers other places in the Indies: To w<sup>ch</sup> yf he yeald yt shall be needfull that you craue Articles of priviledge from him for o<sup>r</sup> Nation the better to incourradge vs to frequent that place. And for your better direc̃cõn, we haue deliuered you the Coppie of priviledge pcured for vs, by S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster from the kinge of Achen[^sec-05-fn-064] before mencioned adding therevnto what other thinge shall be needfull: In this busines Conferr together that you may pceede w<sup>th</sup> good advise, aswell for the priuiledge as whoe shall be left there for ffacto<sup>rs</sup>, except Marlowe[^sec-05-fn-065] & Pennell [p. 121] appointed for other places: Yf he giue leaue to settle a ffactorie, you must alsoe declare vnto the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> what sort*e* of English Commodities you haue brought, but acquainte him w<sup>th</sup> none of yo<sup>r</sup> money, yf you can sell all the Comodities w<sup>ch</sup> we now send att Aden, we rather desire the same then[^sec-05-fn-066] to make tryall of any other place.

13 ITEM arriueing att Aden, & findeing hope of intertaynem<sup>t</sup> & trade, we wish you all to spend some few daies in Consulta<span class="sc">c</span>õn & direc<span class="sc">c</span>õns [(]still haueing reguard that you the Gen<sup>r</sup>all w<sup>th</sup> the Dragon & Pynnasse loose not yo<sup>r</sup> Monsoone) in w<sup>ch</sup> tyme yf you find that more of o<sup>r</sup> Comodities will sell theare, then is in the Hector, we wysh you to take out of the other shipps, what you thinke needfull, and leaue Willm Hawkins & Clarke w<sup>th</sup> the Hector & such other ffactors as may be thought meete to follow that busynes (whome we wish not findinge sufficient & present dispatch of o<sup>r</sup> Comodities & other m<sup>r</sup>chandizes of those p*te* sufficient & att resonable prizes to relade the Hector, then to stay vntill the shipps & Iounck*e* repaire thither from Cambaya, & other places w<sup>th</sup> the next Monsoone, att w<sup>ch</sup> tyme noe doubt you shall finde plentie of all the Comodities, the Indies doe yeald, w<sup>ch</sup> oportunitie we wish you to take []), And for the sale of o<sup>r</sup> Comodities we wish you to stand, vpon the value & estima<span class="sc">c</span>õn thereof, yett soe as you loose not the oportunitie of the first markett*e* & reasonable offers, least often veiwing them they fall to dislike, for Nouelties as you knowe drawe men to buie, and note that by the resorte of all sortes of people thither, you shall finde meanes to sell what Comodities of o<sup>rs</sup> are in any place requested yf you putt yo<sup>r</sup> selfe forwarde & by help of some brokers you seeke to deale: But you must be carefull to vse all men w<sup>th</sup> kindnes & Ciuillitie & soe[^sec-05-fn-067] that yo<sup>r</sup> men doe the like in any wyse, least disorders & scandalous behavio<sup>r</sup> cause you to be abhored & evill intreated. And for that Clarke hath beene brought vpp in the trade of Wollen Comodities, we wysh him to be vsed in the sale thereof who can best tell how to handle yt.

14 ITEM yf you finde theare, that any other of o<sup>r</sup> Comodities, [p. 122] or Coullor<sup>rs</sup> will sell better, then those we now send, or some of those more vendible than the rest, we desire to be adverticed ourland by some Moores that go to Argier,[^sec-05-fn-068] & direct yo<sup>r</sup> tres to Richard Allen Consull theare, to be sent hither w<sup>th</sup> speede, or to Aleppo to m<sup>r</sup> Paule Pyndar[^sec-05-fn-069] Consull, obserueing the note of a character[^sec-05-fn-070] w<sup>ch</sup> we deliu<sup>r</sup> you herew<sup>th</sup> for the better secretie.

15 ITEM for that we haue put into each shipp a porcõn of money viz into the Dragon 13 Cheste, into the Hector 8 Cheste & into the Consent one Chest. Wee pray you to Consider att yo<sup>r</sup> being att Aden, how much thereof, will be there needfull, either for helpinge to putt of o<sup>r</sup> Comodities & m<sup>r</sup>chandize in barter (yf otherwyse the same will nott sell) or to buye such of theirs, as ys needfull & ffitt for o<sup>r</sup> Countrie, & the residue to be continued in the Dragon for the Gen<sup>r</sup>all to ymploy for vs in the Indies.


<!-- page: 215 | folio: 123 -->
16   AND haueing pcured the dispatch of the Hector w<sup>th</sup> her full ladinge, o<sup>r</sup> direction is, that you Will<span class="sc">m</span> Hawkins retourne for England w<sup>th</sup> the next ffitt Wynde & weather leaueing theare for ffactor<sup>s</sup> (yf you thinke needfull[]) Hearne & Clarke, & such others as you may thinke meete w<sup>th</sup> orders to ymploy their endevo<sup>rs</sup> for finding out of ffurther trade, aswell for all sorte of Cloth & kersies & Coullo<sup>rs</sup> best requested, as all other of o<sup>r</sup> Comodities, & for the buying of all those Country wares obserueing still good & c<sup>r</sup>teine note of all sorte of Comodities brought thither from out of the East Indies.

17   ITEM for the better Gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>te</sup> of yo<sup>r</sup> men we pray you when you departe from each other call to the Gen<sup>r</sup>all for the duplicate of the kinge Comission, w<sup>ch</sup> he hath vnder the broade seale, and keepe the same in yo<sup>r</sup> power.

18   AND now touching you the Generall we pray you w<sup>th</sup> the Dragon & the Pinnasse to make noe longer stay att Aden then you must of necessitie as aforesaid, but therew<sup>th</sup> takeing due hold of the Monsoone shape yo<sup>r</sup> spedie course towarde the entraunce to Cambaya endevo<sup>r</sup>ing there to finde out what good saffe Harbor<sup>s</sup> are thereaboute for vs to trust to, for a mayntenance of a trade in those pte heereafter in saffetie from the daunger of the Portingalls, or other enymies, endevo<sup>r</sup>ing alsoe to learne, whether the kinge of *Cambaya* or *Suratt* or any of his havens be in subiection to the Portugalls, & what havens of his are not, together w<sup>th</sup> the daungers & depthes of the water there for passadge, that by this c<sup>r</sup>teine notice & diligent inquirie, (w<sup>ch</sup> we wish to be sett downe in writeing for the Companies better informa͠con) whereby we may hereafter attempt for further trade theare, or otherwyse desiste.

19   AND forasmuch as you haue theare but the Read Dragon & the Pinnasse doe not in any wyse send vpp to the kinge of Cambaia, or putt into any harbor<sup>s</sup>, but rideinge att an Anco<sup>r</sup> in the open Roade some few daies to informe your selfe as afore specified, & what trade may theare be had, the sorte prises & goodnes of their Comodities, as alsoe what sorte of o<sup>rs</sup> are theare best requested: endevo<sup>r</sup>ing to drawe the people to come to you in their Iounckes, or boate w<sup>th</sup> some of their m<sup>r</sup>chandizes for w<sup>ch</sup> you may assaie to barter some of o<sup>r</sup> owne, or sell & buye as [p. 124] you shall finde occasion. Then take yo<sup>r</sup> speedie course alonge the Coaste of Mallabar directlie for Bantam, that you may come thither before the Hollenders yf yt be possible, for they will doe what they cann to prevent[^sec-05-fn-071] you att the Molloccos, & refreshing yo<sup>r</sup> men att Bantam & takeing the first of the Monsoone goe directly for the Molloccos, leaueing order w<sup>th</sup> the ffactors att Bantam to pvide & keepe all lading they cann gett to furnish you, yf you fayle att the Molloccos, or yf the Hector should come thither to lade.

> _[Margin: The dragon to goe to Bantam directlie from hence, & the Hector & assencon to stay if they shall see cause [^sec-05-fn-073]]_

20 BUT yf yt shall happen you come not to Zocotora in such Convenient tyme as you may Convenientlie goe to Aden, & haue the Monsoone to bringe you to the Indies, doe not then goe to Aden att any hand, but sayle directlie w<sup>th</sup> the three shipps towarde the entraunce of Cambaya: whither yf you come aboute the Middle of September you shall finde yt sooner,[^sec-05-fn-072] & faire weather, soe as you may very saffelie ride in the open Roade. At w<sup>ch</sup> place yf vpon diligent inquirie you finde a certaine & saffe expectacõn of trade, and that any of o<sup>r</sup> shipps may goe into saffe harbors free from daunger of the Portugalls, then doe you the Generall in the Dragon w<sup>th</sup>all speede take yo<sup>r</sup> Course alonge the Coaste of Malabar towarde Bantam, w<sup>th</sup>out any stay or abideing to trade by the way in what place soeu<sup>r</sup> & take w<sup>th</sup> you David Middleton to assiste att the Molloccos for the buieing of spices the Hector & Consent to stay in the open Roade neere the barr of Cambaya, & by some of the people w<sup>ch</sup> come out eu<sup>r</sup>y tyde from Suratt we wysh you m<sup>r</sup> Hawkins to send word to the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or Comaunder in Suratt, that there is a messenger arriued w<sup>th</sup> lres from the kinge mat<sup>ie</sup> of England vnto their kinge, praying the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> to send him a Boate w<sup>th</sup> saffe Conveyaunce to bringe him to Suratt, w<sup>th</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> Conveyaunce yf any come to you from the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup>, we wish you m<sup>r</sup> Hawkins to repaier thither, [p. 125] takeing w<sup>th</sup> you his ma<sup>ties</sup> lres & such other pvisions as you haue for that purpose & in yo<sup>r</sup> Companie take Anthonie Marlowe & Iohn Hearne and yo<sup>r</sup> owne servant & comeing to the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> att Suratt, present him w<sup>th</sup> some such guifte as you shall thinke meete & desire him to assist you w<sup>th</sup> meanes & guide to the kinge, that yo<sup>u</sup> may deliu<sup>r</sup> his ma<sup>ties</sup> lres vnto him according to yo<sup>r</sup> chardge, w<sup>ch</sup> haueing obtayned, make all possible speede there-w<sup>th</sup> & deliu<sup>r</sup> his ma<sup>ties</sup> said lre, & the present vnto the kinge, craueing a speedie aunsweare, and his resoluc̃on, yf he will be pleased to graunte you free and saffe trade in his Harbo<sup>rs</sup>, & Countries accordinge to his ma<sup>ties</sup> lre w<sup>th</sup> sufficient defence agaynst those that shall practise to impeach or hinder the same, or annoy or hurte any of the shipps, bodies or goode of any of o<sup>r</sup> Nac̃on, or not. But the better to induce the kinge to graunte vs priviledge & free trade, signifie that we will be readie to bringe him Armo<sup>r</sup>, & other munition from tyme to tyme in o<sup>r</sup> seu<sup>r</sup>all voyages, for the better inablinge him agaynst his enimyes, beside the increase of his Customes: w<sup>ch</sup> yf he pmyse to doe, then desire to haue Comissioners appointed to Consider w<sup>th</sup> you of Articles for priviledge of trade, wherein followe such direcc̃on as is form<sup>r</sup>lie geven you for Aden (w<sup>ch</sup> priviledge being obtayned and signed by the kinge, haueing taken yo<sup>r</sup> leave in Comlie manner, & rec<sup>d</sup> such Comaundem<sup>te</sup> in writeing directed to his Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>rs</sup> & Officers of his Townes & porte for yo<sup>r</sup> defence agaynst all disturbers of you in yo<sup>r</sup> peaceable trade, & for their Assistaunce of you & kinde interteynem<sup>te</sup> in the same: w<sup>th</sup> all speede make yo<sup>r</sup> retourne to Suratt, & haueing deliuered that kinge Comaundem<sup>te</sup> to the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Officers, Craue their Assistanc[e] w<sup>th</sup> Pylotte, & saffe Conducc̃on for yo<sup>r</sup> shipp, we meane the Consent, & therew<sup>th</sup> make all the speede you can to gett into the Harbo<sup>r</sup>, but first shew to some trustie Brokers, such patterns of yo<sup>r</sup> Cloth, kersies, and other Comodities as are in o<sup>r</sup> shipps, takeing knowledge, w<sup>ch</sup> sorte of them will be there sold, & accordinglie giue order to Iohn Hearne to goe w<sup>th</sup> the Pylotte to see some putt out of the Hecto<sup>r</sup> into the Consent & therew<sup>th</sup> order that the said shipp, come w<sup>th</sup> the first oportunitie to Suratt.

21 ITEM the Consent being arriued in Suratt, & yo<sup>r</sup> busines theare sett in good order, & the same left to the chardge of [p. 126] Anthonie Marlowe, and Pennell & ffynch[^sec-05-fn-074] w<sup>th</sup> such moneys as you thinke to be sufficient w<sup>th</sup> our m<sup>r</sup>chandize, to relade the Consent w<sup>th</sup> Indico, fine Callicoes, drugge &c: w<sup>th</sup> what Iewels you can gett, & leaueing them some small stocke for their mainetenance, being, to remayne theare as ffactors. Then you Willm Hawkins to retourne to the Hector, takeing w<sup>th</sup> you for ffactors Iohn Hearne, Clarke, and Batten, & w<sup>th</sup> speede to retourne w<sup>th</sup> the Monsoone to Aden, and there to follow the direccõn geuen you before, for that place. But yf att Aden, you be not kindlie intertayned & admitted to trade, then w<sup>th</sup> the next Convenient Wynde to shape yo<sup>r</sup> course for Bantam, where we referr you to Consider w<sup>th</sup> o<sup>r</sup> ffactors, whether the shipp shall lade theare w<sup>th</sup> pepp, or plie to some other place for lading, wherein we pray you slipp noe oportunitie for dispatch.

22 ITEM touching the Consent, yf she can be laden att Suratt as afore said, then w<sup>th</sup>all diligence, the m<sup>r</sup> to shape his course homewarde, w<sup>th</sup> such ffactor or ffactors as you m<sup>r</sup> Hawkins shall thinke ffitt.

23 BUT yf noe trade can be obtayned at Suratt for lading of the Consent then we wish, the m<sup>r</sup> to take his direct way alonge the Coaste of the Indies to Bantam w<sup>th</sup> the forenamed ffactors in her, & there to followe such direccõn for her ladinge homewarde, as o<sup>r</sup> ffactors att Bantam shall sett downe, either w<sup>th</sup> pepp theare, or to goe for Banda for Mace & Nutmegge.

> _[Margin: To lade the dragon wth Cloues (if not) wth Cloues, mace & nutmeges]_

24 ITEM further touchinge the Dragon, we wish you the Gen<sup>r</sup>all to vse all meanes & diligence to lade her w<sup>th</sup> Cloues att the *Molloccos*, or yf the whole ladinge of Cloues cannot be gotten, then retourne to Banda to furnish out the same, w<sup>th</sup> Nutmegge & Mace, wherein, as for all other spices we would haue you principallie to be advised by Symond Dickenson, who hath best skill [p. 127] therein, And to remember to foresee, that in ladeing either Cloues, Nutmegge or Mace, you clense them what you can from dust & Rumps that the shipp be not stuffed w<sup>th</sup> such vnpffitable ware as is not worth the Custome, & soe we loose all o<sup>r</sup> chardge, therefore rather burne the same then lade yt in the shipps & be carefull to buie drie Cloues, & not such as are greene.

25 ITEM be verie carefull that you haue yo<sup>r</sup> due weight & the same putt into bagge, nombred & m<sup>r</sup>ked & sent abourde the shipps w<sup>th</sup> some of the ffactors, or some other trustie pson, w<sup>th</sup> a łre Conteyneing the pticuler of eu<sup>r</sup>y bagg vnder the nomber, the same łre to be deliu<sup>r</sup>ed to the Pursar whom we chardge to weight eu<sup>r</sup>y bagg, att the takeinge of yt into the shipp, whereby he may see that the weight is accordinge to the łre rec<sup>d</sup>, keepeing eu<sup>r</sup>y łre & entring the Contente into his booke, whereby yf any erro<sup>r</sup> happen, yt may be found out, w<sup>ch</sup> we wish you the Generall to examine eu<sup>r</sup>y nighte. that there growe no abuse.

26 ITEM we chardge that the Pursar be continuallie abourde the shipp, and take true notice of all thinge whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> are brought into the shipp or carried out, either by Generall, Captaines, m<sup>r</sup>chaunte, m<sup>rs</sup>, Marriners the Pursar himselfe, or whosoeu<sup>r</sup>, the same to be entred into his booke, vnder the name of the owner, that eu<sup>r</sup>y one may haue his due att the retourne, as the Pursar will Aunsweare yt w<sup>th</sup> the losse of his wages. And we pray the Generall and Captaines to giue the Pursars strict order for pformaunce hereof.

27 ITEM that there be but one hatch open (yf yt may be) att the ladeing of any of the shipps, and all the other hatches lockt vpp, & that the m<sup>r</sup> or one of his mate & the Pursar to stand by the open hatches when any goode are shott into hould, lockeing the same vpp, when they haue left worke, the key to be geuen to the Generall or Captaine to be kepte.

28 ITEM to be carefull that nothinge be bought but what is especiall good, & that you doe not ou<sup>r</sup>wett the Cloues, when they be laden, fo<sup>r</sup> o<sup>r</sup> ouerwetting Cloues, bad Nutmegge & Mace haue tought vs to advise o<sup>r</sup> ffactors to be more carefull.

> _[Margin: noe priuate trade]_

29 AND for that voyage of this condi<span class="sc">c̃</span>on & greate chardge cannot admitt any private trade. Our will is, that neither you the Generall, nor any other, vpon any [p. 128] pticuler or other Accompt then the Gen<sup>r</sup>all & ioynt stocke doe lade or deale w<sup>th</sup> any of those·Comodities heerevnder expressed, viz pepp, Cloues, Nutmegge, Mace, Synamond, gynger Indico, Callicoes, Amber greece, Muske Alloes Beniamin & Gumlacca, And that yf any shall soe doe the same to be applied to the accompte of the Companie, as o<sup>r</sup> ppp goode, yt being noe way resonable, that we should paie them their wage w<sup>th</sup> meate & drinke, and they lade those thinge in o<sup>r</sup> shipps, w<sup>ch</sup> should defray o<sup>r</sup> chardge.

30 ITEM in eu<sup>r</sup>y place wheare you come & trade, compare their weighte and measures w<sup>th</sup> o<sup>rs</sup>, before you buie, to thend you may know the better what to doe, & how to make yo<sup>r</sup> rekoninge, for w<sup>ch</sup> purpose we haue putt sundrie Cheste w<sup>th</sup> weighte into o<sup>r</sup> shipps.

31 ITEM that there be the sufficientest & best advised of o<sup>r</sup> ffactor<sup>s</sup> appointed to weigh what is bought, by weight on the land, & to keepe a pfect booke thereof, that the same may be nightlie conferred w<sup>th</sup> the Pursars Booke, whereby error<sup>s</sup> may be the better found out.

32 ITEM that o<sup>r</sup> ffactor<sup>s</sup> bring or send by the first shipps 8 or 10 of the dollor<sup>s</sup>, or Royalls w<sup>ch</sup> the Hollenders carrie thither.

33 ITEM we vtterlie forbid any excessiue drinkeing, ffeasting, or banquetting abourd the shipps att Sea, or aland it being agreate waste & consumpcõn of victualls & wyne the Cause of many diseases & disorders in the Companie, & therefore the same to be spent w<sup>th</sup> more discrecõn & sparinge.

34 ITEM remember to matt the inside of yo<sup>r</sup> shipps before you putt any spice into them, espetiallie where you lade Cloues pepp Nutmegge & Mace, & be carefull to make choyse of yo<sup>r</sup> Nutmegge that they be lardge & sound, & att the ladeinge thereof, doe not lyme them too much,[^sec-05-fn-075] for that burne[th] them, & beware you lay the Mace in Canisters in some ffitt place by yt selfe, that yt be not spoyled by the heate<sub>•</sub> of the other spices, takeing good heede to buie that w<sup>ch</sup> is bright, & not withered, nor [p. 129] Redd nor darke browne Colored. And such Cloues as shall be free of dust the w<sup>ch</sup> those people vse to put amongest them for their advantage in the weight

35 <span class="sc">Item</span> yf necessitie drawe you att the lading of the Cloues for bett [er] setling of them, to cast water vpon them, be ye sure that ytt be but sprikling w<sup>th</sup> some thinge for the purpose like a watering pott, for that too much wett in o<sup>r</sup> Cloues in the last voyadge brought vs greate damadge.

> _[Margin: That affactorie be setled at Banda Tornata & tedore if you shall thincke fitt]_
> _[Margin: & to finde out such places where gold may be had & to what end.]_

36 <span class="sc">Item</span> we desire that a ffactorie may be settled for vs att Banda & an other at Turnato or Tedore the better to advise vs for trade heere after & therefore doe wish you to leaue ffacto<sup>rs</sup> att each place w<sup>th</sup> some reasonable stocke for their mayntenaunce, yf vpon due Consideracõn att yo<sup>r</sup> being theare you shall thinke yt ffitt. And seeing we finde by o<sup>r</sup> last Accompte, That those of Lunto<sup>r</sup> & Nero did sell their Cloues & mace much better cheepe; to receiue their paym<sup>te</sup> in gould, then in Royalls: namelie the Bahar of Nutmegge for 9 Royalls & the Bahar of Mace fo[r] 90 Royalls, in sylver: but paying w<sup>th</sup> gould the price of Nutmegge but 7 Royalls & of mace for 70, we therefore thinke yt verie needfull that all meanes be vsed to sell o<sup>r</sup> Comodities for barter or gould: & to fynde out such places where gould may be had, as spetiallie as we are informed att the Iland of Monaginnye[^sec-05-fn-076] for w<sup>ch</sup> place one of o<sup>r</sup> ffacto<sup>rs</sup> that shall lie att Banda, wee hould fittest to be ymployed to this effect: Although he goe att the first but as a passenger in some shipp, to learne & advise vs the certaintie thereof.

37 <span class="sc">Item</span> That the Gen<sup>r</sup>all & Captaines giue often notice to the ffacto<sup>rs</sup> & others what they are to obserue by this o<sup>r</sup> Comission w<sup>th</sup> espetiall chardge to the ffacto<sup>rs</sup>, to make diligent inquirie of what Comodities are to be bought or bartered for in each Iland, & what Englishe m<sup>r</sup>chandize may be there vented, & of what kinde & Collo<sup>rs</sup> most vendable.

> _[Margin: The ffactors at Bantam to procure the bringeing thither of Chenesey silkes.]_

38 <span class="sc">Ittem</span> It is to be remembred that o<sup>r</sup> ffacto<sup>rs</sup> att Bantam doe their best endevo<sup>rs</sup> to pcure the Chineses to bring from Cheney sleave & sowing silkes of the Coullo<sup>r</sup> & sizes we haue now deliu<sup>r</sup>ed to you o<sup>r</sup> [p. 130] Generall as alsoe some rawe silkes, that we may fall into some trade w<sup>th</sup> them, & see yf they can sell any of o<sup>r</sup> English Cloth to them, that they may be brought to thuse thereof.

39 ITEM remember to doe yo<sup>r</sup> best to bringe for the Lorde of Salisburie,[^sec-05-fn-077] some Parratte Mounckeys Marmesatte or other straundge beaste & fowles that you esteeme rare & delightfull.

40 ITEM for the quantities of money & m<sup>r</sup>chandize put into each shipp, we Referr you to o<sup>r</sup> invoice deliu<sup>r</sup>ed you herew<sup>th</sup> w<sup>th</sup> the pticuler sorte Coullors & prises, w<sup>th</sup> patternes of all sorte whereby to make sale.

> _[Margin: The appointem<sup>t</sup>: of the ffactors to be left there to be at the direccon of the Genrall.]_

41 ITEM whereas hearetofore the Company haue rec<sup>d</sup> greate wronge by the Gen<sup>r</sup>all & Captaines, m<sup>rs</sup>, & Marriners admittaunce of voluntarie men to goe in o<sup>r</sup> shipps: We hereby giue an espetiall chardge vnto you o<sup>r</sup> Generall Captaines & m<sup>rs</sup>, that you suffer none such to goe alonge w<sup>th</sup> you, w<sup>ch</sup> putt the Companie to chardge beside many other inconveniences, nor any but such as shall be allowed of by o<sup>r</sup> direction, & whose names are entred into o<sup>r</sup> bookes 42 AS touchinge the ffactors that are to be left there or to be brought home either of those w<sup>ch</sup> are alredie lefte in the Countrie, or of those w<sup>ch</sup> goe now in the shipps: We doe order that the appointem<sup>t</sup> of o<sup>r</sup> said ffactors to reside in those places shall be att the direction and discrecõn of you the Generall, or in yo<sup>r</sup> absence of him that shall be cheeffe Comaunder by vs appointed, wherein wee hope you will haue that Consideracõn, as to make choise of the ffittest w<sup>ch</sup> shall be found able & meete to deserue that truste of ymploym<sup>te</sup>: neither lett o<sup>r</sup> placeing of the ffactors in the seu<sup>r</sup>all shipps, as they are placed be a rule to you, or any ground to them, to [p. 131] enioye those places of ymploym<sup>te</sup> : other wyse then they shall be found ffitt & deserue. And that amonge such of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors as shall be now vsed att the Molloccos, Banda & those places Our Order is that you ymploy those now alreadie remayneing att Bantam aswell such as you thinke ffitt of as of anie others w<sup>th</sup> an espetiall chardg to them all, to carrie them selues verie kindlie w<sup>th</sup> those people, for that the Contrarie as we are informed hath beene hurtfull vnto vs, for that Brownes vnkinde & churlish dealeinge towardę them, did make many of those people refrayne to deale w<sup>th</sup> him & goe to the Hollenders.[^sec-05-fn-078]

> _[Margin: not to imparte the trade to any by[^sec-05-fn-079] the genrall Companie]_

43 ITEM that [as] it is vnfitt & inconvenient that o<sup>r</sup> trade be ympted vnto any but o<sup>r</sup> Gen<sup>r</sup>all Companie : it is expresslie ordered, & soe the ffactors are to haue chardge, not to write or advise any their pticuler freinde or others of the prices of any Comodities either theare bought or sold. But onelie in their Gen<sup>r</sup>all tres to the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie.

> _[Margin: yf the penasse be not left at Bantam to send some one or two of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors thence for diurs places to finde out trade]_

44 ITEM we wish that yf att yo<sup>r</sup> comeing to Bantam, it be not thought ffitt that the Pinnasse be theare left to traffique from place to place as we doe desire. Then o<sup>r</sup> will is that some one or twoe of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors left theare shall by the best meanes they cann there finde, goe as passengers in some other shipps, to finde out trade in such places as shall be thought needfull as Mesapatania[^sec-05-fn-080] in the partes of Bengalla Cheremandall S<sup>t</sup> Thome or any other places fitt for trade, & to take good observac̃on what English Comodities, as Iron, Tynn, Leade, steele Clothes kersies and Saies w<sup>th</sup> their seu<sup>r</sup>all kinde & Coullo<sup>rs</sup> are there best in request, & their value: As alsoe what Comodities are theare to be bought, as namely Pyntados, & such like, for the *Molloccos* And likewyse booke Callicutte & lanes called casa, & such other thinge as may serve for England where the finest sorte will serve best, w<sup>th</sup> Pearles, stones, Muske Bezar, & such like, w<sup>th</sup> their seu<sup>r</sup>all prices, wherein we wishe Pennell to be cheeflie ymployed, for Callicutte lanes &c : & other ffactors according to their skill in other Comodities, The Omission of seekeinge out whereof all this while hath [p. 132] retourned to o<sup>r</sup> greate losse, & to the benefitt of the Hollenders, who haue beene laborious and industrious therein : And this sending to those places, & inquirie to be made, yf yt be possible before the retourne of the dragon from the Molloccos to Bantam, to thend that att her retourne for England we may be effectuallie adverticed of all theis pticulars soe farr as you may, & of all other thinges for o<sup>r</sup> better direccõns of anew voyadge.

> _[Margin: To bringe an Inventurie from Bantam &c of all thinges there left.]_

45 ITEM that you the Generall att yo<sup>r</sup> retourne for[^sec-05-fn-081] Bantam for England, doe bringe w<sup>th</sup> you vnto vs from thence an Inventory of all o<sup>r</sup> goode, debte & moneys then remayneing in those pte, The w<sup>ch</sup> is likewyse to be done by m<sup>r</sup> Hawkins yf he shall leaue any ffactorie els wheare putting to o<sup>r</sup> Gen<sup>r</sup>all accompt all guifte presente and gratificačõns, w<sup>ch</sup> shall be geven, by any forreine Prince or potentate, vnto whom we haue now sent presente or others.

46 ITEM it is o<sup>r</sup> expresse order, that by a gen<sup>r</sup>all Consent of yo<sup>u</sup> the Generall Captaines, ffacto<sup>rs</sup>, m<sup>rs</sup>, & Marriners, some good order be by you taken & sett downe in writeing soe soone as you come to Sea, Concerning the disposeing of dead mens goode in the voyadge, by sale att the Maste, or otherwyse : for buiing sellinge borrowing & lending one an other : And orderinge what sallarie shall be allowed the Pursar vpon eu<sup>r</sup>y pounde for keepeing accompt thereof, to avoied Controu<sup>r</sup>sie, & question hereafter, & eu<sup>r</sup>y marriner & other of each shipp, to sett their hand or marke vnto the same Order. But yf any ffacto<sup>r</sup> shall happen to die, his goode, bookes, accompte and other thinge, are to be by order of the Generall & Captaines saffelie reserved, & brought home for England.

> _[Margin: Any thinge formerlie sett downe,[^sec-05-fn-082] all thinges left to their discreccons.]_

47 ITEM now lastlie but w<sup>th</sup> the first to be remembred we Comend vnto you all an especiall care to haue yo<sup>r</sup> Eyes open to all devises & practises w<sup>ch</sup> may be wrought agaynst you, o<sup>r</sup> shipps & goode in eu<sup>r</sup>y place where you come, keeping a Continuall watch, whereby you may be readie to prevent any mischeefe agaynst you, suspect all, how freindlie soeu<sup>r</sup> they seeme : be readie still & stand vpon yo<sup>r</sup> guarde, trust not yo<sup>r</sup> saffetie to [p. 133] the Carelesse attendaunce of the Comon marriners, whoe will not losse their present pleasures, or ease, though the losse of their liues, o<sup>r</sup> shipps & goode depend vpon yt. And albeyt we haue sett downe eu<sup>r</sup>y thinge what we remember and desier to be desire to be done : in pticuler : Yett yf vpon due considerac̃on you finde cause to alter any thinge, w<sup>ch</sup> we heare haue sett downe, haueing w<sup>th</sup> good aduise resolued therevpon, we referr the same to yo<sup>r</sup> discrec̃ons : And for yo<sup>r</sup> better &[^sec-05-fn-083] Assistaunce & warie pceedinge therein, as alsoe in all other o<sup>r</sup> affaires we appointe Willm Hawkins David Middleton & Anthony Marlow, & such others as you the principall Comaunder shall thinke ffitt to Consider and Consult w<sup>th</sup> you the Gen<sup>r</sup>all of all thinge needfull whome wee wish you to ymbrace & vse w<sup>th</sup> aloueinge respect, & freindlie and diligentlie to hearken to their Councells, puttinge in execution what shall w<sup>th</sup> good deliberation be soe agreed vpon. And soe we we Comend you & yo<sup>r</sup> endevo<sup>rs</sup> to gode pvidence whoe guide you w<sup>th</sup> his feare & defend yo<sup>u</sup> from all daungers. Amen.


#### *post scriptum*

48 AND furder o<sup>r</sup> direcc̃on is That you our Gen<sup>r</sup>all at yo<sup>r</sup> comeinge to Bantam doe (beside the łre & p<sup>r</sup>sent to that kinge) giue vnto the Admirall & such other greate psonages theare as o<sup>r</sup> ffacto<sup>rs</sup> shall advise you to haue beene freindlie to them, such presente or gratificac̃ons as shall be thought ffitt.

> _[Margin: That fewer of o<sup>r</sup> people be kept ther.]_

49 AND further we wishe that some good course be taken att your comeing thither, that fewer of o<sup>r</sup> people be kept theare, for ease of chardge : yett not whollie to be w<sup>th</sup>drawen thence.

> _[Margin: A ffactorie at Priamon]_

50 AND alsoe we wish that a ffactorie, or att least some of o<sup>r</sup> people be appointed to recyde att Pryamon, both for their better health & saffetie,[^sec-05-fn-084] & for pcureing for vs pepp & other Comodities yf there shall be men & stocke there to ymploie.


<!-- page: 226 | folio: 134 -->
51 ITEM o<sup>r</sup> direccõn is that att yo<sup>r</sup> retourne from Bantam you doe bringe thence for the Companie some small quantitie of the East India Tynn for the triall & proofe thereof.

52 ITEM for better p<sup>r</sup>servacõn of health, o<sup>r</sup> order is, that from tyme to tyme as the water Caske shall be emptied of fresh water [they] be forth w<sup>th</sup> agayne filled w<sup>th</sup> salt water, for prevencõn of leakeinge and Mustines.

53 ITEM o<sup>r</sup> direction is that you make diligent inquirie att S<sup>t</sup> Lawrence and Zanzabar, & all other places, in yo<sup>r</sup> passadge & retourne of Tydinge of the Suzan :[^sec-05-fn-085] or yf any English shipp hath beene of late w<sup>th</sup>in theis twoe yeares either cast away or taken : or putt in for releefe, in any of those pte, and receiueing any knowledge of her to vse the best meanes you may, for recou<sup>r</sup>y of her her men & goode.

54 ITEM the ffacte Comitted in the Indies by S<sup>r</sup> Edward Michelborne[^sec-05-fn-086] thoughe we know o<sup>r</sup> selues to be [p. 135] meerelie[^sec-05-fn-087] Innocent therein, yet yf by any meanes we or o<sup>r</sup> goode should be dampnified thereby, we wish you to seeke to that kinge & magistrate for redresse & recompence thereof. The w<sup>ch</sup> yf you cannot obtayne. Then o<sup>r</sup> will is, that you vse the benefitt of o<sup>r</sup> kinge ma<sup>ties</sup> Comission giuen you in that behalfe.

55 ITEM after the depture of the said Willm Kealeinge & Willm Hawkins to diuers Coastes, as we haue by this o<sup>r</sup> Comission ordered, yf the said Willm Hawkins shall happen to die, w<sup>ch</sup> God forbidd. Then we doe appointe in his place for ordering & effecting the busines by vs hereby Comitted vnto the said Willm Hawkins chardge vnto Anthony Marlowe : but neu<sup>r</sup>thelesse yf the said Willm Hawkins shall happen to die before he shall depte Companie w<sup>th</sup> the said m<sup>r</sup> Willm Kealinge for diuers places as aforesaid then o<sup>r</sup> expresse will is That David Middleton be appointed in the place of the said Willm Hawkins of Leiuetenaunte Generall in this present voyadge before any other. As alsoe by the death of the said m<sup>r</sup> Willm Kealeing now o<sup>r</sup> Generall to succeede in his place & chardge in the absence of the said Willm Hawkins by death or otherwyse till their meetinge together agayne in this voyadge.


<!-- page: 228 | folio: 136 -->
> _[Margin: ffor examinacon of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors there.]_

56 ITEM we giue you o<sup>r</sup> Gen<sup>r</sup>all expresse order for examinac̃on of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors dealeing att Bantam in o<sup>r</sup> gen<sup>r</sup>all accompt & other wayes, & alsoe of all their private trade, vsed since their going thither : Wherein we vnderstand m<sup>r</sup> Towerson hath beene a lardge dealer for him selfe, haueing sould to the Hollenders att one tyme 300 sackes of pepp̃ beside other thinge very straunge vnto us. And yf vpon due examinãcõn thereof he doe not giue you good satisfacc̃on to yo<sup>r</sup> content, then we praye you to reduce the same to the Comon stocke & the like Course to be taken herein w<sup>th</sup> all such others, that you shall finde faultie heerein for that the same is Contrarie to o<sup>r</sup> expresse order formerlie geuen vnto them.

57\. AND for that we finde best p̃ffitt by the lardg sorte of pepp̃ both for the prices that you paye aswell for the one as for the other, we pray you att any hand, to buye soe much of the largest sorte, as by any meanes you cann gett, & lett the same be put by yt selfe into the shipp that yt be nott mingled w<sup>th</sup> any other. And thus not doubting of yo<sup>r</sup> faithfull care & diligence herein Wee pray god to blesse you all & o<sup>r</sup> affaires London the 11<sup>th</sup> of March 1606.

W<sup>m</sup> Kealeing[^sec-05-fn-088] W<sup>m</sup> Hawkins David Middleton.


![Ornate initial letter F](../figures/fig-011_p0228.webp)

> _[Margin: S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancasters remembraunce for obseruacon of the tymes meete to be obserued in the East India voyadge.]_

FIRSTE[^sec-05-fn-089] yf yt please God to send yo<sup>r</sup> shipps to the Cape Bona *Speranza* in time, that is by the first of Iune little more or lesse, & yo<sup>r</sup> people standing in health, myne opinion is that you stay not att Saldania to water or refresh, but rather hould on your Course directlie for S<sup>t</sup> Lawrence & touch att the ryver of S<sup>t</sup> Augustine, for theare as I haue beene crediblie informed is as good meanes of refreshing as is att Saldania This Course will advantage you much in yo<sup>r</sup> [p. 137] Navigac̃on to the Coaste of the India : beside the avoydeinge of fowle whether, that in that monneth comonlie is in Saldania, haueing theare refreshed haue agreate care of the fflatte of the Ilande of Iudea[^sec-05-fn-090] for many shipps haue been lost theare, for the Currant setteth from the Coaste of S<sup>t</sup> Lawrence right vpon them, soe that yf you be not very carefull to looke out night & daye you shall feele them before you see them. Therefore haue a diligent care of this pointe for I my selfe haueing twoe very sufficient m<sup>rs</sup> in my shipp was by the said Currant much deceiued, but that was in the monneth of September.

<span class="sc">If</span> by any misfortune you haue further neede of refreshing, you shall finde yt att the Ilande of Comoza[^sec-05-fn-091] but looke to yo<sup>r</sup> selues, for after their tournes are served of such thinge as they need they will imploye all their witte to betray you in what they Cann, therefore trust noe men aland for the ffleminge haue lost men trice in theis Ilaunde & I my selfe once.[^sec-05-fn-092] If the tyme soe serue you that yo<sup>u</sup> cann gett into Indea by the 5<sup>th</sup> of Iulie, you may as you see cause, first touche in the mouth of the Redd Sea, for although you make yo<sup>r</sup> staye there till the middest of October yett you shall haue wynde to bring you to Indea but not longe after : but yf yt soe fall out that you see yt will be the midst of August or theareaboutes ere you shall gett into the Redd Sea, then I would take my Course directlie for Cambaia & follow my busines there, for by the 20<sup>th</sup> of Decemb̃ or prime of Ianuarie att the ffurthest yf yo<sup>u</sup> settle not yo<sup>r</sup> trade theare, the Wynde growe fayre to goe for the Redd Sea, whither at that tyme yf you take yo<sup>r</sup> Course you shall haue 3 monnethes to staye, to see what you cann doe in setlinge yo<sup>r</sup> trades. And aboute Aprill the West & [p. 138] Norwest wynde begynning to blowe, soe that you may retourne agayne for the Coaste of Indea, but thinke not to touch vpon the Coaste for yt is exceeding daungerous at that tyme of the yeare, & from thence till August, & therefore come not neare yt, for till august yt is fowle weather, & verie thicke & stormye vpon the Coaste of Indea, & the wynde sett right vpon the Coaste, May, Iune & Iulie, but theis wynde will carrie you to Bantam, but take not too high or Sowtherlie a course for then you will hem [out] of the way of the Westerne Monsond that should helpe you in this Navigation, but comeing to Bantam before September you cannot goe for the Molloccos for the Westerne Monsonde reacheth but to Bantam. Therefore as you see cause you may touch att Pryamon where is good pepp reasonable good cheepe & agood ayre. Note that yf you touch not vpon the Coaste of Indea before the 5<sup>th</sup> of November, you cannot doe yt till august or September come twelue monneth.

> _[Margin: Bills of aduenture to the factors. Se for the mr<sup>s</sup> fo 99.[^sec-05-fn-094]]_

<span class="sc">Whereas</span>[^sec-05-fn-093] **A B.** is enterteyned by vs the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chan[te] of London trading to the East Indies to goe as one of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors in this p<sup>r</sup>sent voyadge now by vs p<sup>r</sup>pared towarde the said Indies, & is allowed for his ymploym<sup>t</sup> in the said voyadge the some of for his p<sup>r</sup>parac̃on to Sea the w<sup>ch</sup> he hath received before his goeing forth. Now knowe yee that we the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie for the further allowance w<sup>ch</sup> the said **A B** is to haue & receiue accordinge to o<sup>r</sup> agreem<sup>t</sup> w<sup>th</sup> him doe acknowledge & testifie & doe pmyse & agree by theis presente that the said **A B.** shall haue & inioy for his further allowance & enterteynm<sup>t</sup> in the said voyadge vpon the gaine & pffitt w<sup>ch</sup> god shall send by the retourne of the same [p. 139] voyadge, The principall adventure thereof & all chardge of the voyadge first deducted, such rate & pportion of proffitt as yf he had beene an adventuro<sup>r</sup> of the some of              li and as yf he had putt in soe much Readie money in stocke in the said voyadge, the said rate & pporticõn of proffitt to be paied vnto him after his retourne into England in such manner & forme as the gaine & proffitt of the said voyadge is paied to other the Aduenturo<sup>rs</sup> gen<sup>r</sup>allie vppon the some of              li by them adventured soe as he pceede in the said voyadge, & doe not retourne before the voyadge be ended. And yf he happen to die before the retourne of the shipps from the said East Indies haueing liued & Continued in the said voyadge vntill the shipps shall be laden, or vntill he or other ffacto<sup>rs</sup> shall haue contracted & made pvision for their ladinge then the said gaine proportioned the saide rate of li adventure to be paied to his Executo<sup>rs</sup> administrato<sup>rs</sup> or assignes, as yt should haue beene paied to him, yf he had retourned w<sup>th</sup> the shipps. Provided alwaies that yf he deceease before the shipps shall arrive in the East Indies that then the moneys ymprested & deliu<sup>r</sup>ed him before his goinge to Sea shall be vnto him in full recompence of his interteynem<sup>t</sup> agreed vpon for the voyadge And vpon theis Condicõns & provisoes before mentioned We the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie vnder o<sup>r</sup> Comon seale haue geven vnto the said **A B** this present bill of Contract & adventure dated the 17<sup>th</sup> day of ffebruarie Anno Regni Rñe Eliz quadragesimo tertio.

> _[Margin: A bill of aduenture to the Company.]_

<span class="sc">Whereas</span> **A B** one of the Adventurers & one of the brethren of the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunt*e* of London trading into the East Indies haueing sett downe for his Adventure w<sup>th</sup> the said Company for their first voyadge into the East Indies the some of              li starlinge hath not onelie paied the said some of li to **C D** Thr̃er of the said Company, but hath supplied accordinge to the Ordenances of the Company the [p. 140] some of          łti starlinge more w<sup>ch</sup> is after the rate of ij<sup>s</sup> the łt of his said Adventure. Wee therefore the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company doe by this o<sup>r</sup> present bill of Adventure promyse & agree to & w<sup>th</sup> the said 𝔄 𝔅. That wee the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie & o<sup>r</sup> successo<sup>rs</sup> shall & will vpon the retourne of the shipps or any of them sett out by vs in this present voyadge, or w<sup>th</sup>in Convenient tyme after their said retourne in the same deliuer vnto the said 𝔄 𝔅 his executo<sup>rs</sup> & admīstrā a true & iust accompt & paym<sup>te</sup> of such stocke, benefitt & proffitt of stocke as god shall send vpon the said voyadge according to the gen<sup>r</sup>all distribution proporc̃on & allotm<sup>t</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall be allotted disposed and geven to all & eu<sup>r</sup>y the seu<sup>r</sup>all Adventuro<sup>rs</sup> in the said voyage p̄portionall to their seu<sup>r</sup>all adventures. In Witnes wheareof the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie haue heareto annexed their Comon seale The 17<sup>th</sup> daie of ffebruarie 1600.

> _[Margin: The factors bonde. bounde in 1000 m<sup>r</sup>kes]_
> _[Margin: And furder if the said A B do not at any tyme or tymes duringe his Contynuance in the seruice of the said Companie send any priuate or other lres from the said East Indies but that the same be inclosed in the publick lres to the Companie.  This ordered the 5 of Aprill 1608 [^sec-05-fn-097]]_
> _[Margin: The suierties Bonndes bounde in 200li.]_

THE CONDICON[^sec-05-fn-095] of this Obligac̃on is such That wheareas vpon the spetiall request and intreatie of the aboue bound 𝔄 𝔅. the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of the marchauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies haue interteyned him the said 𝔄 𝔅. into their service. And alsoe the said 𝔄 𝔅 hath agreed & pmysed to serue the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie & their successo<sup>rs</sup> as their ffacto<sup>r</sup> & Couenaunt servant in all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such their traffique of m<sup>r</sup>chandize busynes & affaires whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> as they or any by them authorized shall thinke ffitt to ymploy him in, as well att, in, vnto, & from the East Indies, as att or in any other place or places whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> dureing the space of 5 yeares next ensueing the date aboue written, or dureing soe many & such tyme of the said ffiue yeares as the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie or their successo<sup>rs</sup> or such as shall be by them [p. 141] authorized shall thinke meete for such wage & Considerac̃on as alredie is agreed vpon betweene the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie & him the said **A B**. And w<sup>ch</sup> is specified & sett downe in the Courte booke of the said Companie. If therefore the said **A B** doe henceforth during all the said terme of 5 yeares, or soe longe tyme thereof as the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie, or their Successo<sup>rs</sup> shall reteyne him in their service well trulie & honestlie serue the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie their successo<sup>rs</sup> & assignes as their ffactor in all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such affaires & busines whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> as they or such as shall be by them authorized shall thinke good to ymploy him. And doe from tyme to tyme dureing all the tyme of his service diligentlie ymploye & endevo<sup>r</sup> himselfe to the vttermost of his power knowledge and skill and to the best pffitt he can devise for the vse and behoofe of the said Companie in & aboute the mannâgeing excerciseing pformaunce & execution of all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such traffique busines matters affaires & thinge whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> as by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie or by their assignes aucthorized for the tyme being he shall be directed or appointed to deale in, pforme and doe. And alsoe yf the said **A B**. doe from tyme to tyme & att all tymes to the vttermost of his power strength and skill not onelie resist & w<sup>th</sup>stand all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such pson and psons as shall attempt or practise any matter or thinge whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> to the hindraunce hurte or damadge of the said Companie, or of their goode m<sup>r</sup>chandize trade or any of them or any parte thereof: but alsoe p<sup>r</sup>vent and defeate all & euery such practizes attempte & acc̃ons whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall or may tend to the damadge defraudinge or p<sup>r</sup>iudice of the said Companie or of their goode or traffique or any pte thereof in any wyse. And ffurder yf the said **A B** doe from tyme to tyme giue true notice & intelligence by the spediest meanes he possiblie Cann vnto the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Comitties for the tyme being or to such as shall be by them authorized, or some of them, of all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such deceipte wronges abuses & hindrances as he shall knowe or vnderstand, or crediblie heare to be att any tyme or tymes practized done or offered agaynst the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company or their goode or trade, or any of them, by any pson or psons in any place or places, together w<sup>th</sup> the names of those psons by whom the same shall be soe offered practised or ppetrated. And alsoe yf the said **A B**, [p. 142] doe from tyme to tyme w<sup>th</sup>in 14 daies next after eu<sup>r</sup>y resonable request to him to be made by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Comitties for the tyme being or by any by them in that behalfe to be aucthorized not onelie make yeald & giue to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>rs</sup> & Comitties for the tyme being or to such of their Officers or mynisters as in this behalfe shall be authorized or appointed a true iust & p̃fect Accompte in writeinge of all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such money goode m<sup>r</sup>chaundize & other thinge whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>, as before the makeing of the same Accompt shall haue come to the hande chardge or possession of him the said **A B.** or shall haue beene Consigned vnto him for the vse or behoofe of the said Companie, and of the disposeing factorage and ymploym<sup>t</sup> of all the same money goode m<sup>r</sup>chandize and other thinge whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> & euery pte thereof, But doe alsoe vpon the makeing of the same Accompt, or w<sup>th</sup>in sixe daies then next ensueinge well & truelie deliu<sup>r</sup> & paie vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Comitties for the tyme beinge, or their Officers or mynisters in that behalfe to be appointed, or to some of them. All & eu<sup>r</sup>y such money iewells pearles p<sup>r</sup>cious stones Bezar stones muske & muske Codde sivit amber greece, goode wares & m<sup>r</sup>chandize whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> as by the ffootte of the same Accompte shall appeare to be & remayne in his hande or possession and for w<sup>ch</sup> he ought to be chardgable or aunswearable in any manner of wyse. And furthermore yf the said **A. B.** doe not att any tyme heereafter dureing the tyme of his service aforesaid directlie or indirectlie by himselfe or by any other deale in vse or practise any buieing selling trading or m<sup>r</sup>chandizeinge for the vse or benefitt of him selfe or of any other parson or p̃sons whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> (except what is now ordered lymitted & allowed him by the said Companie as by their Register appeth[^sec-05-fn-096][]) : but onelie [p. 143] to & for the sole & pper vse & benefitt of the Companie aforesaid and their Assignes. And alsoe yf the said **A. B.** doe from tyme to tyme w<sup>th</sup> as much speede as possiblie he cann geue intelligence & notice to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Comitties for the tyme being aswell of all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such pson & psons, whoe being now or att any tyme hereafter shall be ymployed in the service & affaires of the said Companie, doe or shall vse exercyse or practise any secret or private tradinge buieing selling or m<sup>r</sup>chandizeing in any place or places whereby the said Companie shall or may susteyne or incurr any hindraunce or damadge, as alsoe of eu<sup>r</sup>y pticuler of the same private tradinge & dealeing accordinge to his best knowledge & vnderstandinge. **^** And alsoe yf the said **A B.** at all tymes dureing the tyme of his service aforesaid doe gentlelie, faithfullie & diligentlie vse behaue & demeasne him selfe as a good & dutifull servant towarde the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Comitties & those by them aucthorized. That then this present obliga<span class="sc">c</span>õn &c : <span class="sc">the condicon</span>[^sec-05-fn-098] of this obliga<span class="sc">c</span>õn is such That wheareas att the spetiall request and intreatie of **J. D.** the sonne of the aboue bound **R D.** the aboue named Companie of the East India m<sup>r</sup>chaunte [p. 144] haue now hired him the said **I. D.** for one of the third sorte of their ffactor<sup>rs</sup> who by obligãcõn of the date aboue written is entred & become bound vnto the aboue named S<sup>r</sup> Will̃m Romeny[^sec-05-fn-099] & Thomas ffarrington[^sec-05-fn-100] for thuse of the said Company in the some & penaltie of 1000<sup>mrkę</sup> w<sup>th</sup> Condic̃on therevnto for his faithfull service to the said Company & p̃formance of sundrie other Condic̃ons & thingę in the same Condition expressed as thereby att lardge appeth. Now therefore in Case any breach or breaches shall hereafter happen to be made of the Condic̃on of the said obligãcõn wherein the said **I. D.** standeth bound as is aforesaid, or yf any clause article condic̃on matter or thinge, in the Condic̃on of the same obligãcõn expressed specified or conteyned, or of any p̃te or p̃cell thereof Then yf the said **R. D.** & **I. P.** or either of them their or either of their[^sec-05-fn-101] heires Executor<sup>rs</sup> or Administrator<sup>rs</sup> doe & shall from tyme to tyme w<sup>th</sup>in 14 daies next after notice in writeinge, to them or any of them in that behalfe geven by the said S<sup>r</sup> Will̃m Romeny & Thomas ffarrington or either of them, their or either of their Executors admĩstrato<sup>rs</sup> or asss or by the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or Thr̄er of the said Societie for the ty:ne being or by any other being substituted or aucthorized in that behalfe by the said Societie or Companie well and trulie aunsweare satisfie & paie, or cause to be aunswered satisfied & paied vnto the said S<sup>r</sup> Will̃m Romeny & Thomas ffarrington or either of them, or to the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Thr̄er of the said Societie for the tyme beinge to thuse of the said Societie the ffull some and value of good & lawfull money of England That all & eu<sup>r</sup>y damadge losse & hindraunce whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall aryse or growe or be susteyned or incurred by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> Thr̄er and Societie of the m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London [p. 145] trading to the East Indies or their successo<sup>rs</sup>, or by any of them by reason of any breach or breaches happening of the Condicõn of the said obligation wherein the foresaid **J. D.** standeth bound, or yf any clause article condicõn matter or thinge therein mencioned expressed or Conteyned shall amounte vnto, & whereof & for w<sup>ch</sup> he the saied Iohn Dorchester shall not then formerlie haue made fitt and sufficient recompense and satisfaccõn to the saied Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> Thrēr and Societie or their successo<sup>rs</sup> w<sup>th</sup>out fraude or further delaie. That then &c:
