> _[Margin: the first Committies for the direccon of the affaires of the Company being xxiiij in Nomber]_
> _[Margin: A deptie to the Gournor to take an Oath before 5 or more of the Comitties]_

<span class="sc">And</span> further we will and by theis presente for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> we doe ordeine that there shall be from henceforth one of the same Companie elected and appointed in such forme as heereafter in theis presente is expressed w<sup>ch</sup> shall be called the Gou<sup>r</sup>nor of the said Company, and that there shall be from hencforth Twenty ffower of the said Companie elected & appointed in such forme as heereafter in theis presente is expressed, w<sup>ch</sup> shalbe called the Comitties of the said Company[^sec-06-fn-040] for the tyme beinge shall haue the direccon of the voyage of or for the said Company and the ꝑvision of the shippinge and m<sup>r</sup>chaundizes thereto belongeinge, and alsoe the [p. 169] sale of all m<sup>r</sup>chaundizes retourned in the voyage, of or for the said Companie, and the manageing and handling of all other thinge belongeing to the said Company, and for the better execution of this o<sup>r</sup> will and graunte in this behalfe, We haue assigned, nominated, constituted and made, & by theis presente for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and sucessor<sup>rs</sup> we doe assigne nominate constitute and make the said Thomas Smyth Ald: of London to be the first & present Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company to continue in the said office from the date of theis presente vntill an other of the said Companie shall in due manner be chosen and sworne vnto the said Office accordinge to the ordenances and pvision heereafter in theis presente expressed and declared yf the said Thomas Smyth shall soe longe lyue, And alsoe we haue assigned nominated and appointed and by theis presente for vs & o<sup>r</sup> heires and successor<sup>rs</sup>. Wee doe assigne nominate constitute & make the said Paule Bannynge Leonard Holliday, Iohn Moore, Edward Holmeden, Richard Stap Thomas Cordell, Willm Garway, Olyuer Style, Iames Lancaster,[^sec-06-fn-041] Richard Wyseman, ffrancis Chery, Thomas Allabaster, Willm Romeny, Roger Howe, Willm Chambers, Robt Sandy, Iohn Eldred, Richard Witche, Iohn Highlord, Iohn Middleton, Iohn Combe, Willm Harrison, Nichis Lynge, and Robt Bell to be the Twentie ffower first and present Comitties of the said Company to Continue in the said Office of Comitties of the said Company from the date of theis presente for one wholle yeare next ffollowing AND furder we will and graunte by theis presente for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successor<sup>rs</sup> vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies and their successor<sup>rs</sup> that yt shall and may be lawfull to and for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Comp : for the tyme beinge or the more parte of them present at any publick assembly Comonly called the Courte houlden for the said Company, The Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company being alwaies one from tyme to tyme, to elect nominate & appointe one of the said Company to be Deputie to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> Deputie shall take a corporall Oath before the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and ffyue or more of the Comitties of the said Companie for the tyme being [p. 170] well faithfullie and trulie to execute his said Office of Deputie to the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company, and after his Oath soe taken shall & may from tyme to tyme in the Absence of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> exercyse and execute the Office of Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company in such sorte as the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> ought to doe.

> _[Margin: The first day of Julie or w<sup>th</sup>in 6 daies after the yearelie eleccon of the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup>.]_
> _[Margin: eu<sup>r</sup>y brother to take a corporall oath]_

<span class="sc">And</span> further we will & graunte by theis presente for vs our heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies & their successo<sup>rs</sup>, that they or the greater pte of them, whereof the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> for the tyme being or his Deputie to be one from tyme to tyme & at altymes heereafter shall and may haue aucthoritie and power yearelie & eu<sup>r</sup>y yeare on the first day of Iulie, or at any tyme w<sup>th</sup>in 6 daies after that day to assemble and meete together in some Convenient place to be appointed from tyme to tyme by the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or in his absence by the Deputie of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> for the tyme being. And that they being soe assembled yt shall & may be lawfull to and for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or Deputie of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and the said Comp : for the tyme beinge or the greater pte of them, w<sup>ch</sup> then shall happen to be present whereof the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the saide Companie to be one,[^sec-06-fn-042] or his deputie for the tyme being, to elect and nominate one of the said Companie, w<sup>ch</sup> shall be Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company for one wholle yeare from thence next followinge : w<sup>ch</sup> pson being soe elected and nominated to be Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of y<sup>e</sup> said Comp : as is aforesaid before he be admitted to the execucon of the said Office shall take a corporall Oath before the last Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> being his predicesso<sup>r</sup>, or his deputie, & any sixe or more of the Comitties of the said Company for the tyme beinge, that he shall from tyme to tyme well and trulie execute the Office of Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company in all thinge concerninge the same, & that imediatelie after the Oath soe taken he shall and may execute and vse the said Office of Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Companie for one whole yeare from thence next ffollowinge, And in like manner[^sec-06-fn-043] we will and graunte that aswell eu<sup>r</sup>y one aboue named to be of the said Companie, or ffellowshippe as al others heereafter to be admitted, [p. 171] or free of the said Companie shall take a corporall oath before the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of this said Company or his Deputie for the tyme being being to such effect as by the said[^sec-06-fn-044] Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Comp: or more pte of them In any publicke Courte to be held for the said Company shall be in reasonable manner sett downe & devised before they shall be allowed or admitted to trade or traffique as a ffreeman of the said Company.

> _[Margin: xxiiij Comitties to be yearelie elected on the first of Julie or w<sup>t</sup>hin 6 daies ffollowinge.]_
> _[Margin: The Comitties shall take a corporall Oath.]_
> _[Margin: yf the Gou<sup>r</sup>nor die, or be remoued a new to be chosen]_

AND further we will & graunte by theis presentę for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London trading into the East Indies & their successo<sup>rs</sup> that the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup>, or the Deputie of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and the Comp: and their successo<sup>rs</sup> for the tyme beinge or the greater parte of them whereof the gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or the Deputie of the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> from tyme to tyme to be one, shall & may from tyme to tyme and att altymes heereafter haue authoritie and power yearelie & eu<sup>r</sup>y yeare on the first day of Iuly, or att any tyme w<sup>t</sup>hin sixe daies after that day to assemble & meete together in some convenient place to be from tyme to tyme appointed by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company, or in his absence by his Deputie And that they being soe assembled yt shall &may be lawfull to & for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or his Deputie & the Company for the tyme being, or the greater pte of them w<sup>ch</sup> then shall happen to be p<sup>r</sup>sent whereof the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Companie or his Deputie for the tyme being to be one to elect & nominate Twentie ffower of the said Comp: w<sup>ch</sup> shall be Comitties of the said Company for one whole yeare from thence next ensueinge, w<sup>ch</sup> psons being soe elected & nominated to be Comitties of the said Companie as aforesaid before they be admitted to the execuc̃on of their said Offices shall take a Corporall Oath before the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or his Deputie & any 6 or more of the said Comitties of the said Company being their last predicesso<sup>rs</sup> for the tyme beinge that they & eu<sup>r</sup>y of them shall well & faithfullie pforme their said Office of Comitties in all thingę concerning the same. And that ymediatelie after the[^sec-06-fn-045] Oath soe [p. 172] taken they shall & may execute and vse their said Offices of Comitties of the said Companie for one whole yeare from thence next ensueinge.[^sec-06-fn-046] And moreou<sup>r</sup> o<sup>r</sup> will & pleauer is and by theis presentę for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> we doe graunt vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies, & to their successo<sup>rs</sup> that when and as often as yt shall happen the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company for the tyme beinge att any tyme w<sup>th</sup>in one yeare after that he shall be nominated elected & sworne to the Office of the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Companie as is aforesaid to die or to be remoued from the said Office, w<sup>ch</sup> Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> not demeaning he him selfe well in his said Office, we will to be remoueable att the pleasure of the said Company, or the greater pte of them, w<sup>ch</sup> shall be present at any their publike Assemblies, comonly called their[^sec-06-fn-047] gen<sup>r</sup>all Courte houlden for the said Company. That then & soe often yt shall & may be lawfull to & for the residue of the said Company for the tyme being, or the greater pte of them, w<sup>th</sup>in convenient tyme after the death or remoueing any such Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> to assemble themselues in such convenient place as they shall thinke ffitt, for the eleccon of the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Companie, and that the said Company, or the greater parte of them being then and there present shall and may then & theare before their depture from the said place elect & nominate one other of the said Companie to be Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company in the place or steede of him that soe died or was soe remoued w<sup>ch</sup> pson beinge soe elected & nominated to the office of Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company shall haue and exercise the said office for & during the residue of the said yeare takeing first a corporall Oath as is aforesaid for the due execucõn thereof, and this to be done from tyme to tyme soe often as the case shall soe requier.

> _[Margin: If any of the Comitties die or be remoued a new to be chosen]_

<span class="sc">And</span> alsoe o<sup>r</sup> will and pleasure is and by theis presentę for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> we doe graunte vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London trading into the East Indies and to their successo<sup>rs</sup> that when and as often as yt shall happen any of the [p. 173] said[^sec-06-fn-048] Comitties of the said Company for the tyme being at any time w<sup>th</sup>in one yeare next after that they or any of them shalbe nomynated[^sec-06-fn-049] & sworne to the Office of Comitties of the said Company (as is aforesaid) to die or be remoued from the said office, w<sup>ch</sup> Comitties not demeaninge them selues well in the said Office we will to be remoueable att the pleaser of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company or the greater p̄te of them whereof the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company for the tyme being or his dep<sup>tie</sup> for the tyme being to be one. That then and soe often yt shall & may be lawfull to & for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company for the tyme beinge or the greater p̄te of them, whereof the gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup>[^sec-06-fn-050] or his Deputie to be one w<sup>th</sup>in Convenient tyme after the death or remoueinge of any of the said Comitties to assemble themselues in such convenient place as is or shall be vsuall or accustomed for the elecc̃on of the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Companie, or whereells the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Companie for the tyme being or his deputie shall appointe and that the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie or the greater p̄te of them, whereof the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> for the tyme being, or his deputie to be one being then and theare present shall & may then and theare before their depture from the said place elect & nominate one or more of the said Companie to be Comitties of the said Company in the places and steede, place or steede of him or them that soe dyed or were or was soe remoued, w<sup>ch</sup> pson or p̄sons soe elected[^sec-06-fn-051] to the office or offices of Comittee or Comittees of the said Company shall haue & exercyse the said Office and Officees for and during the residue of the said yeare takeinge first a corporall Oath, as is aforesaid for the due execuc̃on thereof and this to be done frome tyme to tyme soe often as the case shall requier.

AND ffurther we doe by theis p<sup>r</sup>sente for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> will and graunte vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the East Indies & their successo<sup>rs</sup> that they and all that are or shall be of the said Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the East Indies [p. 174] & eu<sup>r</sup>y of them and all the sonns of them, & eu<sup>r</sup>y of them att their seu<sup>r</sup>all ages of Twentie one yeares or vpmardes. And further all such the apprentices ffactors or servaunte of them and eu<sup>r</sup>y of them, w<sup>ch</sup> heereafter shall be ymployed by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Comp: in the said trade of m<sup>r</sup>chandize of or to the East Indies beyond the Seas or any other the places aforesaid in any pte of the said East Indies shall and may by the space of xv<sup>teene</sup> yeares from the feast of the birth of o<sup>r</sup> Lord God last past before the date hereof ffreelie traffick & vse the trade of m<sup>r</sup>chandize by Seas in & by such waies and passages already found out and discou<sup>r</sup>ed and [^sec-06-fn-052] w<sup>ch</sup> heereafter shall be found out and discou<sup>r</sup>ed as they shall esteeme and take to be fittest into and from the said East Indies into the Countries and pte of Asia & Affrica and into & from all the Ilande porte Havens Citties Creeke Townes & places of Asia Africa & America or any of them beyond the Cape of Bona Esperansa to the straighte of Magalan where any trade or traffique of m<sup>r</sup>chaundize may be vsed and [^sec-06-fn-052] had and to & from eu<sup>r</sup>y of them in such order manner forme libertie and Condic̃on to all entente & purposes as shall be from tyme to tyme at any publique assemblie or Courte held by or for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or Companie, by or betweene them of the said Company of ffellowshipp of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the East Indies, or the more pte of them for the tyme being present at such assemblie or Courte The Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or his Deputie being alwaies present att such Courte or Assemblie lymitted and agreed: and not otherwyse w<sup>th</sup>out any molestañon impeachm<sup>t</sup> or disturbance any statute vsage diu<sup>r</sup>sitie religion or faith or any other cause or matter whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> to the Contrarie notw<sup>th</sup>standinge; soe ☞ alwaies the same trade be[^sec-06-fn-053] vndertaken nor addressed to any Country, Iland, porte, Haven Cittie Creeke Towne or place alreadie in the lawfull and actuall possession of any such Christian Prince or state as att this present is or at any tyme heereafter shalbe in league or amity w<sup>th</sup> vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> and who doth not or will not accept of such trade but doth ou<sup>r</sup>lie declare and publish the same to be vtterlie against his or their good will and likeinge


<!-- page: 267 | folio: 175 -->
> _[Margin: That the Comp: may assemble in any convenient place.]_
> _[Margin: Authoritie to make reasonable lawes by the greatest part of a gen<sup>r</sup>all assembly.]_
> _[Margin: To punish offenders eyther in body or purse soe as the same be not contrary to the lawes of the Realme.]_
> _[Margin: ffreedome of Custome of goodes outwardes graun-[^sec-06-fn-058]]_

<span class="sc">And</span> further o<sup>r</sup> will & peasuer is, and by theis presente for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successor<sup>rs</sup> we doe graunte vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London trading into the East Indies and to their successor<sup>rs</sup>, that yt shall & may be lawfull to and for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies & their successor<sup>rs</sup> from tyme to tyme to assemble themselues for or aboute any the matters causes affaires or busines of the said trade in any place or places for the same convenient during the said terme of ffifteene yeares w<sup>th</sup>in o<sup>r</sup> dominions or elswheare, & there to hold Courte for the said Companie and the affaires thereof, & that alsoe yt shall & may be lawfull to & for them or the more pte of them being soe assembled, & that shall then & theare be present in any such place or places whereof the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or his deputie for the tyme being to be one, to make, ordeine & constitute such and soe many reasonable lawes constitučōns, orders & ordenances as to them or the greater pte of them being then and theare present shall seeme necessarie and convenient for the good gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> of the same Companie & of all ffactor<sup>rs</sup> m<sup>rs</sup> Mariners & other Officers ymployed[^sec-06-fn-054] in any of their voyage, and for the better advauncement & continuance of the said trade and traffique, and the same lawes constitučōns orders and ordenaunces as by them or the greater pte of them shall be thought necessarie being[^sec-06-fn-055] soe made to putt in vse, & execučōn accordinglie, & at their pleasuer to revoke or alter the same, or any of them, as occasion shall requier and that the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie soe often as they shall make ordeine or establish any such lawes constitučōns orders & ordenances in forme aforesaid shall & may lawfullie ympose, ordeine lymitt & puide such peines punishmentę and Penalties by ymprisonm<sup>t</sup> of bodie, or by fynes or[^sec-06-fn-056] amercementę, or by all or any of them vpon & against all Offenders contrary to such lawes Constitučōns orders and ordenances [p. 176] or any of them as to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie for the tyme being, or the greater pte of them then & there being present the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or his Deputie being alwaies one shall seeme necessary requisite and Convenient for the observacõn of the same lawes constitucõns orders and ordenances, & the same fynes, & amercem<sup>t</sup>e, shall and may levy fyne take & haue to the vse of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie & their successo<sup>rs</sup> w<sup>th</sup>out the ympedim<sup>t</sup> of vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> or of any the Officers or mynisters of vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or[^sec-06-fn-057] successo<sup>rs</sup>, or w<sup>th</sup>out any accompt to vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> to be rendred or made. All & singuler w<sup>ch</sup> lawes, constitucõns, orders, and ordenances soe as aforesayd to be made we will to be dulie observed and kept vnder the peines and penalties therein to be conteyned: Soe alwaies the said lawes Constitucõns orders ordenance ymprisonm<sup>t</sup>e fynes and amercem<sup>t</sup>e be reasonable & not contrary or repugnant to the lawes statutes or Customes of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme AND forasmuch as the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the East Indies haue not yet experience of the kinde of Comodities and m<sup>r</sup>chandizes w<sup>ch</sup> are or will be vendible or to be vttered in the said pte of the East Indies and therefore shall be driven to carrie to those pte in their voyadge dyvers & sundry Comodities w<sup>ch</sup> are likelie to be retourned againe into this o<sup>r</sup> Realme. WEE therefore of our speciall grace certeine knowledge and meere mocõn for the better encourageing of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the[^sec-06-fn-059] East Indies and for the advauncem<sup>t</sup> of the said trade doe graunt vnto the saide Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company, and to their successo<sup>rs</sup> that they and their successo<sup>rs</sup> during the fower first voyage w<sup>ch</sup> they shall make or sett forth for or towardes the said East Indies shall & may transporte and carrie out of o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England, & the porte Creeke & havens thereof all such and soe much goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes, being goode and m<sup>r</sup>chandizes lawfullie passable & transportable out of this Realme and not prohibited to be transported by any lawe or statute of this Realme as shalbe by them their ffactor<sup>rs</sup> or assignes shipped in any shipp or shipps vessell or [p. 177] vessels to be ymployed in any of the said fower first voyage free of Custome subsidie or Pondage or any other duties or paym<sup>te</sup> to vs or o<sup>r</sup> successor<sup>rs</sup> due or belonging for the shippinge or transporting of the same or any of them: And yett neu<sup>r</sup>thelesse our will & pleasure is and we doe by theis presentę straightly chardge & Comaund that all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes soe to be transported out of this Realme from tyme to tyme during the[^sec-06-fn-060] ffower first voyage as ys aforesaid shall from tyme to tyme be dulie entered by the Customer Comptroller or other officer of such porte Creeke or place where the same goode or m<sup>r</sup>chaundizes shall happen to be shipped and laden before such tyme as the same shall be shipped or laden to be transported as aforesaid.

> _[Margin: <span class="sc">6 & 6 monnethes tyme for paym<sup>t</sup> of Custome & subsidie inward</span>]_
> _[Margin: If goodes miscarry going outward the value of Custome shall be allowed in other goodes afterward shipped]_
> _[Margin: The Custome of goodes being paid at the comeinge into this Realme it shalbe lawfull for any naturall subiect to shipp yt out againe vpon the first Custome w<sup>thin</sup> 13 monnethes]_

<span class="sc">And</span> alsoe of o<sup>r</sup> further espetiall grace certeyne knowledg and meere mo<span class="sc">con</span> we doe for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successor<sup>rs</sup> graunte to & w<sup>th</sup> the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London trading into the East Indies and their successor<sup>rs</sup> that when & as often at any tyme during the said terme and space of ffyfteene yeares as any Custome pondage subsidie or other duties shall be due & payable vnto vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successor<sup>rs</sup> for any goode wares or m<sup>r</sup>chandize whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> to be retourned out or from any the Ilande & porte Havens Citties Townes or place aforesaid vnto the porte of London or any of the Havens Creeke members or places to[^sec-06-fn-061] the said porte belongeing that the Customers and all other officers for the tyme being of vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successor<sup>rs</sup> for or concerning receipte of Custome Pondage subsidies or other duties vnto whom yt shall apperteyne shall vpon the request of the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of the said m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies or any their Agente ffactor<sup>rs</sup> or assignes[^sec-06-fn-062] sixe monnethes tyme for the payment of the one halfe, and after those sixe monnethes ended other sixe monnethes tyme for the payment of the other halfe of their said Custome pondage or other subsidie or duties receyueing good & sufficient bonde w<sup>th</sup> suertie to the vse of vs o<sup>r</sup> heires & successor<sup>rs</sup> for the true payment [p. 178] of the same accordinglie and vpon the receipt of the said bonde w<sup>th</sup> suertie from tyme to tyme to giue vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Comp: of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the East Indies for the tyme being their Agente ffactor<sup>s</sup> or Assignes their Cockette or other warrante to take out & receiue on land the same goode wares & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes by vertue thereof w<sup>th</sup>out any disturbaunce. And that alsoe as often as at any tyme duringe the said terme of ffifteene[^sec-06-fn-063] yeares any goode wares or marchandizes of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company for the tyme being Laden from o<sup>r</sup> porte of London or any the Creeke members or places to[^sec-06-fn-064] the same porte belongeing to be transported to or towarde any of the porte Ilande Havens Citties townes or places aforesaid shall happen to miscarrie or be lost before their safe arrivall or dischardge in the Porte for and to w<sup>ch</sup> the same shall be sent that then and soe often, soe much Custome pondage subsidies or other duties as they aunsweared to vs for the same before their goinge forth of o<sup>r</sup> said porte Havens or Creeke shall after due proofe made before the Thr̄er of England for the tyme beinge of the said losse and the iust quantitie thereof be by vertue hereof allowed by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company their Agente or ffactor<sup>s</sup> by warrant of the said Thr̄er to the said Customers or officers in the next goode wares or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes that the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company or their successor<sup>s</sup> shall and may shipp for or towarde those places[^sec-06-fn-065] accordinge to the true rate of the Customes pondage or subsidies before paid for the goode wares or m<sup>r</sup>chaundizes soe loste or myscarrying or any pte thereof and for y<sup>t</sup> the[^sec-06-fn-066] Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies are like to bringe into this o<sup>r</sup> Realme a much greater quantetie of forreine Comodities from the parte of the said East Indies then can be spent for the necessarie vse of the same o<sup>r</sup> Realme w<sup>ch</sup> of necessitie must be transported into other Countries and there vented, We for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successor<sup>s</sup> of o<sup>r</sup> espetiall grace c<sup>r</sup>teine knowledge & meere moc̃on doe graunte to and w<sup>th</sup> the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> [p. 179] & Companie of marchauntę of London trading into the East Indies and their successor<sup>rs</sup> that at all tymes from tyme to tyme during the space of thirteene monnethes next after the dischardge of any of the said forreine Comodities soe to be brought in the subsidies pondage Customes & other duties for the same being first paied or compounded for as afore said, It shall be lawfull for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company and their successor<sup>rs</sup> or any other naturall subiecte of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme w<sup>ch</sup> may or shall buie the same of them or[^sec-06-fn-067] transporte the same in English Bottoms freelie out of this Realme aswell vngarbled as garbled w<sup>th</sup>out paym<sup>te</sup> of any further Custome, pondage, or any further subsidie to vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successor<sup>rs</sup> for the same whereof the subsidy pondage Customes or other duties shall be soe formerlie paid or Compounded for as aforesaid and soe prouided[^sec-06-fn-068] and the said Customer or other officer or officers to whome yt shall in that behalfe appteine for the tyme being by vertue hereof shall vpon due and sufficient prooff thereof made in the Customes[^sec-06-fn-069] howse[^sec-06-fn-070] or belonging to the said[^sec-06-fn-071] port of London giue them sufficient cockett or certificate, not[^sec-06-fn-072] for the safe passinge out therof accordinglie. And to theend noe deceipt be vsed therein[^sec-06-fn-073] to vs our heires or successor<sup>rs</sup> Certificate shalbe brought from the Collector of the Custome, subsidie, pondage, or other duties inwardes of vs our heires or successor<sup>rs</sup> that the said goode wares or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes haue w<sup>th</sup>in the tyme lymitted aunsweared their due custome subsidy pondage or other duties for the same inwardes vnto the Collector[^sec-06-fn-074] of the Custome subsidy pondage or other duties outwardę of vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successor<sup>rs</sup>.[^sec-06-fn-075]

> _[Margin: That yt shall be lawfull in the first voyadge to carry out in forreine coyne procured by the Comp: or bullion the value of xxx m<sup>li</sup> soe as 6 m<sup>li</sup> thereof be new coyned in the mynt]_
> _[Margin: After the said first voyadge in all the rest of the voyages they may carry but[^sec-06-fn-082] in eury vyadge xxx m<sup>li</sup> of such forreine Coyne as they bringe into the Realme soe as thereof 6 m<sup>li</sup> be new coyned in the mint.]_

AND moreou<sup>r</sup> we of o<sup>r</sup> further espetiall grace certeine [p. 180] knowledge and meere moc̃õn haue graunted & by theis presente for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires & successo<sup>rs</sup> doe graunte vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of marchaunte of London trading into the East Indies that yt shall & may be lawfull for them their ffactor<sup>rs</sup> or Assignes in their first voyadge or ffleete w<sup>ch</sup> is now in p<sup>r</sup>paringe for their first Adventure to the said East Indies to transporte out of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England all such forreine Coyne of sylver, eyther spannish or other forreine sylver as they haue p̄cured p<sup>r</sup>pared & gotten, or shall procure prepare or gett as likewyse all such other Coyne of sylver as they haue p̄cured or shall p̄cure to be coyned in o<sup>r</sup> mynte w<sup>th</sup>in o<sup>r</sup> Tower of London out of such plate or bullion as ys or[^sec-06-fn-076] shall be p̄uided for[^sec-06-fn-077] the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the East Indies their ffactor<sup>rs</sup> or assignes before the goinge forth of the same ffleete in[^sec-06-fn-078] this their[^sec-06-fn-079] first voyadge[^sec-06-fn-080] soe as the whole quantetie of Coyne & moneys to be transported in this their said first voyadge[^sec-06-fn-081] doe not exceede the value or some of Thirtie Thowsand pounde starlinge And soe as the some of sixe thowsand pounde att the least p̄cell of the said some of Thirtie thowsand pounde be first Coyned in o<sup>r</sup> minte w<sup>th</sup>in our Tower of London[^sec-06-fn-083] before the same shall be transported as aforesaid any lawe restrainte or p̄hibition in that behalfe notw<sup>th</sup>standinge. And in like mann<sup>r</sup> of o<sup>r</sup> espetiall grace c<sup>r</sup>teine knowledge & meere moc̃õn, we haue graunted and[^sec-06-fn-084] doe for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> graunte vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the East Indies & their successo<sup>rs</sup>.

That yt shall and may be lawfull to & for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie and their successo<sup>rs</sup> after the said first voyadge sett forth yearelie for and during the residue of the [p. 181] said terme of ffifteene yeares to shipp and transporte out of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England or dominions of the same in any their other voyadge to or towarde any the parte aforesaid in forme afore mencioned all such forreine Coyne of sylver, spannish or other forreine sylver or bullion of sylver, as they shall duringe the said terme bringe or cause to be brought into this Realme of England in[^sec-06-fn-085] the pte beyond the Seas, eyther in the same kinde sorte stampe or ffashion w<sup>ch</sup> yt shall haue when they bringe it in, or any other forme, stampe or fashion to be coyned w<sup>thin</sup> o<sup>r</sup> Mint w<sup>thin</sup> o<sup>r</sup> Tower of London at their pleasuer, soe as the whole quantities of coyne or moneys by them to be transported in any their said voyage during the residue of the said terme doe not exceede the value or some of Thirtie Thowsand pounde in any one voyage, and soe as the some of sixe thowsand pounde at the least pcell of the said some or value of xxx m<sup>li</sup> soe to be transported as aforesaid, be first coyned w<sup>thin</sup> o<sup>r</sup> said Tower of London before the same shall be transported in any of the said voyage any lawe statute restrainte or phibĩcõn in that behalfe in any wyse notw<sup>th</sup>standinge.

> _[Margin: That the trade shalbe traded according to y<sup>e</sup> Ordenances of the Company & not otherwyse]_

<span class="sc">And</span> further we of o<sup>r</sup> ample and aboundant grace, more[^sec-06-fn-086] moc̃on and certeyne knowledge haue graunted by[^sec-06-fn-087] theis presente for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successors, doe graunt vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the East Indies & their successo<sup>rs</sup> that they and their successo<sup>rs</sup> and their ffacto<sup>rs</sup> servante or assignes in the trade of m<sup>r</sup>chandize for them & on their behalfe & not otherwyse shall for the said terme of ffyfteene yeares, haue, vse, and enioy the wholle entyre & onelie trade & traffique and the wholle entire & onelie libertie vse & priviledge of tradinge & traffiqueing & vsinge feat & trade of m<sup>r</sup>chandize to & from the said East Indies & to & from all the Ilande Porte Havens Citties Townes and places aforesaid in such manner & forme as ys aboue mencioned And that[^sec-06-fn-088] the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into [p. 182] the East Indies, & eu<sup>r</sup>y pticuler & seu<sup>r</sup>all pson that now is, or that heerafter shalbe of that Company or incorporac̃on shall haue full and free authoritie libertie facultie lycence & power in forme aforesaid to trade & Traffique to & from the said East Indies, & all & eu<sup>r</sup>y the ptę thereof in forme aforesaid according to the orders ordenances & agreem<sup>te</sup> heereafter to be made & agr&ed vppon by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London trading into the East Indies & their successo<sup>rs</sup> or the more ptę of them present at any Courte or publique assemblie of or for the said Companie the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Companie or his Deputie for the tyme beinge alwaies present att such Courte or assembly & not otherwyse.

> _[Margin: That 6 good shipps & 6 pinnaces shalbe yearelie permitted to goe into the East Indies & 500 mariners any restraint notwthstandinge except the Nauie Royall goe forth.]_

And for that the shipps sayleing into the said Indies must take their due & propp tymes to pceede in theis voyage w<sup>ch</sup> otherwyse as we well pceaue cannot be pformed in the rest of the yeare followinge. THERFORE we of o<sup>r</sup> especiall grace certeine knowledge & meere moc̃on for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires & successo<sup>rs</sup> do graunt to & w<sup>th</sup> the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies and their successo<sup>rs</sup>, that in any tyme of restrainte sixe good shipps & sixe good Pynnaces well furnished w<sup>th</sup> ordenance & other munic̃on for their defence, & fiue hundred Mariners Englishmen to guide & sayle in the same sixe shipps & sixe Pynnaces att all tymes during the said terme of fyfteene yeares shall quietlie be p̄mitted & suffered to departe & goe in the said voyages accordinge to the purport of theis p<sup>r</sup>sentę w<sup>th</sup>out any stay or contradicc̃on by vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> or by y<sup>e</sup> Lo: High admirall or any other officer or subiect of vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successors for the tyme being in any wyse any restrainte lawe statute vsage or matter whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> to the contrarie notw<sup>th</sup>standinge.

> _[Margin: A prohibicon to all other subjectes not free of this comp: for trading into those partes upon seuerall peines wthout the licence & assent of the Companie.]_
> _[Margin: forfecture of goodes & shipps]_

PROUIDED neu<sup>r</sup>theles that yf we shall att any tyme w<sup>th</sup>in the said terme of fifteene yeares, haue iust cause to arme our Navy in warlike manner in defence of o<sup>r</sup> Realme or for Offence of o<sup>r</sup> enymies or that yt shall be found needfull to ioyne to the Navy of vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> the shipps of o<sup>r</sup> subiectę to be alsoe armed for the warres to such a number as can not be supplied yf the said sixe shipps and sixe Pynnasses should be p̄mitted to [p. 183] departe as aboue is mentioned then vpon knowledge geven to[^sec-06-fn-089] vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> or by any[^sec-06-fn-090] Admirall to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company aboute the xx<sup>th</sup> day of the monneth of Iulie, or three monnethes before the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie shall begynn to make readie the same sixe shipps and sixe Pynnasses, that we may not spare the said sixe shipps & six Pynnasses & the Mariners requisite for them, to be out of o<sup>r</sup> Realme during the tyme that o<sup>r</sup> Navy shall be vpon the Seas. That then the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company shall forbeare to send sixe such shipps & sixe Pinnacę for their trade of m<sup>r</sup>chandize, vntill that we shall revoke or w<sup>th</sup>drawe o<sup>r</sup> said Navy for this[^sec-06-fn-091] service. And we of o<sup>r</sup> further royall favo<sup>r</sup> and of o<sup>r</sup> especiall grace certeine knowledge and meere moc̃on haue graunted, and by theis presentę for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires & successo<sup>rs</sup> doe graunte vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies and to their successo<sup>rs</sup> That the said East Indies nor the Ilandę Havens Portę Citties Townes or places thereof, nor of any pte thereof shall[^sec-06-fn-092] be visited frequented or haunted by any of the subiectę of vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> during the said terme of xv<sup>teene</sup> yeares contrarie to the true meaneing of theis presentę. And by vertue of o<sup>r</sup> p<sup>r</sup>rogatiue royall, w<sup>ch</sup> we will not in that behalfe be argued or brought in question: We straight chardge comaund and phibitt for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires & successo<sup>rs</sup> all the subiectę of vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> of what degree or qualitie soeu<sup>r</sup> they be, that none of them directlie or indirectlie visitt haunte frequent or Trade, traffique or adventure by way of m<sup>r</sup>chandize into or from any of the said East Indies, or into & from any of the Ilandę, Portę Havens, Citties Townes or places aforesaid other then the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London trading into the East Indies, and such pticuler psons as now be or heereafter shall be of that Companie their Agentę ffacto<sup>rs</sup> & assignes duringe the said terme of fyfteene yeares[^sec-06-fn-093] vnles [p. 184] yt be by & w<sup>th</sup> such licence and agreement of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunt*e* of London tradinge to the East Indies in wryting first had & obtayned vnder their Comon seale to be graunted, vpon payne that euery such pson or psonns that shall trade or traffique into or from any of the said East Indies other then the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunt*e* of London & their successo<sup>rs</sup> shall incurr o<sup>r</sup> indignac̃on and the forfecture & losse of the goodes m<sup>r</sup>chaundizes & other thing*e* whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> soe shall be brought into this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England or any the dominion[s] of the same contrarie to o<sup>r</sup> said phibition, or the purporte or[^sec-06-fn-094] true meaneing of theis present*e* as alsoe the shipp and shipps w<sup>th</sup> the furniture thereof wherein such goode m<sup>r</sup>chaundizes or thing*e* shalbe brought:

> _[Margin: Diuision of the forfectures.]_
> _[Margin: Imprisonm<sup>t</sup>.]_
> _[Margin: entring into bond of 1000<sup>li</sup>]_

The halfe[^sec-06-fn-095] of all the said forfectures to be to vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup>, and the other halfe of all & eu<sup>r</sup>y the said forfecture[s] we doe by theis present*e* of o<sup>r</sup> espetiall grace certeine knowledge & meere moc̃on clearlie and whollie for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> giue and graunte vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunt*e* of London trading into the East Indies. And further all & eu<sup>r</sup>y the said Offendo<sup>rs</sup> for their said Contempt to suffer imprisonment duringe o<sup>r</sup> pleasure and such other ponishm<sup>t</sup> as to vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> for soe high a Contempt shall seeme meete & convenient & not to be in any wyse deliu<sup>r</sup>ed vntill they & eu<sup>r</sup>y of them shalbe come bound vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> for the tyme being in the some of 1000<sup>li</sup> att the least at noe tyme then after during this present graunte to sayle or traffique into any of the said East Indies contrarie to o<sup>r</sup> expresse Comaundement in that behalfe herein sett downe & published.

> _[Margin: How the Comp: may graunt lycence to others & what tymes.]_
> _[Margin: That her matie will not graunt lycence to any others to enter into the partes aforesaid during the terme of xvteene yeares]_
> _[Margin: That the Company may admitt others att their pleasures into this fredome]_
> _[Margin: That yf any named in the pattent doe not bring in his promysed aduenture sett downe yt shall be lawfull for]_
> _[Margin: y<sup>e</sup> Companie to disfranchyse him.]_
> _[Margin: The Companie doe promyse to bring in after eu<sup>r</sup>y voyadge retourned w<sup>th</sup>in 6 monnethes as great a quantetie of silver gould or forraine Coyne as they shall carry out th first viadg excepted]_
> _[Margin: All sylver or gould[^sec-06-fn-103] carried forth by the Comp: shalbe shipped att the portes of London Dartmouth or Plymouth.]_
> _[Margin: This priuiledg shall not extend into any place being in the actuall possession of any prince in league or amytie wth her matie:]_

And further for the better encouragem<sup>t</sup> of m<sup>r</sup>chaunt[^sec-06-fn-096] straungers & others to bringe in Comodities into this our Realme, we for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> doe graunt vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunt*e* of London tradinge into the East Indies that they & their successo<sup>rs</sup> shall from tyme to tyme for any Considerac̃on or benefitt to be taken to their owne vse graunt or giue [p. 185] licence to any pson or psons to sayle trade or traffique into or from any of the said East Indies soe as such licence be graunted or geuen before such goode wares & m<sup>r</sup>chaundizes be laid on land, & soe as such lycence be made by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies for the tyme beinge vnder their Comon seale. And further of o<sup>r</sup> especiall grace certeyne knowledge, & meere moc̃on, we haue Condescended and graunted, and by theis presente for[^sec-06-fn-097] o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> wee doe condescend & graunt vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into the[^sec-06-fn-098] East Indies and their successo<sup>rs</sup> that we o<sup>r</sup> heires & successo<sup>rs</sup> during the said terme of xv<sup>teene</sup> yeares will not graunte libertie licence or power to any pson or psons whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> contrary to the Teno<sup>r</sup> of theis o<sup>r</sup> lres Pattente to sayle passe trade or traffique to the said East Indies or into or from the Ilande porte Havens Citties Townes or place aforesaid or any of them contrarie to the true meaneinge of theis presente w<sup>th</sup>out the Consent of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading into the East Indies or the most pte of them. And o<sup>r</sup> will and pleasure is and hereby we doe alsoe ordeyne that that yt shall & may be lawfull to & for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies or the more pte of them whereof the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> for the tyme being or his deputie to be one to admitt into, & to be of the said Company all such apprentises to any of the said ffellowshipp or company and all such servaunte & ffacto<sup>rs</sup>[^sec-06-fn-099] of or for the said Company, & all such others as to them or the more pte of them present at any Courte held for the said Company the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or his deputie being one shalbe thought ffitt and agreeable w<sup>th</sup> the orders and Ordenances to be made for the Gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> of the said Company PROUIDED alwaies that yf any of the psons before named and appointed by theis presente to be free of the said Companie of [p. 186] m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies shall not before the goinge forth of the ffleete appointed for this first voyadge from the porte of London bringe in & deliu<sup>r</sup> to the Thrēr or Thrērs appointed, or w<sup>ch</sup> w<sup>th</sup>in the space of Twentie daies next after the date hereof shalbe appointed by the said gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company or the more pte of them, to receiue the Contribucõns and adventures sett downe by the seu<sup>r</sup>all Aduenturo<sup>rs</sup> in this first[^sec-06-fn-100] & present voyadge now in hand to be sett forth such somes of money as haue beene by any of the said p̱sons by theis presentę nominated to be of the said Company expressed sett downe & written in a booke appointed for that purpose, & left in the handę of the said Thomas Smyth Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the said Company or of the said Paule Bannynge Ald of London and subscribed w<sup>th</sup> the names or[^sec-06-fn-101] of the same aduenturo<sup>rs</sup> vnder their handę & agreed vpon to be aduentured in the said first voyadge that then yt shall be lawfull for the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie or the more pte of them, whereof the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> or his deputie to be one at any their generall Courte, or generall assembly to remoue disfranchise & displace him or them att their wills and pleasures. And the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London tradinge into the East Indies for them and their successo<sup>rs</sup> doe by theis presentę couenant p̱myse & graunte to & w<sup>th</sup> [^sec-06-fn-102] o<sup>r</sup> heires & successo<sup>rs</sup> that they the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company and their successo<sup>rs</sup> in all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such voyage as they att any tyme or tymes heareafter duringe the said tearme shall make out of this Realme by vertue of this o<sup>r</sup> graunt and łres Pattentę the first voyadge onelie excepted shall & will vpon eu<sup>r</sup>y retourne w<sup>ch</sup> shall be made backe agayne into this o<sup>r</sup> Realme or any of o<sup>r</sup> dominions or w<sup>th</sup>in sixe monnethes next after eu<sup>r</sup>y such retourne bringe into this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England from the said East Indies or from some other parte beyond the seas out of o<sup>r</sup> Dominions, as greate or greater value in bullion of gould or syluer, or other forreyne Coyne of gould or silver respectiuelie for eu<sup>r</sup>y voyadge, the first voyadge [p. 187] onelie excepted as shall be by force of theis presente transported and carried out of this Realme by them or any of them in any kinde of sylver abouesaid whatsoe<span class="sc">u</span><sup>r</sup> in any of the said voyadge and that all such sylver as by vertue of this o<sup>r</sup> graunte & lres Patente shall be shipped or laden by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company or their successo<sup>rs</sup> to be transported out of this Realme in any of the said voyage, shall from tyme to tyme at the settinge forth of eu<sup>r</sup>y such pticuler voyadge be shipped or laden att the Porte or Havens of London Darmouth or Plymouth, or at some of the same porte or havens, & at no other porte or haven whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> w<sup>th</sup>in this o<sup>r</sup> Realme or the dominions thereof and that all & eu<sup>r</sup>y such syluer as from tyme to tyme shall be shipped & laden in the said Porte of London Dartmouth or Plymouth, or any of them to be by force of theis presente transported out of this Realme as[^sec-06-fn-104] aforesaid shall from tyme to tyme be dulie entered by the Customer Comptroller Collector or other officer to whome yt shall appteyne of eu<sup>r</sup>y such Porte or Haven where the same shall happen to be shipped or laden in the Custome booke belonging to the said porte or Haven before such tyme as the same shall be shipped or laden to be transported as aforesaid w<sup>th</sup>out any Custome or subsydie to be paied for the same. And that in like manner all & all manner of gould & sylver whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall be brought into this realme or any of o<sup>r</sup> dominions by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie or any of them accordinge to the true meaneinge of theis presente shall be likewyse[^sec-06-fn-105] from tyme to tyme dulie entered by the Customer Comptroller or other officer of eu<sup>r</sup>y such Porte Creeke or place where the same gould or silver shall happen to be vnshipped or brought to land before such tyme as the same gould or silver, or any pte thereof shall be vnshipped or brought to land as ys aforesaid. P<span class="sc">ROUIDED</span> alwaies neu<sup>r</sup>theles & o<sup>r</sup> will & pleasure is that theis o<sup>r</sup> lres Patente or any thinge therein Conteyned shall not in any sorte extend to giue or [p. 188] graunte any lycence power or aucthoritie vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunt*e* of London trading into the East Indies or to any of them to vndertake or addresse any trade vnto any Countrie Port, Iland, Haven, Cittie, Creeke Towne or place being alreadie in the lawfull & actuall possession of any such Christian Prince or state as at this present is or at any tyme heereafter shall be in league or amytie w<sup>th</sup> vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup>, or w<sup>ch</sup> doth not or will not accept of such trade but doth ouertlie declare and publishe the same to be vtterlie against his or their good will & likeing any thinge beinge[^sec-06-fn-106] before in theis present*e* conteyned to the Contrarie thereof notw<sup>th</sup>standinge.

> _[Margin: If this priviledge be found vnproffitable for the Realme then w<sup>th</sup>in 2 yeares warning geven vnder y<sup>e</sup> privie seale the same shall be voyde, but yf it shalbe found beneficiall then y<sup>e</sup> same to be renewed w<sup>th</sup> some addicons &c:]_

<span class="sc">Prouided</span> alsoe that yf yt shall heereafter appeare to vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> that this graunte, or the Continuance thereof in the wholle or in any p*e*te thereof shall not be p*f*fitable to vs o<sup>r</sup> o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> & to this o<sup>r</sup> Realme that then and from from thenceforth vpon & after two yeares warneinge to be geven to the said Company by vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> vnder o<sup>r</sup> or their priuie seale or signe Manuell, this present graunt shall cease, be voied, and determined to all entent*e* construc<span class="sc">c</span>õns & purposes. And further of o<sup>r</sup> espetiall grace certeine knowledg & meere mo<span class="sc">c</span>õn we haue Condescended and graunted, and by theis present*e* for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> doe Condescend & graunte to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunt*e* of London trading into the East Indies & their successo<sup>rs</sup> that yf att the end of the said tearme of fifteene yeares yt shall seeme meete & Convenient vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company or any the p*e*ties aforesaid that this present graunte shall be continued. And yf that alsoe it shall appeare vnto vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> that the Continuance thereof shall not be preiudiciall or hurtfull to this o<sup>r</sup> Realme but that we shall finde the further continuance thereof proffitable for vs o<sup>r</sup> heires and successo<sup>rs</sup> and for our Realme w<sup>th</sup> such Condi<span class="sc">c</span>õns as are herein mencioned, or w<sup>th</sup> some altera<span class="sc">c</span>õn or qualifica<span class="sc">c</span>õn thereof that then we o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> at the instaunce and humble peti<span class="sc">c</span>õn of the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company or any of them [p. 189] to be made vnto vs o<sup>r</sup> heires & successo<sup>rs</sup> will graunte and make vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company or any of them soe suing for the same and such other pson or psons o<sup>r</sup>[^sec-06-fn-107] subiecte as they shall nominate and appointe or shall be by vs o<sup>r</sup> heires or successo<sup>rs</sup> newly nominated not exceedinge in number fower & Twentie new łres Patente vnder the greate seale of England in due forme of lawe w<sup>th</sup> like graunte couenante[^sec-06-fn-108] clauses & articles as in theis presente are conteyned or w<sup>th</sup> addicõn of other necessarie articles or changeinge of theis into some other parte for and duringe the full terme of ffyfteene yeares then next followinge Willinge hereby and streightlie chardgeinge and Comaundeinge all & singuler o<sup>r</sup> Admiralls viceadmiralls Iustices Maiors Sheriffe Escheato<sup>rs</sup> Cunstables bayliffe and all & singuler other o<sup>r</sup> Officers ministers leidgmen and subiecte whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> to be aydeinge favo<sup>r</sup>inge helpeing and assistinge vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company and to their successo<sup>rs</sup> and to their deputies officers ffacto<sup>rs</sup> servaunte assignes & mynisters and eu<sup>r</sup>y of them in executeing and enioyeinge the premisses aswell on land as on Sea from tyme to tyme when you or any of you shall there vnto be required any statute, acte, ordenance provisoe proclamačon or restrainte heretofore had made sett forth ordeyned or puided, or any other matter cause or thinge whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> to the Contrarie in any wyse notw<sup>th</sup>standinge Although expresse menčon of the true yearelie value or certeinetie of the premisses or of any of them, or of any other Guifte or graunte by vs or any of o<sup>r</sup> progenito<sup>rs</sup> to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies, or to any of them before this tyme made in theis presente is not made Or any statute Acte ordenaunce pvision pclamačon or restrainte to the Contrary hereof heretofore had, made, ordeyned or puided, or any other thinge cause or matter whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> in any wyse notw<sup>th</sup>standinge.

<span class="sc">In Witnes</span> whereof wee haue caused theis o<sup>r</sup> łres to be made Patente Witnes o<sup>r</sup> selfe att Westminster the xxxi<sup>th</sup> day of December in the three & forteth yeare of o<sup>r</sup> Reigne p łre de privato sigillo &c<sup>a</sup> Huberd.

#### An agreem<sup>t</sup>[^sec-06-fn-109] w<sup>th</sup> Willm Cobreth for discou<sup>r</sup>y of the Norwest Passadge w<sup>th</sup> C:[^sec-06-fn-110] Waymouth.

<span class="sc">His</span> Indenture made the xx<sup>th</sup> day of Aprill Anno Dni 1602. & in the 44<sup>th</sup> yeare of the Reigne of o<sup>r</sup> sou<sup>r</sup>eigne Ladie Elizabeth by the grace of god Queene of England ffraunce & Ireland defendo<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c: Betweene Thomas Cambell of London Alderman on thone ptie & Willm Cobreth of Ratliffe in the Countie of Midds̄ Mariner on thother ptye. Witnesseth that whereas a c<sup>r</sup>teine voyadge is p<sup>r</sup>tended by godę grace, to be made from hence into the Norwest pte of China, Cataia, or Iapan or any other land in the latitude of 50 Degres Northward in the pte of [^sec-06-fn-111] beyond the Seas. It is Couenanted, condescended, and now fullie agreed by and betweene the said pties to theis presente in manner and forme following that is to saie. The said Willm Cobreth for him his Executors and Administrators & for euery of them doth Couenant and graunte to and w<sup>th</sup> the said Thomas Cambell his Executors & Administrators & eu<sup>r</sup>y of them by theis p<sup>r</sup>sente. That he the said Willm Cobreth shall and will be readie in the Cittie of London & goe on the said voyadge, & therein Contynue for the discou<sup>r</sup>y of the said Norwest pte, from hence of China Cataia or Iapan or any other land in the latitude of 50 Degres Northward at the Comaundem<sup>t</sup> will & appointm<sup>t</sup> of Capt: George Waymouth in such a ship as the same Capten shall thinke good. And on the same voyadge shall proceede and saile effectuallie to thutmost of his skill or knowledg w<sup>th</sup>out fraude or Coven, and not depte or goe from the said voyadge w<sup>th</sup>out the spetiall lycence of the said Capt: George Waymouth first had and obtayned in that behalfe. In Consideracõn whereof the said Willm Cobreth hath receiued in hand at thensealeing & deliu<sup>r</sup>y hereof the some of xx<sup>li</sup> of &c: in pte of paym<sup>t</sup> of his wages for the said pretended voyadge, whereof he acknowleth himselfe fullie satisfied and contented. And the said Thomas Cambell for him his [executors] and Adminī & for eu<sup>r</sup>y of them doth Couenante & graunte to & w<sup>th</sup> the said Willm Cobreth his Executors & Admin̄ by theis p<sup>r</sup>sente That he the said [p. 191] Thomas Cambell his Execū or Ass<sup>s</sup> shall well and trulie paie or cause to be paid vnto the said Wilłm Cobreth his Execū or Ass<sup>s</sup> vpon the discou<sup>r</sup>y of the said Norwest passadg or pt*e* of China, Cataia, or Iapan, or any other land in the latitude of 50 Degres Northward and retourne from thence into the Realme of England the some of six pound*e* of &c, for eu<sup>r</sup>y monneth that the said Wilłm Cobreth shall be vpon the said voyadge (the said xx<sup>li</sup> paid in hand as aforesaid being reconed as pte & pcell thereof [ ]). Provided alwaies that yf the said Wilłm Cobreth & his Comp. shall not fortune to discou<sup>r</sup> the said Norwest pt*e* of China, Cataia or Iapan or any other Land in the Latitude of 50 Degres Northward as aforesaid : Then the said Thomas Cambell his Execū or Assignes shall well & trulie paie or cause to be paid vnto the said Wilłm Cobreth his Executor<sup>s</sup> or Assignes, onelie the some of iij<sup>li</sup> of &c: for eu<sup>r</sup>y monneth that the said Wilłm Cobreth shall be vpon the said voyadge the said xx<sup>li</sup> paid in hand as aforesaid being alwaies accompted as pte & pcell thereof. In Witnes &c:


#### A Coppie of a łre of Reprisall for the East Indian Marchaunt*e*.[^sec-06-fn-112]

<span class="sc">Charles</span> Earle of Notingham[^sec-06-fn-113] Baron of Effingham knight of the most noble order of the Garter, Lord Leiuetenante of her ma<sup>ties</sup> Counties of Sussex & Surrey Constable of hir mat*e* honor[^sec-06-fn-114] and Castle of Windsor Ld : High Admirall of England Ireland and Wales and the Dominions & Iles of the same, Of the Towne of Callis & m<sup>r</sup>ches thereof Normandy Gascoyne and Guines & Capteine Gen<sup>r</sup>all of her ma<sup>ties</sup> Seas & Navy royall. To all Christian People to whome theis present*e* shall come or other wyse appteyne greeting in o<sup>r</sup> Lord god eu<sup>r</sup>lasting. Whereas o<sup>r</sup> souereigne Lady [p. 192] Elizabeth by the grace of god Queene of England ffraunce & Ireland defendo<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c : beinge Crediblie adverticed that the kinge of Spaine hath of late made staye of the shipps goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes of hir ma<sup>ties</sup> : loueing subiecte w<sup>th</sup>in the Realme of Spaine & Portingale & other places of his Dominions, & hath caused them their[^sec-06-fn-115] being for the trade of m<sup>r</sup>chandizes to be reteyned & kept in prizon Contrary to the order of Lawe & Iustice.   Upon the humble and pitifull sute of hir ma<sup>ties</sup> said subiecte the m<sup>r</sup>chaunte owners & others interessed in the said ships goode and psonns soe stayed made to hir ma<sup>tie</sup> for łres of Reprisalls to be graunted vnto them and that they not haueing any other meanes by order of Iustice to be yealded vnto them might by lycenced to stay apprehend and take the shipps goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes of the kinge of Spaine, or any his Subiecte wheresoeu<sup>r</sup> vpon the Seas to aunsweare and satisfie the losse and damadge by them susteyned by reason of their ships and goode soe taken and reteyned hath by her ma<sup>ties</sup> : łres Patente beareing date the ninth day of Iulie— 1585. vnder her ma<sup>ties</sup> : seale willed and authorized me as hir ma<sup>te</sup> Admirall to graunt Comission for the apprehending and takeing the shipps goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes of the kinge of Spaine, or any his subiecte to such hir ma<sup>tes</sup> loueing subiecte soe dampnified & in such manner and forme and according to such articles & orders as by the lorde & others of her ma<sup>te</sup> privie Councell or by any six of them should be agreed vpon & set downe vnder their hande.   And whereas tenn of the Lorde & others of her ma<sup>ties</sup> : privy Councell haue agreed upon Certeine articles & orders in that behalfe & haue set downe the same in writeing vnder their hande & haue deliuered the same to me for my direcc̃on herein w<sup>ch</sup> ar<sup>cles</sup> & orders be & remaine w<sup>th</sup> me of recorde.   And whereas further the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Assistante & Companie of the m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading for the East Indies, haue made proofe before me that certeine of their goode shipps & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes, were of late stayed arrested & deteyned in the pte of Spaine by the kinge order & authoritie there, & that the losse & damadge thereof vnto them by reason of the said stay & seasure ariseing doth amounte to the some of 2000<sup>li</sup> ster: or thearaboute wherevpon the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Assistaunte & Company of the m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading for [p. 193] the East Indies aforesaid haue reedy victualled & furnished to the Seas one Shipp Called the Suzan[^sec-06-fn-116] of London of the burthen of 250 Tonnes or thereaboutes whereof Iohn Havard goeth Capteine & Samuell Spencer m<sup>r</sup> w<sup>th</sup> mariners & menn of Warr being victualled for monnethes & furnished w<sup>th</sup> Caste peeces & haue likewyse entred into bond in hir ma<sup>ties</sup> high Courte of the Admiralty that neither the said shipp nor any the Company thereof shall not attempt against any hir ma<sup>ties</sup> loueing subiecte the subiecte of the ffrentch kinge the kinge of Scotland Denmarke or Sweden or any the Inhabitants of the United provinces of the Haunce Townes or lowe Countries or the subiecte of any other Prince or potentate being in good league and amity w<sup>th</sup> her ma<sup>tie</sup>, but onelie against the Subiecte of the kinge of Spaine: And alsoe shall bring or cause to be brought all such shipps goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes as they shall soe take & apprehend of the kinge of Spaine or any his subiecte together w<sup>th</sup> three or fower of the Company of eu<sup>r</sup>y such prize as shall be of most accompte whereof the m<sup>r</sup> & Pilott to be twoe to some porte of this hir ma<sup>ties</sup> Realme of England as shall be most Convenient for them, And shall not breake, bulke, waste, spoyle, sell or diminish any such shipps & goode soe taken vntill the shall be adiudged in hir ma<sup>ties</sup> high Courte of the Admiraltie to be lawfull prize. And therevpon an Inventorie to be taken by the viceadmirall of the place or his Deputie & other publique Officers of the same, And appraisment made of the same goode by some six honest menn Inhabitante of the said Porte where they shall soe arriue, and that the same Inventory & appraism<sup>t</sup> shall be retourned into hir ma<sup>ties</sup> high Courte of the Admiraltie w<sup>th</sup>in six weeke then next ensueing. Know ye therefore that I the said Charles Earle of Notingham Lord High Ad<sup>ll</sup> aforesaid by vertue of her ma<sup>ties</sup> said łres Pattente to me directed doe lycence and authorize the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Assistaunte & Company of the m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London trading for the East Indies to sett forth to the Seas the said shipp called the Suzan, soe as is aforesaid [p. 194] furnished & munited and therew<sup>th</sup> to sett vpon and by force of Armes to staie & apprehend of the ships goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes of the kinge of Spaine, or any his subiecte in as ample manner as if it were in the tyme of open warr betwixt her ma<sup>tie</sup>: & the said kinge of Spaine, & the said ships goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes soe taken and brought into some porte of this hir ma<sup>ties</sup> Realme of England, & thereof an Inventory taken, appraism<sup>t</sup> made & iudgm<sup>t</sup> geven in the said high Courte of the Adm<sup>tie</sup>: in the said high Courte of the Admiralty for the Approbac̃on of the same to be agood & lawfull prize in manner & forme aforesaid. Then the said ships goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes to keepe and reteyne in his or their possession & to make sale & dispose thereof in open m<sup>r</sup>kett or howsoeur els to their best benefitt in as ample & beneficiall manner, as if the said ships goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes had bene Come by, through the lawfull traffique & trade of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte or of iust prize in the tyme of open warr betwixt hir ma<sup>tie</sup> & the said kinge of Spaine soe that neither the said Capteine master nor any the Company thereof that shall in his or their owne psonn serue in the shipp aforesaid, or otherwyse bear Chardge in the Adventure, or in any other sorte further or sett forewarde the said enterprize in manner & forme aforesaid, shall not be reputed or challendged for any offendo<sup>r</sup> against hir ma<sup>ties</sup> lawes and that alsoe it shall be lawfull for any manner of pson to buye the said ships goode & m<sup>r</sup>chandizes soe as aforesaid taken prayzed Inventoryed & adiudged w<sup>th</sup>out any daunger losse hindraunce trouble molestac̃on or incumbraunce whatsoeur Provided alwaies that yf by Colo<sup>r</sup> of this Comission there shall be taken any shipps goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes of any hir ma<sup>ties</sup>: loueing subiecte the subiecte of the ffrench kinge, the kinge of Scotland Denmarke or Sweden or any the Inhabitante of the united prouinces of the hance Townes or lowe Countries or the subiecte of any other Prince or Potentate being in good league & amity w<sup>th</sup> hir ma<sup>tie</sup> & the same or any other shipps taken by authoritie hereof shalbe spoyled sould imbeaselled or dyminished before they shall be adiudged in her ma<sup>ties</sup> high Courte of the Ad<sup>ty</sup>: to belong to the king of Spaine, or any of his subiecte that then this Comission to be void and of noe sufficient authoritie, either to take the said shipps & goode or to warrante [p. 195] or saue harmlesse such as shall receiue, bye or intermeddle therein, but that alsoe both the prizes soe taken, & the shipps of warr shall be Confiscate to o<sup>r</sup> vse. Prouided alsoe that the said shipps goode and m<sup>r</sup>chandizes soe as is aforesaid, after an Inventory taken, appraism<sup>t</sup> made & iudgment geven in manner and forme aforesaid shall be equallie devided into three p<sup>te</sup>, whereof one p<sup>te</sup> to goe to the m<sup>r</sup>chaunt*e* & owners of the said shipp, another p<sup>te</sup> to the victuallers & the third parte to the Captaine master mariners & souldiers thereof. Provided further that this Comission shall remaine and be in force during this their present voyadg, & noe longer In witnes whereof I haue herevnto caused the greate seale of myne office to be affixed: Yeven at London in hir ma<sup>ties</sup> high Courte of the Ad<sup>ty</sup> aforesaid the 23<sup>th</sup> day of Aprill. 1601. And in the 43<sup>th</sup> yeare of the Reigne of o<sup>r</sup> sou<sup>r</sup>eigne Lady Elizabeth by the grace of god Queene of England ffraunce & Ireland defendo<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c :


#### A łre from the Earle of Nottingham to m<sup>r</sup> Ceasar[^sec-06-fn-117] Iudge of the high Courte of the Ad<sup>ty</sup> :

<span class="sc">M<sup>r</sup> Ceasar</span> the marchaunt*e* of London haueing prepared fower good shipps for the voyadg to the East Indies in the trade of m<sup>r</sup>chandizes haue beene suto<sup>rs</sup> vnto me[^sec-06-fn-118] for Comission to take any shipps or goode belonging to the king of Spaine or to any of his subiect*e* either in their way outward*e*, or in their retourne, w<sup>ch</sup> I haue beene Contented to graunte vnto them. Therefore I doe pray you to cause Comission to be drawen for them, to furnish vnto the [p. 196] Seas in warlike manner for that purpose, the Read Dragon of London, whereof Iames Lancaster goeth Capteine, The Hector the Assencõn & the Suzan of the same Porte vnder such articles & Caucõn as are prescribed by hir ma<sup>tie</sup> for reprisalls, for w<sup>ch</sup> yo<sup>r</sup> soe doing this shall be yo<sup>r</sup> warrante, ffrom the Courte at Whitehall the 14th of Ianuary 1600.

Yo<sup>r</sup> loueing freind Notingham


#### Lres Pattente[^sec-06-fn-119] for transportacõn of 20000<sup>li</sup> in money to the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of East India 1606.

JAMES by the grace of God kinge of England ffraunce and Ireland defendo<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c: To all to whome theis presente shall come greetinge. Wheareas o<sup>r</sup> late deare sister Q: Elizabeth by her łres Patente vnder the greate seale of England beareing date at Westminster the xxxj<sup>th</sup> day of Decemb in the xliij<sup>th</sup> yeare of her Reigne vpon peticõn made vnto her by diu<sup>r</sup>s her loueing Subiectę, for her Royall assent and lycence to be graunted vnto them. That they at their owne Adventure Costę and Chardgę aswell for the Honor of this Realme of England, as for increase of Navigacõn & Advancem<sup>t</sup> of Trade of m<sup>r</sup>chandize w<sup>th</sup>in the same, might Adventure and set forth c<sup>r</sup>teine voyadgę w<sup>th</sup> a Convenient nomber of shipps and Pinnaces by way of Traffique & m<sup>r</sup>chandize into the East Indies in the Countries and Portę of Asia & Africa did incorporate the said Peticioners into abodie pollitique by the name of the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of the m<sup>r</sup>chauntę of London trading to the East Indies. To haue hould and enioye the sole benefitt of the trade and traffique of the said East Indies for the space of xv yeares from the byrth of o<sup>r</sup> Lord God then last past before the date of the said łres Patente. And [p. 197] whereas by the same lres Patente lycence was graunted to the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies to transporte out of this Realme into the said Indies in eu<sup>r</sup>y of their voyadge duringe the said terme of 15 yeares all such fforreigne Coyne of silver, spanish or other fforraine sylver, or bullion of sylver, as they should duringe the said tearme bringe or cause to be brought into this Realme of England, from the pte beyond the Seas, either in the same kinde, stampe, sorte or fashion, w<sup>ch</sup> yt should haue when they brought it in, or in any other forme, stampe, or fashion coyned in the Mynte w<sup>th</sup>in the Tower of London; soe as the whole quantities of Coyne or moneys by them to be transported in any their said voyage during the said tearme should not exceed the value of 30000<sup>li</sup> in any one voyadge, and soe as the some of vj<sup>m</sup> poundes at the least pcell of the said some or value of 30000<sup>li</sup> to be transported as aforesaid should be first Coyned w<sup>th</sup>in the same Tower of London, before the same might be transported in any of the said voyadge as by the said lres Patente more at lardge appeareth.

Now forasmuch as the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of the said m<sup>r</sup>chante since the said lres Patente to them graunted, haue made 2 seu<sup>r</sup>all voyadge into the said East Indies, & retourned their ships from thence laden w<sup>th</sup> sundrie kinde of m<sup>r</sup>chandizes pffitable for o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes, and haue alsoe prepared & are readie to set forth an other voyadge into the said East Indies, & haue humblie besought by petiñon, & shewed vnto vs, that by experience they haue form<sup>r</sup>lie found that they could not w<sup>th</sup>out greate difficultie, & losse vnto them in the value of their moneys new coyned, make trade for their m<sup>r</sup>chandize into the said East Indies, because they were not such as the people of those pte were acquainted w<sup>th</sup>all: but stamped w<sup>th</sup> an Image or supscripc̃on straunge & vnknowne vnto them.[^sec-06-fn-120] And that they haue beene and are desierous by all good meanes to manadge, & carrie their said trade as neare as they Cann for the benefitt of o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes and dominions rather by the transportac̃on of the Natiue Comodities of the same and by bartringe & exchaunge of them for fforreine Comodities w<sup>ch</sup> now they purpose more [p. 198] lardglie to attempt and haue good hope to accomplish, then by vsing the whole libertie graunted to them by the said łres Patente for carrieing out of the full some of 30000<sup>li</sup> in eu<sup>r</sup>y voyadge in manner aforesaid. And that they will content them selues in this their now third entended voyadge into the East Indies, w<sup>th</sup> the liƀtie of transportinge xx<sup>mli</sup> onelie in forreine Coynes w<sup>th</sup>out transportac̃on of any other Coyne, bullion, or silver. In reguard whereof they did humblie pray in their said petic̃on that we would be graciouslie pleased to graunte them lycence that they may transporte the value of xx<sup>mli</sup> of forreine Coyne in this their entended voyadge, w<sup>th</sup>out new coyninge the same or any p̃te thereof. Know yee therefore that we favoringethe said m<sup>r</sup>chante, & being desierous to giue them all furtherance & encouradgm<sup>t</sup> to proceede & goe forward in their trade of o<sup>r</sup> especiall grace, certeine knowledge and meere moc̃on, haue geven and graunted, and by theis presente for vs, o<sup>r</sup> heires & Successo<sup>rs</sup> doe giue and graunte lycence vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into the East Indies. That it shall and may be lawfull for them their facto<sup>rs</sup> & Assignes in his[^sec-06-fn-121] now p<sup>r</sup>tended voyadge into the East Indies to transporte out of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England all such forreine Coine or sylver, either spannish or other forreine silver, as they haue prepared, p̃cured, or gotten, or shall prepare p̃cure or gett being alredie brought or to be brought from the parte beyond the seas, before the depture of their shipps out of the Ryver of Thames. Soe as the whole quantitie of the Coyne an[?d?] moneys by them to be transported in this their p<sup>r</sup>sent intended voyadge towarde the said East Indies, doe not exceed the said value of 20000<sup>li</sup>. The same to be transported in the same kinde, sorte, stampe, or fashion, as the said moneys, are or shall be p̃cured, gotten, or brought into this Realme of England, and that w<sup>th</sup>out any new coyninge or altringe the said moneys or any p̃te thereof, from the stampe it beareth, any statute restrainte or p̃hibic̃on in that behalfe made to the Contrarie in any wyse notw<sup>th</sup>standinge. In Witnes whereof we haue caused theis o<sup>r</sup> łres to be made Patente. Witnes o<sup>r</sup> selfe at Westminster the v<sup>th</sup> day of Ianuarie [p. 199] in the 4th yeare of o<sup>r</sup> Reigne of England ffraunce & Ireland, & of Scotland the xl<sup>th</sup>.[^sec-06-fn-122]

Ravencroft p̄ b̄re de priuato sigillo &c:


##### <span class="sc">A Coppie</span>[^sec-06-fn-123] of the Patent for mitiga<span class="sc">c</span>õn of the Statute for garbling spices.

JAMES by the grace of God king of England Scotland ffraunce and Ireland defendo<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c: To o<sup>r</sup> high Treasurer, and Admirall of England, and to all other o<sup>r</sup> Admiralls Viceadmiralls Captaines and others seruinge vpon the Sea. And to all Maiors Sheriffe Constables Customers Comptrollers Surveyo<sup>r</sup> Searchers, Keeps of o<sup>r</sup> Porte, Creeke and Passadge and to all others o<sup>r</sup> Officers Ministers, and subiecte whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> to whome in that behalfe it shall or may appteyne and to eu<sup>r</sup>y of them greetinge.
