Item a Coppie of the Priviledge obtayned by S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster at Dachem & Sumatra to the Companie[^sec-07-fn-051] his obseruac̃on of tymes meete to be obserued in the East Indies[^sec-07-fn-052] And the Discripc̃on of the Ilande of Banda Amboyna Selebes o<sup>r</sup> Makasser Botton Seran w<sup>th</sup> the wares therein spent and bought & their weighte [p. 265] together w<sup>th</sup> c<sup>r</sup>teine direcc̃ons for saileing vpon the Coaste in the Indies.[^sec-07-fn-053]
- 6. A lre howe to deale w<sup>th</sup> Salbancke according to order of Courte the 5th of March 1607.[^sec-07-fn-054]
- 7. An order of Courte held the 11th of the said monneth of March, not to deale in any other mann<sup>r</sup> but by way of honest m<sup>r</sup>chandize[^sec-07-fn-055]
- 8. A lre to the ffactor<sup>s</sup> of the 3 voyadge[^sec-07-fn-056] w<sup>th</sup> a Coppie thereof & of theirs form<sup>r</sup>lie sent the last yeare for better vnderstandinge what is to be pformed on their pte of the 4<sup>th</sup> voyadg w<sup>th</sup> a note of the manner of his priuate trade & howe the same is to be registred &c :
- 9. An Invoice of all moneys & other thinge now sent : Carracters[^sec-07-fn-057] to write Overland (if need be) & Beames weighte & Scales &c.

#### Thinge then deliu<sup>r</sup>ed to m<sup>r</sup> Richard Rowles Leiuetenante gen<sup>r</sup>all.

<span class="sc">I. Inprimis</span> the foresaid Comission of the Companie vnder their seale signed by the Secretory

- 2 A Coppie of the foresaid Priuiledge obtayned by S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancaster at Dachem w<sup>th</sup> the obseruac̃on of tymes in the Indies & the discripc̃on of Ilande wares weighte & direcc̃on for saileinge vpon the Coaste of the Indies &c : before mencioned.
- 3 An other lre to the ffactor<sup>s</sup> of the 3 voyadge for the more saffetie in deliu<sup>r</sup>y thereof accordinge to the supscripc̃on w<sup>th</sup> a note of the mann<sup>r</sup> of his priuate trade & how the same is to be registred &c : The Copies of all thinge before mencioned are form<sup>r</sup>lie recorded in this Register.

<!-- page: 358 | folio: 266 -->
THE some of a Passe[^sec-07-fn-058] to be procured for the East India Companie from the Grandsignio<sup>r</sup> to **A B** and **C D** Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>rs</sup> of his Citties of Aden and Mocca at the mouth of the red sea & to all & eu<sup>r</sup>y other his Officers Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>rs</sup> and superio<sup>rs</sup> of any his Provinces Citties Townes Seas Rivers & Bridge &c: thereaboute, or ells where in any his Dominions.

> _[Margin: The some of a saffe Conducte from the Grand signior.]_

That whereas he and his Predicesso<sup>rs</sup> are and haue beene for the space of many yeares in league and amitie w<sup>th</sup> the mightie kinge of England & the subiecte of that kingdome haue longe had and now haue free traffique and trade in Marchandizeing in his dominions and Countries through the Mediterranean Seas: And whereas some of the Subiecte of that kingdome (as he is informed[]) haueing w<sup>th</sup> their greate chardge and labo<sup>r</sup> found out atrade in Theast Indies, & heareing of the fame & wealth of some pte of his Countries in their passadge to the said Indies, are desirous to vizitt those place for thenlardginge of their said trade. And Considering how beneficiall the same may be to him & his kingdomes, & that such men in soe good an enterprize proffitable to humane Societie deserue not onelie praise and favo<sup>r</sup> but alsoe aide and helpe soe far as may be lawfullie & convenientlie yealded. He hath beene pleased of his Princelie favo<sup>r</sup> to vouchsaffe them theis his łres of saffe Conducte and Comendačon Comanding the said **A B.** and **C D.** and all other his said Officers &c: not onelie kindlie and loueinglie to enterteine and receiue the said Marchaunte subiecte of England, comeing or passinge throughe, or by any of his dominions assistinge and releiueinge them w<sup>th</sup> all thinge needfull for them selues, their men and shipps: But alsoe freelie to pmitt them by land or by Sea to goe or saile to goe forward, or retourne and as their occasion shall requier to remaine in any his Countries Citties or dominions, grantinge them such libtie of traffique and priuiledge as shall be reasonable, w<sup>th</sup>out giueing or sufferinge any lett hindrance Iniurie or molestačon to be offered or done vnto them, & yealdinge vnto them such offices of benevolence & humanitie as shall be convenient to be yealded honest men and strangers vndertakeinge soe longe and laborious a iourney handlinge their owne affaires & behaueing them selues honestlie and peaceablie.


<!-- page: 359 | folio: 267 -->
> _[Margin: To o<sup>r</sup> verie loueing freind m<sup>r</sup> Hum: Smyth m<sup>r</sup>chant at Hull.]_

AFTER[^sec-07-fn-059] o<sup>r</sup> hartie Comendačóns &c: fforasmuch as we haue an intent to buie the shipp at Hull called the m<sup>r</sup>chaunt Royall soe as shee vpon veiwe may be found fitting for vs in all respectę aswell in her price as goodnes: & vnderstanding that by some yo<sup>r</sup> affaires, you now haue occasion to be at Hull or thereaboutę: we haue thought yt good and haue soe concluded to send the bearer hereof m<sup>r</sup> Robert Earle vnto you a man skilfull in shippinge to thend that by o<sup>r</sup> instrucčóns giuen him (a coppie whereof we send you here inclosed) & yo<sup>r</sup> good direcčóns, a diligent veiwe and inquirie may be taken of her, both for her price, goodnes, strength, breadth and fitnes for o<sup>r</sup> seruice, as for o<sup>r</sup> saffe inioyinge of her &c: Wherefore we pray you to make ymployment of the said m<sup>r</sup> Earle herein, & to giue him yo<sup>r</sup> helping hand for the pformance thereof in the best manner you may for the good of the Company. And further we doe requier you (yf you w<sup>th</sup> the advice of the said m<sup>r</sup> Earle) shall soe finde the said shipp in all respectę as aforesaid fitt for o<sup>r</sup> service to vse the best meanes you cann to buie her for thuse of this Companie soe as you may haue her deliu<sup>r</sup>ed here at London w<sup>th</sup> all thingę now belonging vnto her vnder or for the some of seaven hundred poundę at the most for the cheeffest man of abilitie and otherwise w<sup>th</sup> whome you are to deale for sale and securitie of her we conceiue to be m<sup>r</sup> Ioseph ffeild a man not vnknowne vnto you as we vnderstand But yf you cann not bargaine for her vnder or at that price at the most then we pray you to c<sup>r</sup>tifie vs of the pticulars thereof by the said m<sup>r</sup> Earle or by some more speedie [p. 268] Messenger that vpon receipt of yo<sup>r</sup> łres we may resolue what to doe in the same. And thus not doubting of yo<sup>r</sup> care and kindnes we comitt you to the tui<span class="sc">c</span>õn of Thalmightie London the 20<sup>th</sup> of Aprill 1608.

Yo<sup>r</sup> loueing freinde the Adventurers of theast India Company in the 4<sup>th</sup> voyadge.


#### The Twenteth of Aprill 1608.

A remembraunce for m<sup>r</sup> Robert Earle to be sent to Hull about veiwing of the shipp there to be sould called the m<sup>r</sup>chant Royall.[^sec-07-fn-060]

INPRIMIS you are w<sup>th</sup>all convenient expedi<span class="sc">c</span>õn to goe for Kingston vpon Hull or to Beverley or theareaboute to m<sup>r</sup> Humfrey Smyth of London m<sup>r</sup>chaunt at what place you may there first finde him & deliu<sup>r</sup>ing him theis o<sup>r</sup> łres you are to take and ffollowe what direc<span class="sc">c</span>õns he shall giue you in this busines.

Item yo<sup>u</sup> comeinge thither and findinge (w<sup>th</sup> the advice of the said m<sup>r</sup> Smyth) that the said shipp may be for o<sup>r</sup> seruice, you are to make diligent search and veiwe of her, of what strength she is of, what crosse beames, futtick Riders,[^sec-07-fn-061] bottume riders & needfull stannders[^sec-07-fn-062] &c : she hath in her : whereby yt may be the better conceiued what the cost will be to make her fitt for o<sup>r</sup> voyadge.

Item you are c<sup>r</sup>teinelie to learne her burthen, her breadth her length : how much water she draweth in her ballast, & howe much full laden, yf she be any way weakened by the longe lyinge not ymployed : her adge, & yf all her tymbers be sounde.

Item you are to vnderstand & see howe she is fitted w<sup>th</sup> good maste, sailes, yarde, Cables & other furniture.


<!-- page: 361 | folio: 269 -->
Item you are to make inquirie howe she is Condicioned in her saileing & steridge as otherwise : & alsoe what ordinance she hath, of weight and length &c : & of all other thinge needfull.

Item to learne her lowest price, & in that price what ordinance maste sailes yarde Cables & other thinge are to be sould w<sup>th</sup> her and being bought howe she may be brought hither & at whose chardge & what good securitie may be had for enioyinge of her, & by whome yt will be geven.

Lastlie you are to make an Inventorie of all the premisses in writeinge the better to informe vs at yo<sup>r</sup> retourne, in what state she is, what she hath & what she wanteth & the same being pformed you are to retourne by the first meanes you may : But yf before yo<sup>r</sup> comeing thither yt shall fall out that m<sup>r</sup> Humfrey Smyth shall be retourned thence for London then you are to followe theis yo<sup>r</sup> direccons w<sup>th</sup>out him wherein you are to vse all care & expedicon & Retourne.

> _[Margin: A Bill of Adventure to mr. Groues]_
> _[Margin: this is corrected & [^sec-07-fn-064] made as it was deliured to his wieff]_

<span class="sc">HEAREAS</span>[^sec-07-fn-063] we the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company of Marchaunte of London trading into the East Indies Haue interteyned and hired Phillipp de Graeffe of the precinct of S<sup>t</sup> Katherines neare to Tower of London Mariner to goe as principall m<sup>r</sup> in one of the twoe shipps now latelie by vs prepared & sent in o<sup>r</sup> fourth voyadge for those pte. And haue allowed and paied him for his ymployment in the said voyadge before his depture hence theis seu<sup>r</sup>all somes following Viz. The some of One hundred Twentie and ffyve pounde for his prepacon to sea: The some of Twentie pounde for fower monnethes Harborrow wage after the rate of ffyve [p. 270] pounde p̃ monneth : The some of ffortie shillinge for Boate hier : And further vpon his intreatie haue lent and ymprested vnto him the some of Eeighteene pounde ouʳ & aboue the somes formerlie giuen him, the wᶜʰ some of Eighteene pounde is onelie to be defalked out of such proffitt of Adventure as hereafter is granted him. Now knowe yee that we the said Gouʳnoʳ & Company, for further allowance & recompence of the good service travell and paines wᶜʰ he the said Phillipp de Graeffe faithfullie p̃myseth to to his best endeuoʳˢ to p̃forme in the said voyadge both outwarde & homewarde for the good of the said Company Doe by theis presente for vs & oʳ Successoʳˢ promyse and agree to giue and allowe vnto him the said Phillipp de Graeffe his Executoʳˢ Administratoʳˢ or Assignes, vpon the gaine & proffitt wᶜʰ god shall send by the retourne of the same voyadge (the principall Adventure thereof, & all chardge of the voyadge goode & mʳchandizes of what kinde soeuʳ both by land or water first borne & deducted[])] Soe much gaine as ffyve hundred and fyftie pounde will produce that is to saie such rate & pffitt as yf he had beene an Adventurer of the some of ffyve hundred and ffyftie pounde, & as yf he had put in soe much readie money in stocke in the said voyadge. The wᶜʰ rate and proporc̃on of proffitt is to be paid vnto him the said Phillip de Graeff his Executoʳˢ Adˢ or Assignes in such manner and forme · as the gaine and proffitt of the said voyadge shall be paid to all other the Adventurers genʳallie, vpon the some of ffyue hundred and ffyftie pounde by them adventured.

But if he happen to die before the retourne of the said shipps from the said East Indies, or those other place whither they they are directed, hauinge liued & Contynued in the said voiadge vntill the shipps, or shipp wherein he shall serue shall arriue & come to such porte in those parte, at wᶜʰ it shalbe founde fitt to lade the same : Then the said gaine p̃porcioned of the said rate of 550<sup>li</sup> aduenture to be paid to his Executoʳˢ Adˢ or Assignes, as it should haue been paid vnto him, if he had retourned wᵗʰ the said shipps. Prouided alwaies that if [he] decease before the shipps shall arriue to such porte in those pte at wᶜʰ they are to take in their ladinge. That then the moneys imprested & deliuʳed him before his goinge to Sea shalbe vnto him, in full recompence of his [p. 271] entertainem<sup>t</sup> formerlie agreed vppon for the voiadge. And vppon theis Condicõns & pviso before menc̃oed we the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie vnder o<sup>r</sup> Comon Seale, haue giuen vnto the said Phillip de Graeff this p̄nte Bill of Contract & aduenture dated the 20<sup>th</sup> day of Iune 1608 And in the yeare of the reigne of o<sup>r</sup> sou<sup>r</sup>eigne lord Iames Kinge of England ffrance & Ireland the Sixt & of Scotland the one & fforteth.

> _[Margin: The Bill of an Aduenturer of 550<sup>li</sup>, in the 4<sup>th</sup> voiadge, to an Adventurer vnder him]_

<span class="sc">Wheareas</span> Wiłłm Iennyngꬵ Citizen and             of London one of the Adventurers and one of the Brethren of the Company of Marchauntꬵ of London trading into the East Indies Hath not onelie Adventured the some of 100<sup>li</sup> vnder me Wiłłm Bonham Citizen and Vintener of London & alsoe one of the Adventurers & one of the said Company of m<sup>r</sup>chantꬵ tradinge into the East Indies in their fourth voyadge for those p̄tꬵ: But hath likewyse trulie paid the said some of 100<sup>li</sup> to me the said William Bonham as appeth by the register of the said Company the 4th of March 1607.[^sec-07-fn-065] Now knowe yee that I the said Wiłłm Bonham doe by theis p̄ntꬵ p̄myse and agree to & w<sup>th</sup> the said Wiłłm Iennyngꬵ That I the said Wiłłm Bonham my Executor<sup>rs</sup> & Administrator<sup>rs</sup> shall & will vpon the retourne of the shipps or either of them sett out by the said Company in their said 4th voyadge or w<sup>th</sup>in Convenient tyme after their said retourne in the same deliu<sup>r</sup> vnto the said Wiłłm Iennyngꬵ his Executor<sup>rs</sup> Administrator<sup>rs</sup> or Assignes a true and iust accompt and paym<sup>t</sup> of the said some of 100<sup>li</sup> soe by him adventured vnder me & of the proffitt & benefitt w<sup>ch</sup> god shall send thereof ratablelie and accordinge to the gen<sup>r</sup>all distribucõn proporcõn and allotm<sup>t</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall be allotted disposed and geven to me the said Wiłłm Bonham & to all other the seu<sup>r</sup>all Adventurers of 550<sup>li</sup> in the said fourth voyadge proporcionallie to each mans seu<sup>r</sup>all Adventure. In witnes whereof I haue herevnto sett my hand and seale the 4th day of Iulie 1608. And in the Yeare of the Reign of &c:


<!-- page: 364 | folio: 272 -->
> _[Margin: The Bill of Adventure of 550<sup>li</sup> in the fourth voyadge to an Adventurer vnder him the Bill on totherside of this leafe[^sec-07-fn-066] not being allowed.]_

<span class="sc">This</span> Bill or writeinge witnesseth That whereas I Henrie Bridgman Citizen and Leatherseller of London, Haue vndertaken to adventure as one of the Brethren & Adventurers of the Company of Marchaunte tradinge to the East Indies the some of 600<sup>li</sup> of lawfull money of England in this their p̄nte intended expedĩcõn or fourth voyadge to the East Indies in the good shipps called the Asseñcõn & the Vnion. And whereas Nicholas Skynner Citizen and Cutlar of London, & alsoe one of the Brethren of the said Company of Marchaunte trading to the said East Indies, hath alreadie trulie paid to me the said Henry Bridgman the some of 150<sup>li</sup> of like lawfull money of England being one 4<sup>th</sup> parte of the said some or stocke before mencioned, w<sup>ch</sup> said some he the said Nicholas Skinner is Contented to Adventure vnder me in the said fourth voyadge in such manner as all other Vnderadventurers haue done. Knowe ye therefore That I the said Henrie Bridgman for me my Executors and Administrators & eu<sup>r</sup>y of vs doe couenant promyse and graunte to and w<sup>th</sup> the said Nicholas Skinner his Execū & Administr & eu<sup>r</sup>y of them by theis pnte That yt shall and may be lawfull to and for the said Nicholas Skynner his Execū Administr & Ass<sup>s</sup> & eu<sup>r</sup>y of them vpon the retourne of the ships or either of them sett out in this said fourth Voyadge or w<sup>th</sup>in Convenient tyme after their said retourne in the same to haue recciue & enioye to his and their propp vse & behoofe out of my said stocke & adventure of 600<sup>li</sup> the some of One hundred and ffyftie by him the said Nicholas Skynner adventured vnder me in the said fourth voyadge as aforesaid together w<sup>th</sup>all such benefitt proffitt encrease and gaine as god shall send thereof ratablie from tyme to tyme according to the gen<sup>r</sup>all distribũcõn propor̃cõn and allotm<sup>t</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall be allotted disposed and giuen to me the said Henry Bridgman & all other the Aduenturers in the said voiadge, proportionallie to eache mans seu<sup>r</sup>all Aduenture. And furder that I the said Henrie Bridgman my execū & Ađs & eu<sup>r</sup>y of vs shall and will at all tymes & from tyme to tyme hereafter vpon reasonable request to vs or any of vs made by the said Nicholas [p. 273] Skynner his Executor<sup>s</sup> Admī or Ass<sup>s</sup> make him the said Nicholas Skynner his Execū & Admī acquainted, w<sup>th</sup> all & eu<sup>r</sup>y the proceedinge in the said voyadge, w<sup>ch</sup> shall Concerne the takeing out & receiueing of the said some of 150<sup>li</sup> w<sup>th</sup> the proffitte thereof as amplie as shall any way come to the knowledge of me the said Henrie Bridgman my Executor<sup>s</sup> and Ađs w<sup>th</sup>out fraude or guile. In witnes whereof I haue &c.

> _[Margin: A Bill of Adventure for the 4<sup>th</sup> voyadge]_
> _[Margin: The Bill of Adventure to the third voyadge.]_

WHEREAS[^sec-07-fn-067] **A B** Citizen and &c . . . . . . one of the Adventurers and one of the Brethren of the Companie of Marchaunt*e* of London tradinge into the East Indies hath not onelie sett downe for his Adventure w<sup>th</sup> the said Company to the some of 550<sup>li</sup> in their 4<sup>th</sup> voyadge to the East Indies by the Cape *Bona spei:* in the good shipps called the Assenc̃on & the Vnion But hath alsoe trulie paied the said some of 550<sup>li</sup> for his Adventure to Richard Atkinson Casheare to the said Adventurers in the 4<sup>th</sup> voyadge. We therefore the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company doe by this o<sup>r</sup> present Bill of Adventure promyse and agree to and w<sup>th</sup> the said **A B.** That we the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Comp : and o<sup>r</sup> Successor<sup>s</sup> shall and will vpon the retourne of the ships called the Assenc̃on & Vnion or either of them sett out by vs in this present fourth voyadge or w<sup>th</sup>in Convenient tyme after their said retourne in the same deliu<sup>r</sup> vnto the said **A B** ..... his Execū Administ: or Assignes atrue and iust Accompt and paym<sup>t</sup> of such stocke benefitt and proffitt of stocke as god shall send vpon the said voyadge according to the gen<sup>r</sup>all distribuc̃on pporc̃on and allotm<sup>t</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall be allotted dispôsed and given to all & eu<sup>r</sup>y the seu<sup>r</sup>all Adventurers except & alwaies reserued out of the said some or stocke before mencioned for and to thuse of the right owners of the same all such somes w<sup>ch</sup> shall in due tyme iustlie appeare to [p. 274] the said Company to be adventured vnder the said 𝕬 𝕭...... by any vnderadventurer in the said fourth voyadge togither w<sup>th</sup>all the proffitte & benefitte thereof w<sup>th</sup>out fraude or guile. In witnes whereof &c : <span class="sc">wheareas</span>[^sec-07-fn-068] 𝕴 𝕸.[^sec-07-fn-069] citizen and grocer of London one of the Adventurers & one of the Brethren of the Company of Marchaunte of London trading into the East Indies hath not onelie sett downe for his Adventure w<sup>th</sup> the said Company the some of 150 pounde in their third voyadge to the East Indies by the Cape *Bona spei*: But hath alsoe trulie paid the said some of 150<sup>li</sup> for his Adventure to Thomas ffarrington Threr of the said Company. We therefore the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company doe by this o<sup>r</sup> p̄nte Bill of Adventure p̄myse and agree to and w<sup>th</sup> the said 𝕴 𝕸. That we the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Company & o<sup>r</sup> Successo<sup>rs</sup> shall and will vpon the retourne of the shipps or any of them sett out by vs in this p̄nte third voyadge or w<sup>th</sup>in Convenient tyme after their said retourne in the same deliu<sup>r</sup> vnto the said 𝕴 𝕸. his Execū Adminī or Ass<sup>s</sup> a true and iust accompt and paym<sup>t</sup> of such stocke benefitt and [p. 275] proffitt of stocke as god shall send vpon the said voyadge according to the gen<sup>r</sup>all distribũcõn propor̃cõn and allotm<sup>t</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall be allotted disposed and giuen to all & eu<sup>r</sup>y the seu<sup>r</sup>all Adventurers in the said voyadge proporcionally to their seu<sup>r</sup>all Adventures. In witnes whereof we haue herevnto annexed o<sup>r</sup> Comon seale the 26th day of Aprill 1608. And in the yeare of the reigne of o<sup>r</sup> sou<sup>r</sup>eigne Lord kinge Iames of England ffraunce and Ireland the Sixt & of Scotland the One and fforteth.

Examined by me Thomas ffarrington

Sealed w<sup>th</sup> the Comon seale of the Companie in the pn̄te of me W<sup>m</sup> Leighton[^sec-07-fn-070] Secretarie Copia

> _[Margin: The lo: Thrers warrant to y<sup>e</sup> ffarmors for transportacon of 6000li parte of 2000li[^sec-07-fn-076] form<sup>r</sup>lie granted the Company by Patent from his matie:]_

AFTER my harty Comendačons, Whereas the Marchantes tradinge to the East Indies, by his Ma<sup>te</sup> warraunt vnder the greate Seale of England beareinge date the Eight daye of february: In the v<sup>th</sup> yeare of his highnes raigne had licence to carry foorth: 20000<sup>li</sup>: sterlinge of forreine Coyne, and havinge as yett transported onely: 14000<sup>li</sup>: Theis are to will and require yo<sup>u</sup> to suffer them to transporte the said somme in a Shippe called the Expedičon, accordinge to his Ma<sup>te</sup> pleasure, signified in the said letters pattente: And for so doinge this by vertue thereof shalbe yo<sup>r</sup> warrant: from *Whitehall:* the xj<sup>th</sup> of Aprill: 1609:

Yo<sup>r</sup> Lovinge freind *R. SALISBURY*

> _[Margin: The Coppie of his maties Comission to Capt: David Middleton ye 11th of Aprill. 1609]_

To my very lovinge freindes the officers of his Ma<sup>te</sup> Customes outwarde in the Port of London, and to eu<sup>r</sup>y of them to whome it may apperteine JAMES[^sec-07-fn-077] by the grace of God kinge of England Scotland ffraunce and Ireland defender of the faith &c: To o<sup>r</sup> trustie and welbeloued David Middleton whereas diu<sup>r</sup>s of o<sup>r</sup> loueinge Subiecte at their owne Adventures, Coste and chardge, aswell for the honor of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England, as for the increase & advancem<sup>t</sup> of trade and m<sup>r</sup>chandize, w<sup>th</sup>in the same, Haue form<sup>r</sup>lie sett forth fower voyadge to the East Indies, w<sup>th</sup> c<sup>r</sup>teine shipps and Pinnaces by way of m<sup>r</sup>chandizinge, by w<sup>ch</sup> shipps and Pinnasses they haueinge discou<sup>r</sup>ed and begunn to settle a trade in some parte of the said East Indies & their shipps beinge retourned in three of their former voyadge from thence, laden w<sup>th</sup> sundrie m<sup>r</sup>chandize brought from [p. 283] those ptę, They the said Marchauntę intendinge to feequent those Countries of the East Indies by contynueinge the trade alreadie discouʳed and begun. And indevoringe further discouʳy of trade of those partę for the more ample vent of the natiue Comodities of oʳ kingdomes And retourneing from the place of their discouʳy such necessarie comodities as shallbe of spetiall vse & benefitt both to Vs and oʳ Subiectę & haue now prepared a cʳteine shipp to the said East Indies: *A<span class="sc">nd wheareas</span>* the said Marchauntę haue chosen yoᵘ the said David Middleton, to be principall Gouʳnoʳ or Generall of all the Marchauntę, Mariners and other oʳ Subiectę wᶜʰ are or shall be shipped in the said Shipp, we gratiouslie favoringe their intended voyadge and approueinge and shallowinge of their choise of you to the same gouʳnmᵗ, beinge desierous to furnish yoᵘ wᵗʰall fitt and Convenient power and authoritie to rule and gouʳne all & euʳy our Subiectę imployed in this voyadge, by a due obedience to be by them yealded Vnto you, in the obserueinge and executeinge of all such good orders & Constitucõns as yoᵘ shall thinke Convenient to ordeine and appointe for the furtherance of the said voyadge to the honor of Vs and oʳ kingdomes, and the advancemᵗ of the said trade, *D<span class="sc">oe</span>* hereby straightlie chardge and Comand all & euʳy pson and psonns imployed vsed or shipped in this Voyadge in the said Shipp, to giue all due obedience and respect Vnto yoᵘ during the said Voyadge & to beare themselues one towardę another in all good order and quietnes for avoieding any occasion that might breede mutiny quarrells or dissençõn amongst them to the hindrance of the good successe wᶜʰ is to be hoped for by Godę providence of the said intended Voyadge *A<span class="sc">nd</span>* in default of such dutie and obedience to be pformed towardę you for the correccõn and quenchinge of all such mutiny quarrells or dissençõn that shall or may be moved by the disorder evell disposicõn or pversnes of any the said psonns, *W<span class="sc">ee doe</span>* hereby authorize you the said David Middleton duringe the said Voyadge or during soe longe tyme as yoᵘ shall lyue in the said Voyadge to chastice correct and ponish all offenders & transgressors in that behalfe accordinge to the qualitie of their offenses wᵗʰ such punnishmᵗę as are comonlie vsed in all Armies at Sea, when they are not Capitall And for Capitall offences, as wilfull murther wᶜʰ is hatefull in the sight of God, or mutinie wᶜʰ is an offence that may tende to the ouʳthrowe of the [p. 284] said Voyadge, the same being trulie and iustlie proved against any of the pson or psons aforesaid, *WE DOE* hereby giue vnto yo<sup>u</sup> the said David Middleton duringe all the tyme of the said voyadge, or during soe longe tyme as yo<sup>u</sup> shall lyve in the said Voyadge full power & authoritie to vse and putt in execucõn o<sup>r</sup> Lawe called Martiall Lawe in that behalfe: *AND THEIS* o<sup>r</sup> łres shalbe vnto you sufficient warrant and dischargdge for the doinge and executinge of all & singuler the premisses: *A<span class="sc">ND</span>* forasmuch as att this present tyme we are in amitie . w<sup>th</sup>all Christian Princes & are vnwillinge that any our Subiecte should giue occasion of breach or hindrance of that league or amitie w<sup>ch</sup> we hould w<sup>th</sup> any o<sup>r</sup> Confederate freinde or Alleys. And because we are not ignorant of the emulacõn & envy that doth accompany the discou<sup>r</sup>y of Countries and trade, & of the quarrells and Contencõns w<sup>ch</sup> doe many tymes fall out betweene the subiecte of diu<sup>r</sup>s Princes, that meete the one w<sup>th</sup> theother in forraine & farr remote Countries in the Course & psecutinge of their discou<sup>r</sup>yes, & being desierous that our subiecte should forbeare to moue or beginn any quarrell or Contencõn (Vppon the Subiecte of our Confederate freinde or Allies[]], either in their proceedinge or retourne vpon or from any of their Voyadge, *WE THERFORE* doe hereby straightlie chardge and Comand you the said David Middleton & all other vnder yo<sup>r</sup> gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> that neither in yo<sup>r</sup> voyadge outwarde or homewarde or in any Country, Island, Porte, or place where yo<sup>u</sup> shall abide or come duringe the tyme of yo<sup>r</sup> beinge abroad out of o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes or dominions where you meete w<sup>th</sup> any the Subiecte of the kinge of Spaigne or of any other o<sup>r</sup> Confederate ffreinde or Allies, or of any other Nacõn or people their Shipps Vessells Goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandize yo<sup>u</sup> doe not attempt or goe aboute to sett vpon take or supprise their psonns Ships Vessells goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes or offer any iniury or discourtesie vnto them vnlesse yo<sup>u</sup> shall be by them first therevnto iustlie provoked, or driuen either in the iust defence of yo<sup>r</sup> owne psonns yo<sup>r</sup> Shipps Vessells Goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes either by any other their disturbance or hindrance whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> in yo<sup>r</sup> quiett course of trade either for recompence or recou<sup>r</sup>y of the psonns goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandize of any o<sup>r</sup> Subiecte that are alreadie in or neare the East Indies or otherwyse for any iust cause of yo<sup>r</sup> defence, as yo<sup>u</sup> will awnsweare the contrary at yo<sup>r</sup> vttermost prills.


<!-- page: 377 | folio: 285 -->
<span class="sc">And</span> wheareas we are informed that the said David Middleton hath sould in the East Indies, Three small peece of cast Iron Ordinance contrary to the Lawes of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme, for that the same was done vpon necessitie, & for the good of the publique service, & the releefe of such as were distressed in that voyadge. *W<span class="sc">e</span>* are gratiouslie pleased to dispence w<sup>th</sup> him in that behalfe: And doe by theis presente pardon and remitt the said offence, and dischardge him the said David Middleton of and from all such penalties as by o<sup>r</sup> said Lawes may be inflicted vpon him for sellinge of the said Ordinance w<sup>th</sup>out o<sup>r</sup> licence first had and obteyned in that behalfe, Any Lawe statute or restrainte to the contrary in any wyse notw<sup>th</sup>standinge. In wittnes whereof we haue caused theis o<sup>r</sup> lres to be made Pattente: Witnes o<sup>r</sup>selfe at Westm̄ the 11<sup>th</sup> day of Aprill in the Seaventh yeare of o<sup>r</sup> Raigne of England ffraunce and Ireland, & of Scotland the Twoe and fforteth.

p̄ breve de privato sigillo:

Coppin.

> _[Margin: A Coppie of the lres sent to the ffactors at Bantam in thexpedicon by Capt : David Middleton.]_

<span class="sc">After</span>[^sec-07-fn-078] o<sup>r</sup> hartie Comendañons &c Yo<sup>r</sup> letters of the xv<sup>th</sup> of Ianuary 1607[^sec-07-fn-079] by Cornelius Matalife together w<sup>th</sup> a briefe of the state of o<sup>r</sup> busines in yo<sup>r</sup> handlinge we haue receiued: As alsoe yo<sup>r</sup> last of the xv<sup>th</sup> of Iulie[^sec-07-fn-080] by Captaine David Middleton in the Consent: w<sup>ch</sup> shipp arriued here in Ianuary last (thanke be to god) in good saffetie, laden w<sup>th</sup> Cloues to o<sup>r</sup> very good contentm<sup>te</sup>, for w<sup>ch</sup> we haue had a good price & present dispatch, Soe as we haue none remaineinge to sell: By him we alsoe receiued Henry Sydalls Iournall, wherein appeared what goode yo<sup>u</sup> sent in the said Shipp to the Molluccoes, what thereof was sould, what retorned to yo<sup>u</sup>, & of Captaine Middletons whole proceedinge in the buyinge of the said Cloues: Alsoe one other Iournall of yo<sup>r</sup> accompte touchinge [p. 286] o<sup>r</sup> busines in yo<sup>r</sup> handlinge since the same was deliu<sup>r</sup>ed over to yo<sup>u</sup> by Edmund Scott, vntill the first of Iulie last, and thereby rest satisfied w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>r</sup> due pceedinge in accompte, albeit as yett we haue not examined the same: By yo<sup>r</sup> lres we alsoe pceiue that yo<sup>u</sup> borrowed 3000 Royalls of the Dutch Marchaunte to satisfie soe much taken vp of the Captaine and Company of the said shipp to supplie o<sup>r</sup> wante, for the ladinge of the said Cloues w<sup>ch</sup> we hope vpon the arriuall of the Dragon and Hector, or by some other meanes, yo<sup>u</sup> haue dulie repaid w<sup>th</sup>all thankfullnes, assureinge them further That we will hould their said kindnes in remembraunce, and be readie to requite the same whensoeu<sup>r</sup> occasion shalbe offred: We are very sorry that there was noe better dispatch found for o<sup>r</sup> Cloth at the Molluccoes, consideringe the same is much ympaired by the longe lieinge as yo<sup>u</sup> advertice vs, But we hope that the Dragon and the Hector arriued w<sup>th</sup> you shortlie after, And that by them the same will be vented, either at Banda or the Molluccos w<sup>ch</sup> God graunte we may heare: Moreou<sup>r</sup> we trust that yo<sup>u</sup> haue vsed diligence to putt of all other the remaine of o<sup>r</sup> goode at Bantam, recouered o<sup>r</sup> debte there, and ymployed the proceede thereof, accordinge to o<sup>r</sup> lres by the said twoe shipps[^sec-07-fn-081] If not we pray yo<sup>u</sup> to hasten the same.

> _[Margin: ballance the Ac-comptes &c:]_

That thaccompt of that busines may be ballanced & to ymploy what yo<sup>u</sup> haue remaineinge [(]not inuested into pepp) in Rawe silke of China called Lamkin, like vnto that sample w<sup>ch</sup> Iohn Saris sent vnto o<sup>r</sup> Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> S<sup>r</sup> Tho: Smyth: But take heed yo<sup>u</sup> buy not of the silke that is crosse reeled, & called canton for that sorte is not here vendible.[^sec-07-fn-082]

> _[Margin: silke called Lawkin]_

The silke called Lawkin, is here well requested Therefore we pray yo<sup>u</sup> vse your best endevors to putt of o<sup>r</sup> english Cloth for that Comoditie, whereto as it seemeth by Robt Brownes lres the Chineses were willinge & desierous, if yo<sup>u</sup> had beene furnished w<sup>th</sup> any w<sup>ch</sup> giueth vs good hope that those people, will fall to weare o<sup>r</sup> Cloth, Soe as we shall finde good vent for the same hereafter, & haue better [p. 287] meanes to maintaine an ampler trade there. ffor the better procureinge whereof, we haue now and will heerafter, send such Cloth as shall be true, both in substaunce and Couller, and soe yo<sup>u</sup> may assure them Moreou<sup>r</sup> we Vnderstand by m<sup>r</sup> Brownes letter that a trade may be had to *Siquedana*,[^sec-07-fn-083] for Diamonde whereof we would be glad to tast, and doe approue of his diligence in that and other adv<sup>r</sup>tisem<sup>te</sup>.

> _[Margin: Diamondes Bezar stones &ca:]_
> _[Margin: Indico]_

We hope that the Dragon and Hector arriued w<sup>th</sup> you in Convenient tyme, and that yo<sup>u</sup> haue pceeded, to buy some Diamonde, Bezar stones, Muske & other Comodities (whereof hitherto we haue had none) according to o<sup>r</sup> Comission, and lres sent by o<sup>r</sup> Generall m<sup>r</sup> W<sup>m</sup> : Keelinge, for w<sup>ch</sup> purpose we sent m<sup>r</sup> Marlowe a Ieweller to goe to such place for the buyinge thereof, as yo<sup>u</sup> should direct him : And yf neither m<sup>r</sup> Keelinge, nor m<sup>r</sup> Sharpie, haue entred into the trade of Cambaio, *Surat* or some other place of the maine, Then we would haue yo<sup>u</sup> to informe yo<sup>r</sup> selues howe strangers are intertayned at Suratt & Cambaio : And beinge imbouldenned by their aduise we wish yo<sup>u</sup> to appointe twoe of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors such as yo<sup>u</sup> shall thinke fitt to goe passengers in some Iuncke or other shippinge of that Country to Surat & Cambaia w<sup>th</sup> such stocke as yo<sup>u</sup> thinke good, to beare chardge to and againe to buy such Comodities as they shall finde there as Indico, of Laher,[^sec-07-fn-084] here worth viij<sup>s</sup> the pounde *Serchis*[^sec-07-fn-085] and the best *Belondri*[^sec-07-fn-086] worth v<sup>s</sup> the pounde the Courser sorte [p. 288] will not requite the chardge and such other Comodities as they shall finde theare: Alsoe we would haue yo<sup>u</sup> procure the best favor yo<sup>u</sup> can w<sup>th</sup> the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and other principall men of each place, yo<sup>u</sup> come to, whereby yo<sup>u</sup> may be able to enforme vs what hope we may haue of trade heereafter to such place, and yo<sup>u</sup> learne what Comodities of o<sup>rs</sup>, kinde, sorte, & Cullo<sup>rs</sup> will vent there, as namelie what Clothes, karsies ppetuanoes or other woollen Comodities & what Cullo<sup>rs</sup> are in best and worse request leade, Tynn, Iron, steele, muskette, Calliuers,[^sec-07-fn-087] Dagge,[^sec-07-fn-088] swordblade, headpeece, &c: and alsoe what Commodities they finde there fitt to serue for the Molluccos or other easterne pte, or to bringe home for England w<sup>th</sup> such other informac̃ons as experience there shall enable yo<sup>u</sup> w<sup>th</sup>: Alsoe to send them to any other Citties or places of cheefest trade in those parte, & there to learne the matters before mentioned, and not to lie still at Bantam as yf yo<sup>u</sup> were tyed and bound to that Towne onelie.

> _[Margin: <span class="sc">Thomas Emmesworth</span>]_
> _[Margin: spices from Banda &c]_

we haue sent in this Ship a younge man one Thomas Emmesworth[^sec-07-fn-089] a man of good reputac̃on, and soe we wish yo<sup>u</sup> to accompt of him, whoe hath beene brought vp some tyme in Turkey and hath verie good skill in *Indico*, of all sorte of silke, & other Comodities vsuallie bought in Turkey, whose advise therein we wish yo<sup>u</sup> to followe Alsoe we haue sent in this Shipp three other servaunte, whoe albeit they haue place in the shipp: (Viz) Richard Wooddis[^sec-07-fn-090] pursar, Sophony Cosuke[^sec-07-fn-091] pursers mate, & Edward Nettles[^sec-07-fn-092] Steward, yett we haue interteyned [p. 289] them to serue vs vij yeares, there w<sup>th</sup> you, & would haue them ymployed in o<sup>r</sup> busines & such other p̱sonns, as yo<sup>u</sup> shall thinke fitt sent backe in the shipp in their place. ffurther we pray yo<sup>u</sup> to Consider w<sup>th</sup> your selues & thereof w<sup>th</sup> the next, advise vs, if it be not more convenient to procure Cloues, Nutmegge, mace, Synamon, Camfere, Benianyn, S[^sec-07-fn-093] redd & yellow to be brought from the molloccos, Banda & other places in Iuncke of Bantam, & other the Islande, to yo<sup>u</sup>, & yo<sup>u</sup> thereto by[^sec-07-fn-094] them, & lay the same in yo<sup>r</sup> warehowse, to be reddie Clensed & fitted for o<sup>r</sup> shipps, when they shall theare arive, Then[^sec-07-fn-095] to send o<sup>r</sup> ships to the places to fetch them, In w<sup>ch</sup> Considerac̃on yo<sup>u</sup> are to remember, to thinke on the price they may be had at, beinge soe brought to Bantam of the Custome and chardge there, of the saffetie of the place, from the invasion of the Portugalls w<sup>ch</sup> yt is thought they will assaye by Comand of the kinge of Spaigne (haueing now peace w<sup>th</sup> the Hollenders[^sec-07-fn-096]) wherew<sup>th</sup> yt shall not be amisse to acquainte that kinge, that he may endevor to prevent yt : We thinke yf this could be brought to passe much hazard of o<sup>r</sup> shipps and men in comeinge to those parte may be prevented, o<sup>r</sup> voyadge shortened, to o<sup>r</sup> greate ease in victualls and mens wages, & the people of the Country better Contented in that their meanes of liveinge is not taken from them, for w<sup>ch</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> write they hate the Hollenders and much bewaile their owne hindrance. And as yo<sup>u</sup> haue sent vs a Iournall of yo<sup>r</sup> accompte, we desire in like manner to haue a Iournall p̱fectlie drawen out, and sent vs by this shipp of all o<sup>r</sup> busines, as the same hath beene passed there, from S<sup>r</sup> Iames Lancasters comeinge thence, vntill the begininge of yo<sup>r</sup> chardge, aswell of William Starkey his accompte, w<sup>th</sup> the ballance thereof, deliuered to Edmund Scott, As alsoe a p̱fect Iournall of Edmund Scotte accompte, and the ballance thereof deliu<sup>r</sup>ed over to Gabriell Towerson & the same carefullie pvsed, That entrance thereof may be made into o<sup>r</sup> Booke accordinglie.


<!-- page: 382 | folio: 290 -->
> _[Margin: money and goodes sent by Capt: David Middleton.]_
> _[Margin: This voyadge to be a particular acct : aparte from the rest &c :]_

Nowe yo<sup>u</sup> shall vnderstand that vpon the hopes we haue of better and more ample trade in those parte: we haue resolued yearelie by Gode pmission and help, to send some shippinge vnto yo<sup>u</sup>: and for that cause not being fitted w<sup>th</sup> a better at this present haue furnished and sent out this o<sup>r</sup> shipp called the Expedic̃on of the burthen of 240 tonnes, whereof Edmund Musgraue is m<sup>r</sup> and Iohn Davies[^sec-07-fn-097] Pilott, And therein haue laden 13 ballette cont 41 Clo: 40 devonshire karsayes. 12 hamshire ke. 10 Northerne karseys: & 46 tonns of Iron the nomber sorte Cullers and prices, being expressed in the Invoise hereinclosed, alsoe Chests Cont Royalls of 8. All w<sup>ch</sup> money and goode we haue appointed Captaine David Middleton w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>r</sup> Councell, advise, and assistaunce to make sale of, and ymploy for vs, either at the Molloccos, *Banda*, *Bantam*, or els wheare, as in his & yo<sup>r</sup> discrec̃ons shall seeme fitt for o<sup>r</sup> most benefitt, Consideringe what sorte and quantities of those East Indian m<sup>r</sup>chandize our other shipps haue laden there whome we haue appointed cheefe Comander in the said Shipp, and for whose assistaunce we would haue the aforesaid Thomas Emmesworth Henry Sydall and Augustine Spaldinge to accompany & assist him, for the better pformance of the ladinge thereof, either at the Molluccos Banda or ellswhere, as yo<sup>u</sup> shall resolue: And the said Emseworth or Siddall to write and send vs a pfect accompt, of the whole pceedinge therein, and this further we advise yo<sup>u</sup>, That [p. 291] whatsoeur shall be either sould or bought for this shipps ladinge must be done as a pticular stocke a pte from the rest of o<sup>r</sup> busines Soe as yf there be any Cause to vse any of o<sup>r</sup> goode w<sup>ch</sup> are there belonginge to o<sup>r</sup> generall accompt the same is to be deliuered to this stocke, by weight, measure, or tale, And the same Valewed as yt is there worth: In like manner yf any thinge of the goode sent in this Shipp shall be left ther vnsould, the same in like case to be valued as yt is there then worth, & a note of all the said quantities & valua<span class="sc">c</span>õns to be sent to vs by this Shipp, That o<sup>r</sup> accompte there may be rightlie chardged therewith and a due repti<span class="sc">c</span>õn made accordinglie: And for that we vnderstand Augustine Spaldinge behaueth him selfe both honestlie and dilligentlie in matters comitted to his chardge for o<sup>r</sup> occasions, we are contented to increase his wages from what he formerlie had, to xl<sup>s</sup> p monneth (yf he be liueinge) The same wages to beginn at the arriuall of this Shipp att Bantam, not doubtinge but that in his honest and faithfull carriadge towarde vs, he will deserue the same.

> _[Margin: Tho : Hemsworth.]_

ffurther concerninge Thomas Emmseworth o<sup>r</sup> desire is that the shipp beinge laden and retourned from the Molluccoes Banda or elswheare to Bantam: That he stay w<sup>th</sup> you in o<sup>r</sup> howse there, and take chardge of the passinge of o<sup>r</sup> busines to accompt, being assisted and acquainted w<sup>th</sup> the manner of m<sup>r</sup>chandizeinge there, by some of you best acquainted therewith: And that yearelie we may receiue a true Iournall of what hath passed in o<sup>r</sup> affaires there, by you, Soe as we may knowe trulie the pfect state thereof: we have alsoe sent you herewith, the Coppies of o<sup>r</sup> <span class="sc">l</span>res formerlie sent you, aswell by m<sup>r</sup> Keelinge, as by m<sup>r</sup> Sharpey o<sup>r</sup> twoe Generalls in the third and fourth Voyadge: And we wish you, That yf you cann, you doe lade and send vs any other Comodities rather then pepp, Yett rather then the shipp shall wante or retourne w<sup>th</sup>out ladinge, Then to send vs some pepp. w<sup>ch</sup> is more at lardge specified in o<sup>r</sup> Comission for the Captaine.

Lastlie forasmuch as we haue vnderstoode, That Gabriell Towerson hath a greate desier to retourne home, we are Contented that he soe doe: hopinge that he hath not soe lightlie reguarded the trust reposed in him, That he would abandon the [p. 292] place, before o<sup>r</sup> leaue and direccõn, neither doe we thinke that any of yo<sup>u</sup> all will soe lightlie reguard either yo<sup>r</sup> reputacõn in the world, or yo<sup>r</sup> Creditt w<sup>th</sup> vs, That yo<sup>u</sup> will leaue yo<sup>r</sup> place of ymployment, before we giue o<sup>r</sup> Consent, The like leaue we alsoe giue to Henry Siddall to returne for England, if he may be spared, wherein we wish you to haue reguard to keepe a convenient nomber in o<sup>r</sup> howse both for the defence of yo<sup>r</sup> selues and o<sup>r</sup> goode, as to giue releefe and supplie to such ffactories, as haue beene setled by m<sup>r</sup> William Keelinge in any other place thereaboute: And whereas we finde by yo<sup>r</sup> accompte, That yo<sup>u</sup> receiue yo<sup>r</sup> sallarie or wages at iiij<sup>s</sup> the Ryall of : 8 : and soe pay yo<sup>r</sup> selues, we haue thought good to lett yo<sup>u</sup> knowe that we pay for the same 4<sup>s</sup> 7<sup>d</sup> beside the adventure thither: wherefore we thinke yt fitt That yf yo<sup>u</sup> receiue yo<sup>r</sup> wages there fforasmuch as we Vnderstand that they are worth there : 8<sup>s</sup>: That yo<sup>u</sup> sett them at such an indifferent rate as may neither be too lowe for vs, nor too high for yo<sup>r</sup> selues, whereof by yo<sup>r</sup> next letters we desire to receiue some satisfaccõn: *Alsoe* we vnderstand that yo<sup>u</sup> make greate benefitt by Casshes and dealinge there w<sup>th</sup> other Comodities & yett we finde nothinge putt to o<sup>r</sup> accompte in that respect.

Wherefore we could wish and hereby requier yo<sup>u</sup>, That such a course may be taken w<sup>th</sup> the stocke that remaines in yo<sup>r</sup> hande from tyme to tyme, That thereby a proffitt may be made thereof towarde the greate chardge of howsekeepinge & otherwyse expended there: whereof we make noe doubte but yo<sup>u</sup> will be carefull, And soe Comitt yo<sup>u</sup> to the proteccõn of Thalmightie. London the xv<sup>th</sup> of Aprill 1609

Yo<sup>r</sup> loueinge freinde Thomas Smyth William Romeny William Greenwell Robert Bell Robert Middleton W<sup>m</sup>: Cater Iohn Busbridge.


<!-- page: 385 | folio: 293 -->
Edmond Scott and George Scott Citizens and grocers of London bound vnto S<sup>r</sup> Tho : Smyth of London knight in 500<sup>li</sup> to be paid vnto him, or his certeine Atturney, Executors or Administrators ad vsum Gubnator et Societatis m<sup>r</sup>cator Londinensiū ad Indias Orientales negotiantiū. That the said Edmond Scott his Executors Administrators & Assignes doe stand to the arbitram<sup>t</sup> of those mentioned in this Condic̃on of awarde : And S<sup>r</sup> Tho : Smyth bound in the like some That the w<sup>th</sup>in named Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Company of m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London tradinge into theast Indies & their Successors shall doe the like.[^sec-07-fn-098]


![Decorative drop capital T.](../figures/fig-016_p0385.webp)

> _[Margin: The bond of award betweene the Companie & Edmond Scott. 1609.]_

THE Condic̃on of this Obligac̃on is such That yf &c : shall at all tymes heereafter stand to, abide, obay obserue pforme, fulfill, & keepe the award, arbitram<sup>t</sup>, order, determinac̃on & Iudgm<sup>t</sup> of Robt Middleton, Robert Iohnson, Raphe ffreeman and Christopher Cletherowe Citizens & m<sup>r</sup>chaunte of London, Arbitrators indifferently named elected & chosen aswell on the pte and behalfe of &c : as on the pte of &c : to arbitrate awarde deeme & iudge betweene the said &c : and the said &c : for touchinge & conc'ninge all accompte Reckonninge debte debate and demande whatsoeur now dependinge betweene the said &c : & the said &c : Except all such seu<sup>r</sup>all Adventures & stocke as the said Edmond hath here adventured w<sup>th</sup> the said Company & the proffitte thereof: Soe as the same awarde determinac̃on & Iudgm<sup>t</sup> of the said Arbitrators be made & yealded vp in writeinge vnder their hande & seales on this side or before the 24<sup>th</sup> day of Iulie next ensueinge the date of this present Obligac̃on w<sup>th</sup>out fraude or covyn. That then this present Obligac̃on shalbe &c : Or ells &c :

The w<sup>ch</sup> are as ffolloweth. Viz to.—
