And for a demonstrac̃on of o<sup>r</sup> favorable inclynation towarde yo<sup>u</sup>, and embraceinge of yo<sup>r</sup> loue & freindshipp, wee haue sent yo<sup>u</sup> atoken by o<sup>r</sup> servant S<sup>r</sup> Henrie Middleton knight, Generall of this o<sup>r</sup> voyadge, w<sup>ch</sup> wee pray yo<sup>u</sup> to accept in good parte, and to hono<sup>r</sup> and respect him accordinge to the quallity of his place. Given at o<sup>r</sup> Pallace of Westminst<sup>r</sup> this &c:

> _[Margin: A warrant for transportacon of 300li into Irel :]_

AFTER[^sec-08-fn-095] my hartie Comendac̃ons wheras the Companye of m<sup>r</sup>chante trading to the *East Indyes*, being now buylding a Shippe in *Ireland*, and hauing occasion to vse some readye monye, for prouiding of sundrie thinge ther, necessarye for the finishing of the said shippe haue made suite for lycense to transport from hence, the some of Thre hundred pounde sterling, Theis are therfore to wyll and require y<sup>u</sup> to suffer any [p. 356] p̄sons aucthorized by thē to shippe forth the said some of Thre hundred pounde. Prouided that y<sup>u</sup> take bond for deliu<sup>r</sup>ye of the said mony in *Ireland*, ther to be employed as aforesaid. And for so doing this (being grounded vppō his ma<sup>te</sup> warrant vnto me in that behalf) shalbe yo<sup>r</sup> sufficyent discharge. ffrom *Whitehall* the 4 of Octob̄r 1610.

Yo<sup>r</sup> louing friend

To my louinge friende, the *R* <span class="sc">Salisberye</span>

> _[Margin: A Commyssion from his Mat<sup>ie</sup> to S<sup>r</sup> Henry M<sub>y</sub> ddleton knight]_

JAMES,[^sec-08-fn-096] by the grace of God, king of *England*, *Fraunce* and *Ireland*, defend<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c. TO our trustye and welbeloued seru<sup>a</sup>nt *Henry Myddleton* knight, Greting. WHERAS, dyuers of o<sup>r</sup> louing subiecte, by the name of the *Gouerno<sup>r</sup> and Companye of Marchants of London trading into the East Indyes*, at ther owne aduentures, coste and charge, for the hono<sup>r</sup> of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of *England*, and for the encrease and aduauncement of trade, and m<sup>r</sup>chandize w<sup>th</sup>in the same, haue set forth sundrie voyage to the *East Indies*, and alreadye discouered and begunne to settle a trade into those parte, and intending the contynuinge therof, aswell by frequenting those place alreadye setled, as by furth<sup>r</sup> discouerye of other parte, w<sup>ch</sup> may be fitt for the enterchaunging of the Comōdityes of our kingdomes, w<sup>th</sup> the Comōdityes of those place, such as may be of spīall vse and benefitte to vs and o<sup>r</sup> subiecte, hauing to this purpose now p<sup>r</sup>pared and sett forth thre Shippes to the said *East Indyes*, and the place adioyning therunto AND WHERAS our said Subiecte the Aduenturer<sup>s</sup> of those voyage, haue chosen y<sup>u</sup>, our said seru<sup>a</sup>nt *Henry Myddleton* knight, to be y<sup>e</sup> principall Gouerno<sup>r</sup> or Generall of all the m<sup>r</sup>chante, maryners and oth<sup>r</sup> our Subiecte, w<sup>ch</sup> are or shalbe shipped in the said thre Shippes, WE graciouslye fauouring the<sup>r</sup> intended voyage, and approuinge and allowinge of [p. 357] ther choice of y<sup>u</sup> to the same gouernm<sup>t</sup>, being wylling to furnishe y<sup>u</sup> w<sup>th</sup> all fitt and conuenyent power and aucthoritye, to rule & gouerne all and euerye our Subiecte, employed in this voyage, by a due obedyence to be by them yeilded vnto yo<sup>u</sup> in the obseruinge and executing of all such good orders, and constitucõns, as y<sup>u</sup> shall thinke conuenyent to ordeine and make for the furtheraunce of y<sup>e</sup> said voiage according to such pticler direccõns and enstruccõns, as y<sup>u</sup> shall receiue from y<sup>e</sup> said Gouerno<sup>r</sup> and Companye of m<sup>r</sup>chante, the Aduenturers in this voyage, Straightlye charging and comãunding all and euerye pson or psons employed in this voyage, and shipped in the said thre Shippes, to giue all due obedyence and respect vnto y<sup>u</sup> during the said voyage, and to beare themselues one towarde anoth<sup>r</sup> in good ord<sup>r</sup> and quyetnes for auoyding any occasion that might breede mutinye, quarrells or dissencoñ amongst them, to the hinderaunce of the good successe, w<sup>ch</sup> is to be hoped for by Gode prouidence of this said voyage. AND in default of such duitie and obedyence to be pfourmed towarde y<sup>u</sup>, for the correcting and quenching of all such mutinyes, quarrells or dissencons̃ that may arise, by the euyll and disorderlye disposicoñ of any pson whatsoeuer, WE do herbye aucthorize y<sup>u</sup> our said seruãnt *Henry Middleton* knight during the said voyage, or during so long tyme as y<sup>u</sup> shall liue in the said voyage, to chastice correct and punishe all Offendo<sup>rs</sup> and transgressors in that behalf according to the qualitye of ther offences, w<sup>th</sup> such punishm<sup>te</sup> as are com̃onlye vsed in all Armyes at Sea, when they are not Capitall. AND for Capitall offence as wilfull murth<sup>r</sup>, w<sup>ch</sup> is hatefull in the sight of god, or mutinye w<sup>ch</sup> is an offence w<sup>ch</sup> may tend to the ouerthrowe of the said voyage, the same being dulye and iustlye proued against any of the pson or psons aforesaid. WE do herby giue vnto y<sup>u</sup> o<sup>r</sup> said seruãnt *Henry Myddleton* knight, during all the tyme of the said voyage, or during so long tyme as y<sup>u</sup> shall liue in the said voyage, full power and aucthoritye to vse and put in execuc̃on our lawe, called Lawe Marciall in that behalf, And these our łres shalbe vnto y<sup>u</sup> sufficyent warrant and discharge, for the doing and executing of all and singłer the p<sup>r</sup>misses. AND forasmuch as at this p<sup>r</sup>sent tyme, we are in amitye w<sup>th</sup> all Christian Princes, and are vnwylling that any o<sup>r</sup> Subiecte should giue occasion of breach or [p. 358] hinderaunce therof towardę any o<sup>r</sup> Confederates friendę or Allyes, And because we are not ignoraunt of the emulac̃on and enuye w<sup>ch</sup> doth accompanye the discouerye of Countryes and trades, and of the quarrells and contenc̃ons w<sup>ch</sup> do many tymes fall out betwene the Subiectę of dyuers Princes when they mete the one w<sup>th</sup> the oth<sup>r</sup> in forreigne and farre remote Countryes in prosecuting the course of the<sup>r</sup> discoueries, and being desirous that our Subiectę should forbeare to moue or beginne any quarrell or contenc̃on vppō the Subiectę of o<sup>r</sup> Confederates friendę or Allies, eith<sup>r</sup> in ther going forth or retourning from any of ther voyage WE THERFORE do hereby e straightlye charge and com̃aund y<sup>u</sup> o<sup>r</sup> said seru<sup>a</sup>nt *Henrye Myddleton* knight, and all other vnder yo<sup>r</sup> gouernm<sup>t</sup>, that neith<sup>r</sup> in yo<sup>r</sup> voyage outward or homeward, or in any Countrye, Island, Port or place, wher y<sup>u</sup> shall abyde or come, during the tyme of yo<sup>r</sup> being abroad, out of o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes or domynions, wher y<sup>u</sup> meete w<sup>th</sup> any the Subiectę of y<sup>e</sup> king of *Spaine*, or of any oth<sup>r</sup> o<sup>r</sup> Confederates, friendę, or Allies, or of any other nac̃on or people, ther Shippes, Vessells, goodę or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes, y<sup>u</sup> do not attempt or go about to sett vppō, take or surprize their ꝑsons, Shippes, vessells, goodę or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes, or offer any iniurye or discourtesye vnto them, as y<sup>u</sup> wyll aunswer the contrarye, at yo<sup>r</sup> vtt<sup>r</sup>most ꝑills. Except y<sup>u</sup> shalbe by them first therunto iustlye ꝑuoked or driuē, eith<sup>r</sup> in the iust defence of yo<sup>r</sup> owne ꝑsons, Shippes, vessells, goodę or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes, by any ther disturbaunce or hinderaunce w<sup>t</sup>soeu<sup>r</sup> in yo<sup>r</sup> quyett course of trade, or for recompence and recou<sup>r</sup>ye of the ꝑsons, Shippes, goodę or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes of any o<sup>r</sup> Subiectę, that are alreadye in or neare the *East Indyes*, or for any oth<sup>r</sup> iust cause of yo<sup>r</sup> defence, In w<sup>ch</sup> cases so excepted, if y<sup>u</sup> attempt, surprize, and take the ꝑsons, Shippes and goodę of any Prince or State, by whose Subiectę y<sup>u</sup> shall susteine any wrong, or losse in manner as aforesaid, y<sup>u</sup> shall not for any such acte or actę, grounded vppō the occasions aboue menc̃oned, be in daung<sup>r</sup> or subiect to the ꝑill and penalties of o<sup>r</sup> lawes, Alwayes ꝑsupposing and so requiring y<sup>u</sup> to vse all possible endeuo<sup>rs</sup> by all meanes whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>, to suffer no spoile to be made of any goodę or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes, nor imbeaseling of any thing whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> that shalbe recou<sup>r</sup>ed by y<sup>u</sup>, but to see thē saufelye brought home w<sup>th</sup> ther Bylles of lading and Chart<sup>r</sup> pties, to the intent that [p. 359] there may be restitucõn made by vs, so soone as y<sup>u</sup> shall receiue satisfaccõn from that State or people, by whome y<sup>u</sup> are dampnifyed of what Natiō soeuer. AND forasmuch as o<sup>r</sup> said Subiectę the m<sup>r</sup>chantę and oth<sup>r</sup> the Aduenturer<sup>s</sup> of this voyadge, out of prouydence and foresight yf any mortalitye eith<sup>r</sup> by sicknes or otherwise (w<sup>ch</sup> God forbyd) should befall vnto o<sup>r</sup> seru<sup>a</sup>nt *Henry Myddleton* knight, haue made choise of o<sup>r</sup> trustie and louing subiecte Cap<sup>n</sup><sup>e</sup> *Nichās Dounton*, to succeede the said *Henry Myddleton* knight, in the charge and com̄aund of principall Gouerno<sup>r</sup> or Gen<sup>r</sup>all of all the ꝑsons employed in this voyage as aforesaid WE do alsoe (in case such an accydent should happen) allowe and approue of ther choyce in that behalf, And do herby giue full power and aucthoritye to the said Cap<sup>n</sup><sup>e</sup> *Nichās Dounton*, to do and execute all and euerye thing, incydent to the charge of principall Gouerno<sup>r</sup> or Generall of all the ꝑsons employed in this voyage as aforesaid in as ample manner and forme, and to all intentę and purposes, as is before com̄ytted and imposed vppō our Seru<sup>a</sup>nt *Henrye Mydleton* knight, And these o<sup>r</sup> łres shalbe also sufficyent warrant and discharge to the said Cap<sup>n</sup><sup>e</sup> *Nichās Dounton*, for the doing and executing of all and singuler the p<sup>r</sup>misses as afores<sup>d</sup>. IN WYTNES wherof we haue caused these o<sup>r</sup> łres to be made Patentę. WITNES our self at Westm̄ the seauententh day of March in the seauenth yeare of our Raigne of *England*, *Fraunce* and *Ireland*, and of *Scotland* the thre and forteth *per breue de priuato Sigillo.* COPPIN.

> _[Margin: A Commyssion from his Matie vnto Anth : Hippon Capne.]_

JAMES,[^sec-08-fn-097] by the grace of God, king of England, Scotland, ffraunce and Ireland, defend<sup>r</sup> of the faith &c TO OUR trustye and welbeloued *Anthonye Hippon*,[^sec-08-fn-098] greting, WHERAS dyuers of our louing subiectę, by the name of the Gouern<sup>r</sup> and Companye of m<sup>r</sup>chantę of [p. 360] Londō, trading into the *East Indyes*, at ther owne aduentures coste and charges, for the hono<sup>r</sup> of this o<sup>r</sup> Realme of England, and for the encrease and aduancem<sup>t</sup> of trade, and m<sup>r</sup>chandize w<sup>th</sup>in the same, haue set forth sundrie voyage to the *East Indyes*, and alreadye discouered, and begunne to settle a trade into those parte, and intending the contynuinge therof, aswell by frequenting those pte alreadie setled, as by furth<sup>r</sup> discouerye of oth<sup>r</sup> pte w<sup>ch</sup> may be fitt, for ent<sup>r</sup>chaunging of the Com̃odityes of o<sup>r</sup> kingdomes, w<sup>th</sup> the com̃odityes of those place, such as may be of speciall vse and benefitte to vs and o<sup>r</sup> subiecte, hauing to this purpose now p<sup>r</sup>pared and sett forth the good Shippe called the *Globe*, AND wheras our said subiecte, the Aduenturer<sup>s</sup> of those voyage, haue chosen y<sup>u</sup> the said *Anthonye Hippō*, to be Gouerno<sup>r</sup> or Captaine of all the m<sup>r</sup>chante, maryners, and all oth<sup>rs</sup>, as well our Subiecte, as of what Natiō soeu<sup>r</sup> that shall goe in the said Shippe, we graciouslye fauouring the intended voyage, and approuing and allowing of ther choyce of y<sup>u</sup> to the same gouernm<sup>t</sup>, being wylling to furnishe y<sup>u</sup> w<sup>th</sup> all fytt and conuenyent power & aucthoritye, to rule and gouerne all and euerye our Subiecte and others whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>, employed in this voyage by a due obedyence to be by thē yeilded vnto y<sup>u</sup> in the obseruing and executing of all such good orders and constitucõns as y<sup>u</sup> shall thinke conuenyent to ordeine and make for the furtheraunce of the said voyage, according to such pticłer direccõns and enstruccõns as y<sup>u</sup> shall receiue from the said Gouerno<sup>r</sup> and Companye of m<sup>r</sup>chante the Aduenturer<sup>s</sup> in this voyage, Straightlye charging and com̃aunding all and eu<sup>r</sup>ye pson and psons employed in this voyage, and shipped in the said Shippe to giue all due obedyence and respect vnto y<sup>u</sup>, during the said voyage, And to beare themselues one towarde anoth<sup>r</sup> in good order and quietnes, for auoyding any occasion that might breede mutinye, quarrells or dissençõns amongst thē to the hinderaunce of the good successe, w<sup>ch</sup> is to be hoped for, by gode puidence of this said voyage AND in default of such duitye and obedyence to be pfourmed towarde y<sup>u</sup>, for the correcting and quenching of all such mutinyes, quarrells and dissençõns, that may arise by the euyll and disorderlye disposic̃on of any pson whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>, we do herbye [p. 361] aucthorize y<sup>u</sup>, our said subiect *Anthonye Hippon*, during the said voyage, or during so long tyme as y<sup>u</sup> shall lyue in the said voyage, to chastize correct and punishe all offend<sup>rs</sup> and transgressor<sup>s</sup> in that behalf according to the qualitye of ther offence; w<sup>th</sup> such punishm<sup>te</sup> as are com̄onlye vsed in all armyes at Sea, when they are not capitall, And for Capitall offence, or[^sec-08-fn-099] wilfull murth<sup>r</sup>, (w<sup>ch</sup> is hatefull in the sight of god) or mutynie, (w<sup>ch</sup> is an offence which may tend to the ouerthrowe of the said voyadge) the same being iustlye and dulye proued, against any of the pson or psons aforesaid WEE do hereby giue vnto y<sup>u</sup> o<sup>r</sup> said subiect *Anthonye Hippon*, during all the tyme of the said voyage, or during so long tyme, as y<sup>u</sup> shall lyue in the said voyage, full power and aucthoritye to vse and put in execuc̃on our Lawe called Lawe Martiall in that behalf, and these o<sup>r</sup> łres shalbe yo<sup>r</sup> sufficyent warrant, and discharge for the doing and executing all and singłer the p<sup>r</sup>misses. AND forasmuch as at this pn̄t tyme we are in Amitye w<sup>th</sup> all xpian prince, and are vnwylling that any o<sup>r</sup> Subiecte, should giue occasiō of breach or hinderaunce therof, towarde any o<sup>r</sup> confederate, friende or allyes, And because y<sup>u</sup>[^sec-08-fn-100] are not ignoraunt of the emulac̃on and enuye w<sup>ch</sup> doth accompanye the discouerye of Countryes, and Trades, and of the quarrells and contenc̃ons w<sup>ch</sup> do many tymes fall out betwene the Subiecte of dyuers Prince when they meete the one w<sup>th</sup> the oth<sup>r</sup> in forreigne and farre remote Countryes, in psecuting the course of ther discoueryes; and being desirous that o<sup>r</sup> Subiecte should forbeare or[^sec-08-fn-101] beginne to[^sec-08-fn-101] moue any quarrells or contenc̃ons, vppō the subiecte of o<sup>r</sup> confederate, friende or allyes, eith<sup>r</sup> in ther going forth or retourning from any the voyage WEE therfore do straightlye charge and com̄aund y<sup>u</sup>, o<sup>r</sup> said subiect *Anthonye Hippon*, and all oth<sup>r</sup> vnder yo<sup>r</sup> gouernm<sup>t</sup>, That neith<sup>r</sup> in yo<sup>r</sup> voyage outward or homeward, or in any Countrye, Island, Port or place, wher y<sup>u</sup> shall abide or come during the tyme of yo<sup>r</sup> being abroad out of o<sup>r</sup> kingdome or domynions, wher y<sup>u</sup> meete w<sup>th</sup> any the Subiecte of the king of *Spayne*, or of any oth<sup>r</sup> o<sup>r</sup> Confederates, friende or Allyes, or of any oth<sup>r</sup> Natiō or people, ther shippes, vessells, goode or m<sup>r</sup>chandizes, yow do not attempt or [p. 362] go about to sett vppō, take or surprize, ther psons, shippes, vessells, goode or mʳchandizes, or offer any Iniurye or discourtesye vnto thē, as yᵘ wyll aunswer the contrarye at yoʳ vttermost pills Except yᵘ shalbe by them first therunto puoked or drawne, eithʳ in the iust defence of yoʳ owne psons, shippes, vessells, goode or mʳchandize, by any their disturbaunce or hinderaunce wᵗsoeuʳ in yoʳ quiett course of trade, or for recompence, and recouerye of yᵉ psons, shippes, goode, or mʳchandizes of any oʳ Subiecte that are alreadie in or neare the *East Indyes*, Or for any othʳ iust cause of yoʳ defence, In wᶜʰ causes so excepted, if yᵘ attempt, surprize and take, the psons shippes and goode of any Prince or State, by whose Subiecte yᵘ shall susteyne, any wrong or losse in manner as aforesaid, yᵘ shall not for any such Act or Acte, (grounded vppō the occasions aboue menčōned,) be in daungʳ or subiect to the pill and penaltyes of oʳ Lawes, Alwayes pʳsupposing, and so requiring yᵘ to vse all possible endeuoʳˢ by all meanes whatsoeuʳ, to suffer no spoyle to be made, of any goode or mʳchandizes nor embezzilling of any goode whatsoeuʳ that shalbe recouʳed by yᵘ, But to see them saufelye brought home, wᵗʰ ther bylles of lading, and Chartʳ pties, to the intent that there may be restitučōn made by vs so soone as yᵘ shall receyue satisfaccōn from that State or people, by whome yᵘ are dampnifyed, of what Natiō soeuʳ AND forasmuch as oʳ said Subiecte, the mʳchante and other the Aduenturerˢ of this voyage, out of prouydence and foresight of any mortalitye, eithʳ by sicknes or otherwise, wᶜʰ god forbyd should befall, vnto our Subiect *Anthonye Hyppon*, haue made choyce of oʳ trustie and welbeloued Subiect *Robert Browne*,[^sec-08-fn-102] to succede the said *Anthonye Hyppon* in yᵉ charge and com̄aund of Gouernoʳ and Captaine of all the psons employed in this voyage WEE do also in case such an accydent should happē allowe and approue of ther choyce in that behalf, And do herby giue full power and auchoritye to the said *Robert Browne*, to do and execute all and euerye thing incydent to the charge of Gouernoʳ and Capⁿᵉ of all the psons employed in this voyage, as aforesaid, in as ample manner and forme, vnto all intente and purposes, as is before com̄ytted and imposed vppō oʳ Subiect *Anthonye Hyppon*, And [p. 363] these o<sup>r</sup> łres shalbe also a suffycyent warrant and discharge to the said *Robert Browne*, for y<sup>e</sup> doing and executing of all and singłer the p<sup>r</sup>misses as aforesaid IN WYTN̄ES whereof, we haue caused these o<sup>r</sup> łres to be made Patenṯe, WYTN̄ES our self at *Westmynster*, the fourth day of Decemƀr, in the Eight yeare of our Raigne of *England Fraunce & Ireland*, and of *Scotland* the fower and fortith.

COPPIN *Per breue de priuato Sigillo*

Articles indented & agreed vpon the thirtenth day of Decemƀ in the yeare of o<sup>r</sup> Lord 1610. Betweene S<sup>r</sup> Thomas Smyth knight Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> of the Company of Marchaunṯe of London, tradeinge to the East Indies, and Certeine Committees of that Company appointed by order of Courte for that purpose, on thone parte. And *Peter Floris & Lucas Athewmes*,[^sec-08-fn-103] Dutch Marchaunṯe on thother parte. In manner & forme followinge.

INPRIMIS. Itt is agreed that a shipp shall be prouided by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Companie of the burthen of fower hundred Tunns or thereabouṯe To be readie to sett saile from hence in this instant Decemƀ, or in Ianuarie next, w<sup>th</sup> fower score men (Marchaunṯe & all others) & victualled for thirtie monnethes for a voyadge (by godę grace) to be made therew<sup>th</sup> into the said East Indies.

Item : ffor the p̄formance thereof, as alsoe for a competent [p. 364] stocke of 12000<sup>li</sup> or thereaboutes is appointed to be leuied, whereof 1500<sup>li</sup> is to be putt into the said stocke by the foresaid *Peter Floris & Lucas Antheumes* for their aduenture And 600<sup>li</sup> of the said 1500<sup>li</sup>, is by them presentlie to be paid, to such a Casheare as shalbe therevnto by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie chosen And the other 900<sup>li</sup> to be likewise paid to the said Chasheare in Iune or Iulie next followinge the date of theis presentes (w<sup>ch</sup> the said Companie doe acknowledge to haue receiued). The rest of the said stocke of 12000<sup>li</sup> is to be supplied by the said Company.

Item. That of the foresaid 12000<sup>li</sup> intended for the said stocke, the chardge of the Shippe, victuallinge & such other necessaries shalbe supplied, & then the Remainder of the said some shall be imployed as a stocke by them for this voyadge.

Item. That the said *Pieter Floris, Lucas Atheumes & Robert Browne* shall be the principall ffactors for sale & imploym<sup>t</sup> of the said stocke, duringe the said voyadge, And that whatsoeuer shalbe by them bought or sould in the tyme of this their said voyadge shalbe registred and written by some English Marchauntę to be appointed by the said Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Companie for that purpose. And alsoe the said *Pieter Floris, & Lucas Atheumes* doe promyse that they will neither buie nor sell any Marchaundize or Comodities whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>, nor make any priuate, nor any other ꝭgaines before hand, but such and att those tymes when the said *Robert Browne;* and other Englishe Marchauntę shall be by att the makeinge of them. Promysinge further to vse their best dilligence & endevo<sup>rs</sup> to informe teach & enstruct the said Englishe Marchauntę in all the misteries & secreetę belonginge to the said trade and busines.

Item. The said *Pieter Floris & Lucas Athemmes* doe promyse that they will not intermeddle nor haue any dealinges w<sup>th</sup> any other busines then buyinge & sellinge of Marchaundize & such other Comodities w<sup>th</sup>out the Consent of the Captaine and *Robert Browne* w<sup>th</sup> the rest of the said English Marchauntę: Nor w<sup>th</sup> setlinge any ffactory in any place, or w<sup>th</sup> any state whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> w<sup>th</sup>out the Consent & resoluc̃on first had of the said Capt & englishe Marchauntę as aforesaid. Prouided & yt is agreed that the said Capt & englishe Marchauntę shall cause the shipp to sayle, & [p. 365] direct their course to all such hauens and portes as the said *Pieter Ploris & Lucas Atheumes* shall from tyme to tyme direct them vnto.

Item The money and Marchandize appointed for the foresaid stocke shall be m<sup>r</sup>ked w<sup>th</sup> the Companies marke, & remaine in the Custodie and chardge of the said Captaine & english Marchauntes vntill there be tyme of ymploym<sup>t</sup>, and then to be deliu<sup>r</sup>ed to the said *Pieter Ploris*, *Lucas Antheumes & Robert Browne* as occasion shall serue, and by them required. And att what tyme soeu<sup>r</sup> the said Marchandize, or any parte thereof shall be sould & ymployed in other wares & goode the same shall presentlie be brought abourd & putt into the hould of the said shipp (marked w<sup>th</sup> the said Companies marke expressed in the margent). And this to be done as often as any chaunge, sale or ymploym<sup>t</sup> shall be made of the said wares goode or marchandize. And due accompte to be kept by the said englishe Marchaunte from tyme to tyme of the doinge thereof, soe as the Gou<sup>r</sup>nor & Company (for the tyme beinge) may receiue true informacõn of eu<sup>r</sup>y pticuler buyinge and sellinge w<sup>th</sup> the places where the same was done, & the tymes when.


![East India Company merchant's mark showing a cross over a heart/circle device containing initials G, C, and E.](../figures/fig-019_p0457.webp)

Item Thatt for the doinge & pformaunce of this busines the said Gou<sup>r</sup>nor & Company doe promise to allowe to the said *Pieter Ploris* and *Lucas Anthumes*, for their factorie vpon the nette pceede of the said stocke (Marriners wages & all other chardges deducted []) as followeth.

If there be vnder Centum p Cento, nette proffitt made, by the said voyadge, then they are to receiue noe factorage.

If there be *Centum* p *Cento* nette proffitt made as for example 24000<sup>li</sup> for 12000<sup>li</sup> then they are to haue 4 p Centū.

If one hundred and a halfe be made, nett proffitt vpon the hundred as 30000<sup>li</sup> for 12000<sup>li</sup> then they are to haue 5 p Cent.

If Twoe hundred be made nette proffitt vpon the hundred as 36000<sup>li</sup> for 12000<sup>li</sup> then they are to haue 6 p Cent.

If twoe hundred & a halfe be made nette proffitt vpon the hundred as 42000<sup>li</sup> for 12000<sup>li</sup> then they are to haue 7 p Centū. [p. 366] If three hundred be made nette proffitt vpon the hundred as 48000<sup>li</sup> for 12000<sup>li</sup> then they are to haue 8 <span class="sc">p</span> Centū.

If three hundred & a halfe be made nette proffitt vpon the hundred as 54000<sup>li</sup> for 12000<sup>li</sup> then they are to have 9 <span class="sc">p</span> Centū.

If ffower hundred be made nette pffitt vpon the hundred as 60000<sup>li</sup> for 12000<sup>li</sup> then they are to haue 10 <span class="sc">p</span> Centū. And noe more what increase soeu<sup>r</sup> they shall retourne of proffitt or gaine, they shall haue noe more then 10 <span class="sc">p</span> Centū.

Item That duringe the said voyadge they shall neither by themselues, nor any other for them or to their vse directlie or indirectlie, vse or exercise any priuate trade or Marchandizeinge whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> But shall applie themselues & their whole endevo<sup>rs</sup> for the good & aduancm<sup>t</sup> of the gen<sup>r</sup>all stocke, And the said Gou<sup>r</sup>nor & Companie, doe promise to vse their best care & diligence to p<sup>r</sup>uent the like priuate trade or Marchandizinge to be made by the said Captaine, englishe Marchauntę or any other Marriners whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>.

Item that the said *Peter Ploris* & *Lucas Antheumes* shall become bound vnto the said Gou<sup>r</sup>nor & Comp: in 2000<sup>li</sup> for their true & faithfull dealeinge w<sup>th</sup> the said Gou<sup>r</sup>nor & Comp: in the said voyadge, and for the due pformance of whatt is for them to be pformed abouesaid. As alsoe for the deliu<sup>r</sup>inge vp in writeinge of a true and iust accompt of all there pceedinge in the said voyadge.

Item yf God shall call the said *Peter Floris* & *Lucas Atheumes* out of this lyfe, before that they shall retourne backe into the porte of London, then the benefitt of their factorage as abouesaid, and nette pceede of their aduenture pporcionablie w<sup>th</sup> the rest of the Aduenturers shall be trulie paid and satisfied vnto their heires Executors or Administrators.

Item yt is further agreed That yf the said *Peter Floris* or the said *Lucas Antheumes* or either of them doe fortune to die, & the other retourne that then the suruiuo<sup>r</sup> shall stand for both, & be accomptable in the behalfe of both, for all that hath past in the said voyadge accordinge to the true meaneinge of theis Articles.

Item. Whereas certaine Articles of Agreem<sup>t</sup> were made and concluded, betwixt the said S<sup>r</sup>: Thomas Smyth Gou<sup>r</sup>nor of the [p. 367] said Companie &c: on the one parte: And Peter *Floris* & *Lucas Antheumes* on thother parte bereinge date the 27<sup>th</sup> day of March 1610. for c<sup>r</sup>teine couenantę to haue beene pformed on either parte: Itt is nowe agreed vpon that the said Articles shall be disannulled and cancelled, & whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> is conteyned in them to be of noe strength nor power.

In Witnes whereof the said *Pieter Floris* and *Lucas Antheumes* haue sett to their handę and seales to thone parte, and the said Companie haue fixed their Comon seale vnto theis presentę to thother parte the day & yeare first aboue written

Whereas mention is made in the precedent Articles of a stocke of 12000<sup>li</sup> to be ymployed by the foresaid *Pieter Floris* & *Lucas Antheumes*, for w<sup>ch</sup> they are to receiue factorie accordinge to the said Articles of agreem<sup>t</sup> betwixt the Companie and them; They nowe findinge that by the increase of chardges the Capitall will be raysed vnto 14000<sup>li</sup> or thereaboutes, doe desier that the Companie would be pleased to graunt them considerac̃on in there factorye for the said encrease, w<sup>ch</sup> the Company are willinge to yeald vnto in manner and forme followinge as is sett downe (accordinge to their owne desier) *on thother side of this Roll. Viz.* as followeth.

*Pieter Floris: Lucas Antheumes:*

Consideringe that the settinge forth of the Shipp cometh to more then was att the first supposed yt would haue done, In reguard whereof the Capitall is encreased w<sup>th</sup> Marchandize and money to 14000<sup>li</sup> or thereaboutę: Wee therefore the Gou<sup>r</sup>nor Deputy & Comittees for the foresaid Companie (att the earnest request of the forenamed Peter *Floris* and Lucas Antheumes) are willinge and contented for their satisfacc̃on to graunt that there prom̃tio and factorie shall be reckoned as followeth.

If they bring in retourne the nette some of 24000<sup>li</sup> then there prom̃tio shall begyn att 4 p Centū, and soe to Continue to 29000<sup>li</sup>

Butt yf it soe happen that they bringe in nette retourne 30000<sup>li</sup> or aboue the same some shall be diuided by 12000<sup>li</sup>, & the prom̃tio to be reckoned as aforesaid.

And in like manner the same some shall be diuided by 14000<sup>li</sup> [p. 368] or as much as the nette Capitall shall come vnto & the prom̄tio reckoned *pro rato* of 12000<sup>li</sup>.

Nowe the difference betweene the twoe pm̄tions shall be equally diuided thone halfe to *Peter Floris* & *Lucas Antheumes* & thother halfe to the Companie.

This 165 must be added to the 1320<sup>li</sup>, or els substracted from 1650 & then our prom̄tion for 33000<sup>li</sup> wilbe 1485<sup>li</sup>.

This 290<sup>li</sup> must be added to 4640<sup>li</sup>, or els substracted from 5220<sup>li</sup> and then o<sup>r</sup> prom̄tio for 58000<sup>li</sup> wilbe y 4930<sup>li</sup>.

*Lucas Antheumes Peter Floris.*


<!-- page: 461 | folio: 369 -->
A Com̄ission[^sec-08-fn-105] graunted by vs the Gou<sup>r</sup>nor Deputy & Comittees, for the Company of Marchauntꬴ of London, tradeinge [into] the East Indies vnto Anthony Hippon Capt *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* & Rob̄t *Browne* o<sup>r</sup> principall ffactors, together w<sup>th</sup> Thomas Essington,[^sec-08-fn-106] Symon Evans, *Adam Denton*, & George *Chauncey* the rest of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors and all other o<sup>r</sup> Marriners employed in this o<sup>r</sup> seaventh voyadge in the good shipp called the *Globe*.

> _[Margin: **I.**]_
> _[Margin: A Comission graunted by the Comp: to Capt Hippon in the 7<sup>th</sup> voyadge &c:]_

<span class="sc">Nprimis</span> Whereas wee the Marchauntꬴ abouesaid w<sup>th</sup> o<sup>r</sup> greate chardge & trouble haue prepared a shipp called the *Globe*, for a voyadge by Godꬴ grace in her to be made to the bay of *Bengala* & other places in att or aboute the East Indies, & haue furnished the same in sufficient & plentifull manner, w<sup>th</sup> men, tackle, victualls, & all other needfull puičons, fitt for such a voyadge. And haueinge beene pswaded by the good reporte of dyvers, & alsoe of an espetiall trust and confidence wee haue of the integritie, wisdome and resolučons of o<sup>r</sup> loueinge freindꬴ Anthonie Hippon, *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* & Rob̄t *Browne* Doe appointe and authorize the said Anthonie Hippon to be o<sup>r</sup> cheefe Captaine & master, duringe the said voyadge, & to comaund o<sup>r</sup> shipp w<sup>th</sup> the men & Marrin<sup>r</sup>s att Sea, And *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* & Rob̄t Browne, our principall ffactors & Cape Marchauntꬴ for the orderinge & disposeinge of such moneys goodꬴ & Marchandize on shore, as shall be carried alonge w<sup>th</sup> them in the said shipp. And Thomas Essington, Symon Evans, *Adam Denton* & George Chauncey, wee appointe to take their passadge in the said shipp as o<sup>r</sup> ffactors to keepe bookes & accomptꬴ of all goodꬴ & [p. 370] Marchandize sould and delyuered, and bought and receiued from tyme to tyme w<sup>th</sup> the names of the portes, where any such trade or traffique is made. All w<sup>ch</sup> both Commanders Marchauntę ffactors and Marriners wee trust will soe carrie them selues w<sup>th</sup> due respect one to another, loue to their equalls & obedyence to their Superio<sup>rs</sup> as loue & kindnes may be contynued on all sides, and all whollie applie their witte and endevo<sup>rs</sup> for the due pformaunce of this voyadge in the best manner they may for the good of the Companie.

- 2 Item for that religious gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> doth best binde men to pforme their duties, It is principally to be cared for, that prayers be said eu<sup>r</sup>y Morninge & eueninge in the Shippe, & the whole Company called therevnto w<sup>th</sup> dilligent Eyes that none be wantinge, soe as all may ioyntlie w<sup>th</sup> reuerence and humilitie pray vnto Almightie God to blesse & preserue them from all dangers in this longe and tedious voyadge And for that purpose wee haue deliu<sup>r</sup>ed vnto the purser a faire Bible, w<sup>th</sup> the booke of Comon prayers.
- 3 Item That noe blasphemeinge of God, sweareinge, theft, drunkennes, or other like misdemeano<sup>rs</sup> be vsed, butt that the same be seuerelie ponished & that noe diceinge or other vnlawfull games be pmitted for that the same are most comonlie the begynninges of quarrells, and many times murther a iust occasion of Godę wrath and vengeance from w<sup>ch</sup> the lord deliuer vs all. Wherefore wee doe order that the Captaine shall puide ponishm<sup>t</sup>ę to be sett vp & published in the said shipp for such offences, whereby eu<sup>r</sup>y man may take notice what he ought to avoied.
- 4 Item. Thatt noe liquor be spilt in the ballast of the shipp, or filthines be left w<sup>th</sup>in bourd w<sup>ch</sup> in heate breedeth noysome smells, and infec̃cõn: Butt that the ou<sup>r</sup>lopps and other places of the shipp be kept cleane & sweete w<sup>ch</sup> is a notable preseruãcõn of health
- 5 Item That contynuall & true Iournalls be kept of eu<sup>r</sup>y dayes course & nauigãcõn duringe the whole voyadge, w<sup>th</sup> the obseruãcõn of fallinge w<sup>th</sup> eu<sup>r</sup>y Coaste & land, or porte where they come, for the depth of water, & in what latitude yt lyeth, w<sup>th</sup> true relãcõn of eu<sup>r</sup>y thinge that passeth And this to be done seu<sup>r</sup>ally by Captaine ffactors, Pylott, M<sup>rs</sup> mate and purser And [p. 371] they att conuenient tyme to conferr together aboute the same, To thend that yf any of them haue forgotten what an other obserued the same may be added whereby a discourse may be sett downe, to be presented by the Captaine to the Gou<sup>r</sup>nor and Company, when God shall graunte the said shipp safe retourne.
6\. Item Thatt all money & Marchandizes w<sup>ch</sup> shall be shipt here by the Gou<sup>r</sup>nor and Companie shall be kept by the Captaine he giueinge a receipt for the same w<sup>ch</sup> said receipt shall be kept by *Peter Floris Lucas Antheumes* and Robt Browne thereby to demand the said money & goode when they shall come to those places, where they shall vse the same And then the same shall be deliu<sup>r</sup>ed ouer by the Captaine vnto them from tyme to tyme duringe the said voyadge.

7 Item Wee will that the Captaine shall cause the Boates or Sciffes to be alwaies in a readines to be ymployed to all such places as o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntę shall appointe them, And not to dispose of them any otherwyse soe longe as they shall haue occasion to vse them.

8 Item such Marchandize wares & money as the Capt shall deliu<sup>r</sup> into the handes of the principall Marchauntę he shall take a receipt from them thereof: And such wares and Marchandize as shall be brought into the shipp by the foresaid principall Marchauntę *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* & Robt Browne (or such as shall succeede in their places) beinge marked w<sup>th</sup> the Companies marke, they shall take a receipt of the Capt for the same. And this shall be done soe often as any goode shall be dischardged forth of the shipp, or laden into the shipp, And the Captaine to be carefull that the goode be well preserued & kept drie. To w<sup>ch</sup> end he shall haue espetiall care to looke often tymes vnto the overloppe, that ytt be well kept.

9 Item the principall Marchauntę shall not doe any thinge (w<sup>ch</sup> is w<sup>th</sup>out the compasse of their tradeinge) w<sup>th</sup>out the Counsaile of the Capt & other ffactors whether yt be in setlinge of any factory, or any contract or agreement to be made w<sup>th</sup> any kinge or potentate in the Indies Neither shall the Captaine haue any comaund or authoritie on the land to haue any thinge to doe w<sup>th</sup> the trade of Marchandizeinge Butt therein whollie wee doe authorize & put in trust o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntę *Peter Floris*, [p. 372] *Lucas Antheumes* & Robt Browne to be cheefe Comanders on the land, to thend they may pforme the busines accordinge to their owne inuention. And Thomas Essington, Symon Evans, *Adam Denton*, and George *Chauncey* shall be w<sup>th</sup> them to assist them both in keepinge the bookes of accomptes as alsoe the Cashe.

- 10 Item yf the principall Marchauntę shall haue occasion to vse 5 or 6 Marriners or more to helpe to watch and keepe the goodę on Land in their howses, then yo<sup>u</sup> Capt Anthonie Hippon shall (vpon their demand) lett them haue soe many as they shall need, and those of the best and trustiest men yo<sup>u</sup> haue.
- 11 Item To the end that the voyadge be not hindred through want of victualls, Wee doe ordeyne and requier that the Captaine shall not alter the daylie allowance of victualls, w<sup>th</sup>out first haueinge taken Counsell & consent of o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntę, Whoe shall keepe Counter bookes of all the Victualls that are spent, and that shall remaine in *Esse*, the better to make their reckoninge for their pceedinge in the voyadge. And when yo<sup>u</sup> shall come vnto the Land then shall the victualls be lockt vp in the shipp, and the principall Marchauntę shall puide fresh victualls from the land, the better to enlardge the store, yf any may be pcured.
- 12 Item. That att any place where yo<sup>u</sup> shall water, and refresh yo<sup>r</sup> selues, or putt in for traffique and Marchandizeinge, you Capt *Anthonie Hippon* shall call the whole Companie together giueinge them most strict & straight chardge and warninge not to straggle, but to behaue them selues peaceablie and Ciuillie towarde the people of that place, (yf any be there) the better to pcure their freindshipp, towarde the supplie of yo<sup>r</sup> wante, and in yo<sup>r</sup> course of trade least the losse of yo<sup>r</sup> liues and ou<sup>r</sup>throwe of o<sup>r</sup> voyadge pay for yo<sup>r</sup> disorders, beside an vtter discreditt to o<sup>r</sup> Nation, And that yo<sup>r</sup> men doe vse a discreete meane in eateinge of fruite, fresh victualls, or drinkinge of water, leaste they surfett and fall into diseases, whereof wee haue had too much experience. But as any fresh prouisions shall be pcured a shore by our principall ffactors, the same shall be first brought vnto the Captaine (whoe w<sup>th</sup> there advise) shall reparte the same vnto the Company as to yo<sup>u</sup> shall seeme good and needfull : And none presume to doe contrary w<sup>th</sup>out seueare ponishm<sup>t</sup> And that [p. 373] espetiall care be had to releiue the sicke, w<sup>th</sup> such fresh meatę, and other Comfortable thinges, wherew<sup>th</sup> wee haue furnished yo<sup>r</sup> shipp for that purpose, and not otherwise to be spent in Ryott and banquettinge and soe the sicke p̱ishe for wante of thingę needfull.
13\. Item Whereas the stragglinge of yo<sup>r</sup> men, in any place where they shall arryue and come, may not onlie proue the losse of such, as shall soe straggle (notw<sup>th</sup>standinge they should be armed) but alsoe thereby much hurte might happen to the residue of o<sup>r</sup> people. It is ordered that yo<sup>u</sup> doe not p̱mitt any man in any place to straggle or goe from the rest of yo<sup>r</sup> Companie vnlesse vpon some spetiall occasions yo<sup>u</sup> giue Warraunt therevnto, vpon paine of seueare ponishm<sup>t</sup> to be inflicted vpon such as shall doe the Contrarie, still doubtinge the worst and standinge vpon yo<sup>r</sup> guarde, w<sup>th</sup>out giueinge any trust vnto the people of the place.

14 Item fforasmuch as wee are well p̱swaded, of the discrec̃on, circumspection & good vnderstandinge of o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntę *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes*, and Rob̃t Browne. Wee doe therefore requier yo<sup>u</sup> Capt *Anthonie Hippon* that yo<sup>u</sup> be alwaies readie to saile to all such hauens and portes, as o<sup>r</sup> foresaid principall Marchauntę shall direct yo<sup>u</sup> to sayle vnto, and there to remayne vntill the said principall Marchauntę, shall haue finished there busines, & then from thence to saile vnto such other places as they shall requier yo<sup>u</sup>. And this shall be soe often by yo<sup>u</sup> p̱formed as they shall thinke fitt: for therein consisteth the welfare of the said voyadge And noe man shall counsaile or resolue to retourne homewardes, vntill such tyme as o<sup>r</sup> said principall Marchauntę shall haue fully finisht there intended trade, vpon forfecture of all their wages.

15 Item It is expreslie ordered that by a generall Consent of yo<sup>u</sup> the Capt: Marchauntę, factor<sup>s</sup>: and Marriners, some good order be by yo<sup>u</sup> taken, and sett downe in writinge, soe soone as yo<sup>u</sup> come to Sea, conc<sup>r</sup>ninge the disposeinge of dead mens goodę in the voyadge eyther by Comittinge the same by Inventory to the p̱ticular keepinge of some men in the shipps (and that vpon some convenient considerac̃ons, for keepinge the same) or by sale of soe much thereof att the mayne maste as may not exceede a [p. 374] third parte of the buyers wages, for either buyinge or borroweinge, to preuent such preiudice to o<sup>r</sup> Company as wee haue felt by Marriners buyinge soe much, as there whole wages came vnto : whereby they haue not onlie forsaken o<sup>r</sup> shipps before their dischardge, butt alsoe depriued vs of meanes to redresse such wronges, as they haue many waies done vs in the voyadge. Alsoe that there be noe dealeinge by Exchange betwixt ptie and ptie, neither mony for mony, Comoditie for Comoditie Comoditie for money outwardes nor homewardes (for such exchange giues way for them to take and purloyne of o<sup>r</sup> goode). ffor preuencon whereof, wee order That neither the purser (nor any other) doe register, witnes, or take knowledge of any such contract by exchange. And noe man to be admitted meanes, to bringe goode abourd, vpon paine of forfecture to the Company of that w<sup>ch</sup> shall be soe brought in. And yf any ffactor shall happen to die, his booke, accompte, and other thinges are to be ordered by the Capt<sup>ne</sup> : & safelie reserued and brought home for England (an Inventory first taken thereof and registred in the pursers booke, to be witnessed by twoe or three others of the Companie[]). And that eu<sup>r</sup>y Marriner or other in the shipp, doe sett there handes or marke to the said Orders mentioned in this 15th Article.

16 Item To the end that all difficult matters may the better be passed over by good endevo<sup>rs</sup> wee doe appointt a Counsell of Eight psonns whereof Capt<sup>ne</sup> : *Anthony Hippon* to be Presedent (in matters of the shipp or for Iustice) and *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* & *Robert Browne*, w<sup>th</sup> *Thomas Essington*, *Symon Euans Adam Denton*, and *George Chauncey* (beinge in all eight psonns, whereof one of them to recorde whatt matters shall passe) shall be a sufficient Counsell to determyne, all cryminall & ciuill causes that shall come before them. Yett forasmuch as *Peter Floris* & Lucas Antheumes haue excused themselues thatt they are not acquaintted w<sup>th</sup> the losse[^sec-08-fn-107] and Iustice of o<sup>r</sup> land, therefore they shall be exempted & not required to come to the Councell, when any matter of Iustice is to be handled (for such matters shall be determined by the rest of the Counsell) But yf yt be for any matters on land (or for any thinge w<sup>ch</sup> conc<sup>r</sup>neth trade[]), [p. 375] then one of the principall Marchantę shall be president (either *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* or Roƀt Browne as they shall thinke fitt amongst themselues, to determyn for that purpose[]). And the foresaid Counsell shall allowe of the said pson for President, and shall hearken to his ppositions, and take Counsell and resolue vppon the same, as occasion shall be offerred. And all of them aforenamed (exceptinge such as shalbe lefte in the Country as ffactors) to be in like manner of the Counsell w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> homewardę.

17\. Item the Cap<sup>tne</sup> : shall haue espetiall care that noe man whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> (of whatt quallity or Condicõn soeu<sup>r</sup> he be) his owne pson beinge alsoe included herein) shall vse any priuate or secreete trade vpon peine of fforfecture of all thatt shall be found by any man soe doinge, and besides shall endure arbitrary ponishm<sup>t</sup>. And wee requier the principall Marchauntę to haue espetiall care hereof on the land, and to preuent yt soe much as they can or is possible. And the Cap<sup>tne</sup> : and other Marchauntę shall alsoe haue a vigillant eye, & good reguard on the principall Marchauntę, to the end the Company may be the better serued [(]whoe haue beene at such excessiue chardges) and reape the benefitt of the trade, discou<sup>r</sup>ed by there expences.

18 Item for better preseruacõn of health, o<sup>r</sup> order is, That from tyme to tyme as the water Caske shall be emptied of fresh water, yt be forthw<sup>th</sup> againe filled w<sup>th</sup> salt water, for preuencõn of leakeinge and mustines.

19 Item No pson whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall succeede by appointm<sup>t</sup> or otherwise, in any place of com̃and or office, either in o<sup>r</sup> shipp, or in any ffactory to be setled, shall take or be allowed the wages of his predecessors. But thoughe he be remoued, preferred, and come to any such place and office, he shall content him selfe w<sup>th</sup> such wages as wee haue form<sup>r</sup>lie agreed w<sup>th</sup> him for, w<sup>th</sup>out any further demand or incroatchm<sup>t</sup> vpon the Company for the same (vnlesse the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & Comittees of the Company for the tyme beinge, shall be pleased to graunt the same att their retourne, or any other allowance of gratitude or rewarde vpon their desertes[]).

20 Item fforasmuch as wee are c<sup>r</sup>teinelie informed that when twoe of o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchantę *Peter Floris*, & *Lucas Antheumes* shall come into the Indies, they are lyke to be much hated by the [p. 376] *Dutchmen* there, whoe will seeke to doe them wronge and all the villanie they may therefore we expreslie chardge yo<sup>u</sup> the Captaine (and all others that are in o<sup>r</sup> shipp & voyadge) to defend and preserue them from wronges, w<sup>th</sup>all the power and strength you may against any that shall offer to doe them wronge or iniury: Or shall goe aboute to hinder them in their busines, w<sup>ch</sup> might much endanger our voyadge. The lyke Comandem<sup>t</sup> wee doe expreslie giue vnto all others that are in any of o<sup>r</sup> shipps, & imployed in o<sup>r</sup> busines in any places whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>.

21 Item Wee doe expreslie chardge yo<sup>u</sup> Capt *Anthony Hippon* not to suffer any Cabbins to be new built or altered, nor pticõns pulled downe in o<sup>r</sup> shipp (except for enlarginge of the hould, or makeinge better puision for the bringinge home of o<sup>r</sup> goode, and that by the aduise of the Councell, or for the better accomodatinge of there fightes[^sec-08-fn-108] if need shall be[]], or changed from the state they nowe are in, att the settinge out of the same, w<sup>ch</sup> in former voyadges haue beene done to the greate hurte of o<sup>r</sup> Companie, and discontent and hazard of all.

22 Item That noe wages to noe pson whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> be encreased or giuen contrary to whatt we haue alreadie appointed, but the pties to be referd to be rewarded by the Company att their retourne as they shall be found to haue deserued. Nor ffactors, mrs mates, nor other officers of espetiall place in o<sup>r</sup> shipp to be remoued w<sup>th</sup>out consent of such of the Councell as wee haue appointed to aduise w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> the Capt<sup>ne</sup> : vpon all occasions. And not to thinke vpon authoritie sett vppon yo<sup>u</sup> That the same should serue for any yo<sup>r</sup> pticular respecte, knowinge that a wise man is best tryed when he is putt in authoritie. And that he is accompted of more fortitude that ou<sup>r</sup>cometh himselfe then he that p<sup>r</sup>uaileth against a multitude.

23\. Item Wee forbid all vnnecessarie expence of shooteinge [p. 377] of Ordinance, att drinkinge of healthes or att the Captaines or Cape Marchauntę goinge a shore, or such like, for that thereby much powder is wastfullie consumed and o<sup>r</sup> shipp and goode putt in much hazard and danger: And likewise by yt way is giuen to the Gunners (vnder colour thereof) to embecyll the same.

24\. Item for avoiedinge confuc̃on, in the gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> of o<sup>r</sup> people, And for that nothinge is soe vnc<sup>r</sup>teine as the state of mans lyfe, Wee ordeyne that yf God shall call you Captaine *Anthonie Hippon* (duringe this voyadge) out of this world, (w<sup>ch</sup> God defend) then wee Comitt the same gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> of o<sup>r</sup> shipp and Marriners therein, to such as wee haue nomynated in a wryteinge subscribed by the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and sealed w<sup>th</sup> the seale of the Company, putt vp into a Boxe N<sup>o</sup>: 1. sealed w<sup>th</sup> hard Waxe & deliu<sup>r</sup>ed to Cap<sup>tne</sup>: *Anthony Hippon* to be kept close, and not opened soe longe as the said Capt *Anthonie Hippon* shall liue: Butt yf it shall please God to take him out of this world (that shall succeede Captaine *Anthony Hippon*) Then wee ordeine thatt o<sup>r</sup> M<sup>r</sup> and Marriners in o<sup>r</sup> said shipp shall submit themselues to the gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> and Comand of such pson or psons as wee haue nominated therevnto, in a writeinge sealed vp in a Boxe No: 2. And remaineinge in the Custodie of the said Capt Anthonie Hippon & those that shall succeede him, Prouided alwaies that noe pson whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>, w<sup>ch</sup> shall succeede in the foresaid place of gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> shall demaund be allowed or expect the wages of his predecessor, but shall content himselfe w<sup>th</sup> his first wages promysed him by the Companie, or referr him selfe to be considered of accordinge to his deserte att his retourne by the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> Deputy and Comittees of the Company for the tyme beinge whoe haue ever respected men that shall deserue well of them.

25\. Item for that in many voyadges heretofore the Company haue beene much wronged by the takeinge in of diu<sup>r</sup>s psonns into ther shipps [()not interteyned by them) w<sup>ch</sup> haue beene carried into the East Indies, for some mens pticular gaine and proffitt to the greate chardge and hindraunce of the Companie Itt is therefore o<sup>r</sup> expresse order & direcc̃on to yo<sup>u</sup> Captaine Anthony Hippon, and to all other the Marchantę ffactors<sup>rs</sup> & Marriners & eu<sup>r</sup>y other pson or psonns, enterteyned & hired to serue in this said voyadge, That neither yo<sup>u</sup> nor any of yo<sup>u</sup> shall admitte, or suffer to passe [p. 378] or receiue into o<sup>r</sup> said shipp (in this o<sup>r</sup> nowe intended voyadge) any pson or psonns, of whatt degree or quallitie soeu<sup>r</sup>, other then such pson or psons as are interteyned and hired by the Gou<sup>r</sup>nor and Comittees of o<sup>r</sup> said Companie to passe therein.

26\. Item If it should happen (as God forbid) that o<sup>r</sup> shipp should haue wante of men or other necessary meanes (w<sup>ch</sup> such longe voyadges are subject vnto) then wee will that you desire to be releeued by any shipp yo<sup>u</sup> shall meete (w<sup>ch</sup> is appteyneinge vnto vs, or any other Englishe shipp, whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>) And wee hereby straightlie chardge and comand all Generalls, Captaines, Masters, or any other Officers (in any of the shipps whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>, appteyneinge to the Companie of Marchaunte of London, tradeinge to the East Indies[])], whome yo<sup>u</sup> shall chaunce to meete in any such yo<sup>r</sup> distresse, That they supplie yo<sup>u</sup>, ayde and releeue yo<sup>u</sup> w<sup>th</sup> such men, or any other necessaries, w<sup>ch</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> shall haue neede of, & they may convenientlie spare yo<sup>u</sup> w<sup>th</sup>out endaungeringe themselues and their shipps. And that yo<sup>u</sup> pforme the like good Offices to any of o<sup>r</sup> shipps, that yo<sup>u</sup> shall meete dureinge the said voyadge, whome yo<sup>u</sup> shall finde distressed.

27 Item If yo<sup>u</sup> shall finde in yo<sup>r</sup> trauaile or can convenientlie come by any faire birde or Beaste or any other thinges fitt for vs to present to his Ma<sup>tie</sup>: or any of the Noble Lorde, that are o<sup>r</sup> honorable freinde, Wee pray and requier yo<sup>u</sup> to be carefull to prouide, and send the same w<sup>th</sup> espetiall chardge to some carefull man or men that retourne to see them carefully kept, and deliu<sup>r</sup>ed to vs. And w<sup>th</sup>all that yf yo<sup>u</sup> shall knowe any of the Marriners or others to haue any such, w<sup>ch</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> cannot pcure from them for reason, then that yo<sup>u</sup> send vs notice thereof, to the end wee may take order therein accordinglie.

28 Item And lastlie to preuent disorders and misbehaiuours of the Marriners of this o<sup>r</sup> shipp, either in their passadge out or retourne whome[^sec-08-fn-109] vpon o<sup>r</sup> owne Coastes, wee ordeyne that yo<sup>u</sup> suffer not o<sup>r</sup> foresaid shipp, either outwarde or homewardes, to goe into any of the portes of Faulmouth Plymouth or Darthmouthe (vnlesse necessitie compell yo<sup>u</sup> therevnto[]).

And soe haueinge remembred what wee thinke needfull for yo<sup>r</sup> direccon in this voyadge, and relyinge vpon yo<sup>r</sup> dilligence and [p. 379] care in psueinge o<sup>r</sup> busines to o<sup>r</sup> most aduantage, Wee comitt yo<sup>u</sup> to the pteccon of the Almightie God, whome wee beseech to blesse yo<sup>r</sup> endevo<sup>rs</sup>, and graunte yo<sup>u</sup> a safe passadge & safe retourne to all o<sup>r</sup> Comforte.

Item Wheareas the stores appteyneinge to eu<sup>r</sup>y pticular Office are nowe sufficientlie furnished for this voyadge, and an Invoice deliu<sup>r</sup>ed vnto yo<sup>u</sup> the Cap<sup>tne</sup>: of eu<sup>r</sup>y pticular store: w<sup>ch</sup> heretofore in some of o<sup>r</sup> former voyadges haue (through the remisnes of o<sup>r</sup> Comanders[]), bene ymbecilled and appropriated to mens pticular vses. ffor the better preuentinge therefore of the lyke inconueniences hereafter, wee ordeyne and giue yt in chardge vnto yo<sup>u</sup> Cap<sup>tne</sup>: *Anthony Hippon*, that yo<sup>u</sup> cause trewe notice to be taken, and a iust accompt kept of the expence of the Gunners, Carpenters, Boateswaines Stewardes and eu<sup>r</sup>y such store, both by the purser and some others that yo<sup>u</sup> shall appointe therevnto. That att yo<sup>r</sup> retourne wee may receiue from yo<sup>u</sup> a iust accompt of eu<sup>r</sup>y pticuler to be awnswered accordinge to the Invoice nowe deliu<sup>r</sup>ed vnto yo<sup>u</sup>, And howe the same haue beene spent and disposed of.

Anthonie Hippon *Pieter Floris Lucas Antheumes* Robt Browne Tho: Essington


![Round seal or stamp containing the text: locus sigillo.](../figures/fig-020_p0471.webp)

*Round seal or stamp containing the text: locus sigillo.[^sec-08-fn-110]*

A Comission[^sec-08-fn-111] graunted by vs the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> Deputy & Committees for the Company of Marchaunte of London tradeinge to the East Indies to be obserued and kept by *Anthonie Hippon* Cap<sup>tne</sup>: and *Pieter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* and *Robert Browne* Marchaunte, o<sup>r</sup> principall [p. 380] ffactors together w<sup>th</sup> Thomas Essington, Symon Euans, *Adam Denton* and *George Chauncey* the rest of o<sup>r</sup> ffactor<sup>s</sup> nowe ymployed in this o<sup>r</sup> *Seauenth Voyadge*.

> _[Margin: I.]_

<span class="sc">Inprimis</span> Whereas we the Marchauntę abouesaid w<sup>th</sup> o<sup>r</sup> greate chardge and trouble haue p<sup>r</sup>pared a shipp called the *Globe* for a voyadge by Godę grace in her to be made to the *Bay of Bengalla* & other places in at or aboute the East Indies and haue furnished the same in sufficient and plentifull manner, w<sup>th</sup> men tackle victualls and all other needfull prouisions fitt for such a voyadge, And haueinge beene pswaded by the good reporte of diuers, and alsoe of an espetiall trust and Confidence wee haue of the integritie, wisdome and resolũcõns of o<sup>r</sup> loueinge freinde *Anthonie Hippon*, *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* and *Robert Browne* doe appointe and authorize the said *Anthony Hippon*, to be o<sup>r</sup> cheef Capt and Maister duringe the said voyadge and ordeine him to haue the full gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> over the shipp and Marriners, And *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* and *Robert Browne* to be o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntę and ffactors. And haue appointed *Tho: Essington*, *Symon Euans*, *Adam Denton*, *George Chauncey* o<sup>r</sup> ffactors to be assistaunt to them, Ouer all w<sup>ch</sup> said Marchauntę and ffactors the Captaine shall haue noe Comand nor authoritie, neither by water nor land in any matters conc<sup>r</sup>ninge trade.

2 Item Thatt all money and Marchandize w<sup>ch</sup> shall be shippt here, by the Gou<sup>r</sup>nor and Comp: shall be kept by the Captaine he geiueinge a receipt for the same, w<sup>ch</sup> foresaid receipt shall be kept by *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* and *Robert Browne* thereby to demand the said money and goodę when they shall come to those places where they shall vse the same, and then the same shall be deliu<sup>r</sup>ed by the Capt vnto them from tyme to tyme duringe the said voyadge.

3 Item To the end that *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* and *Robert Browne* may the better pforme their busines in their trade (the w<sup>ch</sup> wee doe referr vnto their discrecõns []) Wee doe therefore expreslie chardge yo<sup>u</sup> *Thomas Essington*, *Symon Euans*, *Adam Denton*, and *George Chauncey* to be readie att all tymes to goe either by water or land wheresoeu<sup>r</sup> o<sup>r</sup> said principall Marchauntę [p. 381] shall direct yo<sup>u</sup> and requier the same for the Companies occasions.

4 Item We will that the Captaine shall cause the boatę or Sciffes to be alwaies in a readines, to be ymployed to all such places as o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntę shall appointe them, and not to dispose of them any otherwise soe longe as they shall haue occasion to vse them.

5 Item such Marchandize wares and money as the Captaine shall deliu<sup>r</sup> vnto the handę of the principall Marchauntę, he shall take a receipt from them there, And such wares and Marchandize as shall be brought into the shipp by the foresaid principall Marchauntę *Peter Floris, Lucas Antheumes & Robert Browne* or such as shall succeede in their places beinge Marked w<sup>th</sup> the Companies m<sup>r</sup>ke, they shall take a receipt of the Capt<sup>ne</sup>: for the same, and this shall be done soe often as any goodę shall be dischargded forth of the shipp or laden into the shipp. And the Captaine to be carefull that the goodę be well p<sup>r</sup>serued and kept drie, To w<sup>ch</sup> end he shall haue a spetiall care, to looke often tymes vnto the overlopps thatt yt be well kept.

6\. Item The principall Marchauntę shall neither doe nor pretend to begynne to doe any thinge (w<sup>ch</sup> is w<sup>th</sup>out the Compasse of their tradeinge) w<sup>th</sup>out the Counsell of the Captaine and other ffactors, whether ytt be in setling any ffactorie, or any contract or agreem<sup>t</sup> to be made w<sup>th</sup> any kinge or Potentate in the Indies, neither shall the Captaine haue any authoritie on the land, to haue any thinge to doe w<sup>th</sup> the trade of Marchandize. But therein whollie wee doe authorize and putt in trust o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntę Peter ffloris, Lucas Antheumes and *Robert Browne* to be cheefe Comanders on the Land to the end they may pforme their busines accordinge to their owne invention. And Thomas Essington, Symon Evans, Adam Denton, & George Chauncey shall be w<sup>th</sup> them to assiste them both in keepinge bookes of accomptę, as alsoe the Cashe. Butt not meete to disburse any money (eyther in the chardges or otherwyse) w<sup>th</sup>out the knowledge and expresse Comandement of the principall Marchauntę.

7 Item Itt is expreslie ordered, that by agenerall Consent of you the Captaine Marchauntę ffactors & Marriners some good order be by yo<sup>u</sup> taken, and sett downe in writeing, soe soone as [p. 382] yo<sup>u</sup> come to Sea, conc<sup>r</sup>ninge the disposeinge of dead mens goode in the voyadge, either by Comittinge the same by Inuentorie to the pticular keepinge of some men in the shipps & this vpon Conuenient considerañōns for keepinge the same, or by sale of soe much thereof att the mayne maste, as may not exceede a third parte of the buyers wages, for either buyinge or borrowinge to preuent such preiudice to o<sup>r</sup> Company as wee haue felt, by Marriners buyinge soe much as their whole wages came vnto whereby they haue not onlie forsaken o<sup>r</sup> shipps before their dischardge butt alsoe depriued vs of meanes to redresse such wronges as they haue many wayes done vs in the voyadge. Alsoe that there be noe Dealinge by exchaunge betweene ptie and ptie neither money for money, com̄oditie for money, or com̄oditie for com̄oditie outwarde nor homewardes, for such exchaunge giues way for them to take and purloine of o<sup>r</sup> goode. ffor preuenc̃on whereof wee order that neither the Purser, nor any other doe register, witnes, or take knowledge of any such contract by Exchaunge. And noe man to be admitted meanes to bringe goode abourd vpon paine of forfeeture to the Company of that w<sup>ch</sup> shall be soe brought in, And yf any ffactor shall happen to die, his bookes accompte and other thinges are to be ordered by the Captaine, and safelie reserued and brought home for England (an Inuentorie first taken thereof and registred in the pursers booke, to bee witnessed by twoe or three others of the Companie[)]. And that eu<sup>r</sup>y Marriner or other in the shipp, doe sett their hande or marke to the said orders mentioned in this 7<sup>th</sup> article.

8 Item If the principall Marchaunte shall haue occasion to vse 5 or 6 Marriners or more to helpe to watch & keepe the goode on land in their howses, then yo<sup>u</sup> Captaine *Anthonie Hippon* shall vpon there demand lett them haue soe many as they shall need and those to be of the best and trustiest men alsoe.

9 Item To the end that the Company may be the better in all thinge iustlie dealt w<sup>th</sup>all, and the true and vpright carriadge of the busines may be made manifest and appeare plainlie The foresaid principall Marchaunte *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* and Rob̄t Browne shall keepe a iust and true accompt of all that shall be done by way of Marchandizinge And shall doe nothinge [p. 383] att any tyme w<sup>th</sup>out haueinge the English bookep[^sec-08-fn-112] or the Cashere by them, And shall informe instruct and showe, them all such knowledge, misterie, or arte appteineinge to their tradeinge as shall be in their power to pforme, And the said pties shall all of them eu<sup>r</sup>y eight dayes (or soe often as possiblie they may) compare the bookes and the Cashe together, to the end that yf any error should be comitted by the one or thother the same might be amended, and the bookes kept in good ballance : Soe that by life or death of any of them the state of the bookes might be found pfect.

10\. Item to the end the voyadge be not hindred through want of victualls wee doe ordeine and requier that the Captaine shall not alter the dailie allowance of victualls, w<sup>th</sup>out first haueinge taken Counsell & consent of o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchaunt<span class="sc">e</span> whoe shall keepe Counter bookes of all the victualls that are spent, and that shall remaine in *Esse* the better to make their reck[on]inge for their pceedinge in the voyadge. And when yo<sup>u</sup> shall come vnto the Land then shall the victualls be lockt vp in the shipp and the principall Marchaunt<span class="sc">e</span> shall prouide fresh victualls from the land the better to lengthen out their store soe much the longer. But yf they cannot prouide any, then yo<sup>u</sup> may vse the shipps victualls as tyme and occasion shall inforce you.

11 Item forasmuch as we are pswaded of the discretion circumspection and good vnderstandinge of o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchaunt<span class="sc">e</span> *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes*, and Ro<span class="sc">b</span>t Browne wee doe ordeyne that their opinions & direccõns in the busines of trade in Marchandizeinge, be followed w<sup>th</sup>out any controlm<sup>t</sup>, As likewise wee will and requier yo<sup>u</sup> Captaine *Anthony Hippon* that yo<sup>u</sup> be alwaies readie to saile to all such landes and portes as the foresaid *Peter Floris* and *Lucas Antheumes* shall direct yo<sup>u</sup> to saile vnto and there to remayne vntill the said principall Marchaunt<span class="sc">e</span> *Peter Floris* and *Lucas Antheumes* and Ro<span class="sc">b</span>t Browne shall haue finished there busines, And then from thence to saile to such other places as the said *Peter Floris* and *Lucas Antheumes* shall requier yo<sup>u</sup> And this shall be soe often by yo<sup>u</sup> pformed as they shall desire (for therein consisteth the welfare of the whole voyadge[)]. And noe man shall counsaile or resolue to retourne [p. 384] homewardes vntill such tyme as o<sup>r</sup> said principall m<sup>r</sup>chaunte shall haue fullie finisht there intended trade vpon forfecture of all their wages, and seveare ponishment for the same.

12 Item The łres from his Ma<sup>tie</sup>: w<sup>ch</sup> wee haue procured vnto the Kinges Princes and Potentates of the Indies,[^sec-08-fn-113] and haue made in the names of o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntes *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* and *Robert Browne* together w<sup>th</sup> *Thomas Essington Symon Euans*, & *Adam Denton* o<sup>r</sup> factors and deliu<sup>r</sup>ed vnto o<sup>r</sup> said principall Marchauntes shall be presented by them, in the presence of the rest of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors, [()or soe many of o<sup>r</sup> Englishe Marchante as shall be therevnto appointed) in the name of the kinges Ma<sup>tie</sup>: of England, and for the honor of the English Nation, by them to procure such freedome both of Customes and all other thinges as they shall finde to be proffitable for the Companie, and that the Companie may thereby be trewlie informed of whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> shall be done therein.

13 Item To the end all difficult matters may the better be passed over by good endeuors wee doe appointe a Counsell of eight psonns whereof Capteine *Anthonie Hippon* to be president (in matters of the shipp or for iustice []), and *Peter Floris Lucas Antheumes* and Robt Browne w<sup>th</sup> Thomas Essington *Symon Euans* and *Adam Denton* and George Chauncey being in all eight psonns, whereof one of them to recorde whatt matters shall passe, shall be a sufficient Counsell to determyn all Cryminall and Cyuell matters that shall come before them yett forasmuch as *Peter Floris* and Lucas Antheumes haue excused them selues that they are not acquainted w<sup>th</sup> the lawes and iustice of o<sup>r</sup> land therefore they shall be exempted and not required to come to the Counsell when any matter of Iustice is to be handled (for such matters shall be determyned by the rest of the Counsell) But yf yt be for any matters on land (or for any thinge w<sup>ch</sup> conserneth trade) then one of the principall Marchaunte shall be President either *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* or Robt Browne as they shall thinke fitt amongst themselues to determyne for that purpose, And the foresaid Counsell shall allowe of the said pson for president and shall hearken to his propoticõns, and take Counsaile, and resolue vpon the same as occasion shall be offerred.


<!-- page: 477 | folio: 385 -->
14 Item yf yt should happen that o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntę *Peter Floris*, *Lucas Antheumes* and Robt Browne, should not carrie them selues well in this voyadge, there faultes and misdoeinges shall be written vpp & deliu<sup>r</sup>ed over vnto the Company in England for to be censured by them, butt they shall not be displaced duringe the voyadge.

15\. Item the Captaine shall haue aspetiall care that noe man whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>, of whatt quallitie or Condic̃on soeuer he bee (his owne pson beinge alsoe included herein) shall vse any priuate or secreete trade, vpon peine and[^sec-08-fn-114] forfecture of all that shall be found by any man soe doinge, and beside shall endure arbitrary ponishment, And wee requier the principall Marchauntę to haue a spetiall care hereof on the land, and to preuent yt soe much as is possible, And the Captaine and other Marchauntę shall alsoe haue a vigelent Eye & good reguard on the principall Marchauntę to the end the Companie may be the better serued (whoe haue beene att such excessiue chardge) & reape the benefitt of the trade discou<sup>r</sup>ed by their expences.

16 Item fforasmuch as wee are c<sup>r</sup>teinelie enformed, that when twoe of o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchauntę *Peter Floris* & Lucas Antheumes shall come into the Indies they are like to be much hated by the *Dutchmen* there whoe will seeke to doe them wronge and all the villanie they may, therefore wee expreslie chardge yo<sup>u</sup> the Captaine (and all others that are in o<sup>r</sup> shipp and voyadge[]) to defend and preserue them from wronges w<sup>th</sup>all the power and strength yo<sup>u</sup> may against any that shall offer to doe them wronge or iniurie: Or shall goe aboute to hinder them in their busines, w<sup>ch</sup> might much indanger o<sup>r</sup> voyadge, The like Comandem<sup>t</sup> wee doe expreslie giue vnto all others that are in any of o<sup>r</sup> shipps & imployed in o<sup>r</sup> busines in any places whatsoeuer.

17\. Item for avoiedinge Confusion in the gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> of o<sup>r</sup> people, and for that nothinge is soe vncerteine as the state of mans life: Wee ordeine that yf God shall call yo<sup>u</sup> Captaine *Anthonie Hippon* duringe this voyadge, out of the world, (w<sup>ch</sup> God defend) then wee Comitt the gou<sup>r</sup>nment of o<sup>r</sup> shipp & Marriners therin to such as wee haue nominated in a writtinge subscribed by the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> & sealed w<sup>th</sup> the seale of the Company putt vp [p. 386] into a Boxe N<sup>o</sup>: 1 sealed w<sup>th</sup> hard waxe & deliu<sup>r</sup>ed to Captaine Anthonie Hippon to be kept close and not opened, soe longe as the said Captaine Anthony Hippon shall lyue Butt yf yt shall please god to take him out of this world that shall succeede Captaine Anthonie Hippon then wee ordeyne that o<sup>r</sup> Master and Marriners in o<sup>r</sup> said shipp shall submitt them selues to the gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup> and Comand of such pson or psons as wee haue nomynated therevnto in a writeinge sealed vp in a Boxe N<sup>o</sup>: 2 & remayneinge in the Custodie of the said Captaine Anthonie Hippon & those that shall succeede him. Prouided alwayes that noe pson whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> w<sup>ch</sup> shall succeede in the aforesaid place of gou<sup>r</sup>nm<sup>t</sup>, shall demand, be allowed, or expect the wages of his predecessor, butt shall content himselfe w<sup>th</sup> his first wages promised him by the Companie. Or referr himselfe to be Considered of accordinge to his deserte (att his retourne) by the Gou<sup>r</sup>no<sup>r</sup> and Comittees of the Companie for the tyme beinge.

18 Item If yt should happen (as God forbid) that o<sup>r</sup> shipp should haue waunte of men or other necessarie meanes (w<sup>ch</sup> such longe voyadges are subiect vnto) Then we will that yo<sup>u</sup> desire to be releeued by any shipp yo<sup>u</sup> shall meete w<sup>ch</sup> is appteineinge vnto vs, [()or any other Englishe shipp whatsoeu<sup>r</sup>) And wee doe hereby straightlie chardge all Generalls Captaines Masters or any other Officers (in any of the shippes whatsoeu<sup>r</sup> appteineinge to the Company of Marchaunt*e* of London tradeinge to the East Indies[)] whome yo<sup>u</sup> shall chaunce to meete in any such yo<sup>r</sup> distresse thatt they supplie ayde and releyue yo<sup>u</sup> w<sup>th</sup> such men or any other necessaries w<sup>ch</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> shall haue neede of, and they may conuenientlie spare yo<sup>u</sup> w<sup>th</sup>out endaungeringe them selues and their shipps. And that yo<sup>u</sup> pforme like good office to any of our shipps that yo<sup>u</sup> shall meete duringe the said voyadge whome yo<sup>u</sup> shall finde distressed.

19 Item Whereas we haue sent alonge w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> one chest of money conteyneinge fower thowsand Ryalls of 8. w<sup>ch</sup> wee intend for a stocke to be lefte at *Bantam* against the tyme that yt shall please God to send o<sup>r</sup> shippinge thether Wee doe therefore ordeine that o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchaunt*e Peter Floris* Lucas *Antheumes* and Robt Browne shall leaue one or twoe of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors att *Bantam* [()whome they by their experience shall finde most [p. 387] fitt to vndertake the same seruice) together w<sup>th</sup> the said Cheste of money intended for the foresaid stocke (or the valewe thereof) as alsoe halfe of the proceede w<sup>ch</sup> shall be raysed by the ymploym<sup>t</sup> thereof in their said voyadge thither, where o<sup>r</sup> said ffactors shall remaine, and make ymploym<sup>t</sup> of the said stocke and proceede thereof in such Comodities as by your discretion shall be thought most necessarie to be transported w<sup>th</sup> our shipping for o<sup>r</sup> best aduantage to such places as shall be found conuenient, And the other halfe of the gaine to be for the accompt of the *Globe*.

20\. Item yf yo<sup>u</sup> shall finde in yo<sup>r</sup> trauaile, or can conuenientlie come by any faire birdes or beastes, or any other thinge fitt for vs to present to his Ma<sup>tie</sup>, or any of the noble Lorde that are o<sup>r</sup> hono<sup>ble</sup> freinde, Wee pray and requier yo<sup>u</sup> to be carefull to prouide, & send the same w<sup>th</sup> espetiall chardge to some carefull man or men that retourne, to see them carefullie kept and deliu<sup>r</sup>ed to vs. And w<sup>th</sup>all yf you shall knowe any of the Marriners or others to haue any such w<sup>ch</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> cannot ꝑcure from them for reason then that yo<sup>u</sup> send vs notice thereof, to the end we may take order theirein accordinglie.

And soe haueing remembred what wee thinke needfull for yo<sup>r</sup> direcčon in this voyadge, and relyinge vpon yo<sup>r</sup> dilligence and care in pursuing o<sup>r</sup> busines to o<sup>r</sup> most aduantage Wee comitt yo<sup>u</sup> to the ptecčon of the Almightie God, whome wee beseech to blesse yo<sup>r</sup> endevo<sup>rs</sup> and graunte yo<sup>u</sup> a safe passadge and safe retourne to all o<sup>r</sup> comfortes.

Item Whereas wee haue giuen direcčons that one or twoe of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors should be lefte at Bantam, whome o<sup>r</sup> principall Marchaunte *Peter Floris* Lucas Antheumes and Robt Browne by their experience shall finde most fitt for o<sup>r</sup> seruice there, vpon further aduise and Consideračon Wee doe now ordeyne that Thomas *Essington* shall passe from porte to porte w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> dureing the said voyadge, and retourne backe againe w<sup>th</sup> yo<sup>u</sup> in the same shipp into England: And that yo<sup>u</sup> take the oportunitie (from the most conuenient place yo<sup>u</sup> shall arriue att) to send one or twoe of o<sup>r</sup> ffactors in such conuenient shippinge as [yo<sup>u</sup>] may procure) to carrie his Ma<sup>te</sup> łres vnto the kinge of Iapan, together w<sup>th</sup> such stocke of Marchandize & Comodities as wee haue appointed o<sup>r</sup> said principall Marchaunte to prouide for that purpose And yf [p. 388] you should be driuē to any want of ffactors during this o<sup>r</sup> said voyadge then yo<sup>u</sup> may ymploye the purser or his mate, or both yf occasion require, soe that yo<sup>u</sup> be espetiallie carefull to supply the place of the purser w<sup>th</sup> some sufficient pson to vndertake that voyadge.

Memorandū It is ordeyned by vs that yf God should take out of this world o<sup>r</sup> loueinge freind Robt Browne, Then wee doe referr y<sup>u</sup> vnto a Boxe N<sup>o</sup>. 3. to vnderstand o<sup>r</sup> will and pleasure, Whome wee haue appointed to succeede him in place, of o<sup>r</sup> principall ffactor, to be ioyned w<sup>th</sup> Peter ffloris and Lucas Antheumes, o<sup>r</sup> other principall ffactors.

Anthonie Hippon Peter ffloris. Lucas Antheumes Robt Browne Thomas Essington


##### Most highe and mightie kinge:[^sec-08-fn-115]

> _[Margin: Twoe of this draught are to be written wth Blanckes and ingrossed]_

AS there is nothinge w<sup>ch</sup> encreaseth more the glory & dignitie of Sou<sup>r</sup>eigne Princes vpon earth then to extend their renowne vnto farr discident Nations, Soe haueing vnderstoode of late yeares from some of o<sup>r</sup> loueinge Subiectę, that haue traded into diu<sup>r</sup>s Countries neere adioyneinge vnto yo<sup>rs</sup>, of the reputation and greatnes of yo<sup>r</sup> power and dominion.
